findings.statement: BatteryConfig holds two facts (charge and discharge efficiency) in three fields: efficiency, charge_efficiency and discharge_efficiency. When efficiency is set, __post_init__ overwrites both per-direction fields with sqrt(efficiency). It does not refuse a contradicting explicit value. Probed at the pin: BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=5, efficiency=0.81, charge_efficiency=0.99, discharge_efficiency=0.7) constructs with 0.9/0.9 and no error. dataclasses.replace(that, charge_efficiency=0.99) still yields 0.9. The scenario parser admits all three keys in one battery block (config.py _BATTERY_BLOCK_KEYS, lines 753-754) and _parse_battery_config splats the block straight into BatteryConfig. So a YAML block giving both forms parses silently, in a parser whose stated policy is to refuse unrecognised keys. The inverse writer has to branch: scenario_writer._battery_block writes either efficiency or the pair. The class docstring spends 12 lines (battery.py:135-146) on the override and a 'Caveat' that replace() does not take effect. optimize.py:853 already varies batteries with dataclasses.replace(home.battery_config, capacity_kwh=...), the mechanism that silently no-ops here.
findings.proposal: Give each efficiency fact one representation. Either refuse in __post_init__, with a message naming both values, when efficiency is set together with per-direction values other than its square root, or keep round-trip as a classmethod constructor rather than a retained field. Until then, have _parse_battery_config refuse a block that sets both forms. The field is in the frozen surface, so this needs the briefing's version-bump route.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a charge-efficiency or round-trip axis to an optimize sweep, a fleet distribution or a web form. It copies optimize.py's dataclasses.replace(battery_config, ...) pattern, or lets a user's YAML set both keys. To get it right the agent must know that a retained efficiency silently wins, which only the class docstring says. Nothing catches the wrong version: no error is raised, and every sweep point simulates the same efficiency, so the results look plausible and flat.

findings.statement: The 'off_peak' and 'solar' smart-charging modes schedule against windows written as literals inside the function, not against the home's tariff or PV. Off-peak is 00:30-07:30, written out twice for the same-day and overnight branches (ev.py:245-246 and 251-252). Solar is 10:00-16:00 (ev.py:218-219). generate_ev_charging_profile takes no tariff, and neither does load.generate_load_profile, its only src caller. home.simulate_home holds config.tariff_config but has no way to hand it to the EV. The tariff layer, meanwhile, makes these windows configuration: TariffConfig.economy_7 takes off_peak_start/off_peak_end (tariff.py:206-211), economy_10 has three windows (00:00-05:00, 13:00-16:00, 20:00-22:00), and flow._is_cheap_period is the project's one cheap-period classifier. Probed at the pin: a 7 kW, 35 kWh, arrive-18:00, depart-07:00 off_peak EV over 2024-01-10..12 charges 00:30-05:29 on 11 Jan (300 minutes). Against TariffConfig.economy_10(), 30 of those minutes are billed at the peak rate. Under an Economy 7 configured 23:00-06:00, the EV ignores the 23:00-00:30 cheap window. 'solar' mode charges 10:00-16:00 whatever the PV produces.
findings.proposal: Give EV scheduling the same cheap-period input the battery path uses: a TariffConfig, or a public cheap-period predicate moved out of flow's private namespace. Derive the off-peak window from it instead of from literals, and let solar mode read the generation series simulate_home already has.
findings.next_change: An agent is asked to make off-peak EV charging follow the home's tariff (Economy 10, Octopus Go, a custom period list), or to make solar mode follow generation. It has to thread the tariff from HomeConfig through simulate_home and generate_load_profile (where the EV is reached by a function-local import) into ev.py, and replace both copies of the window block. It also has to know that flow._is_cheap_period, a private name in another module, is the cheap-period authority. Nothing catches a schedule that disagrees with the tariff: no test prices an EV schedule against a TariffConfig.

findings.statement: Every default PV simulation uses one CEC module, and nothing names it. It is found by substring search over pvlib's CECMod library for columns containing both 'Canadian_Solar' and '400', taking the first match in catalogue column order. Two looser fallbacks follow: any 380-420 W STC row, then column 0. With the locked pvlib 0.15.1 the library has 21,535 columns, two of which match: Canadian_Solar_Inc__CS1U_400MS (STC 400.428 W) and Canadian_Solar_Inc__CS3W_400P (400.158 W). The first is used. The function's comments say it uses 'Canadian Solar CS6K-400MS' (pv.py:157, 162), a row the catalogue does not hold. The picked row's numbers are restated as facts elsewhere: wired_dc_capacity_kw's doctest (400.428 W), docs/pv-inverter-string-matching.md:66 (400.428 W, V_mp_ref 44.1 V), docs/pv-annual-yield-benchmark.md:12, and tests/unit/test_validation.py:132, 303-305 and 380. Inverters get a guard, _require_cec_library_row, that refuses an unknown name; the module has no equivalent.
findings.proposal: Name the module row as a constant and require it the way _require_cec_library_row requires inverter rows, failing with a message naming the row. Delete the substring search and both fallbacks. Correct the comment to the row actually used.
findings.next_change: The newest-releases lane upgrades pvlib, and its CEC table adds, drops or reorders a Canadian Solar 400 W row. Or an agent 'fixes' the comment by trying to select CS6K-400MS. Either way the default module changes for every home without a word, along with its STC rating, V_mp_ref, string wiring and yield. What catches it is downstream numeric tests in test_validation and test_pv failing with module-count or yield messages that never name the module.

findings.statement: The simulation's cadence is one axis handled three ways. (1) timebase.HOURS_PER_MINUTE is documented both as a unit conversion and as the assumption that 'each row of a simulated series is one minute'. (2) step_hours derives the cadence from an index. (3) The battery, dispatch and flow layers take an explicit parameter: 10 timestep_minutes/duration_minutes parameters across Battery.charge/discharge, the four dispatch decision functions and both flow.simulate_timestep variants. The parameter does not reach the top. home.simulate_home passes the literal timestep_minutes=1.0 twice (home.py:404, 411) and converts back with 1/HOURS_PER_MINUTE (home.py:422). SimulationResults' _power metadata multiplies by HOURS_PER_MINUTE (home.py:82). 13 code sites integrate with series.sum() * HOURS_PER_MINUTE (output.py 10, validation.py 2, load.py 1). community.py instead derives the cadence with step_hours, and output.py uses both forms. The generators hard-code minute indices: freq='1min' in pv.py (1), load.py (2) and ev.py (1); 1440 in ev.py (5) and on 3 code lines of load.py.
findings.proposal: Make the cadence one value owned by the run: the result's index, or a field on SimulationResults. Give the codebase one kW-to-kWh integration helper that reads it, used in place of the 13 inline sites. Alternatively, state the one-minute cadence as an invariant and drop the timestep parameters that only pretend to vary it.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a measured half-hourly smart-meter load input, or runs sweeps at a coarser cadence for speed. The explicit timestep parameters in flow, dispatch and battery suggest the engine already supports any cadence, but home.py, SimulationResults, validation, output and the generators each assume one minute. The per-step energy balance is scale-free and still passes, so what catches a missed site is only totals off by the cadence ratio in tests pinned at one minute.

findings.statement: calculate_annual_consumption does not compute an annual figure. Its docstring opens 'Despite the name (kept for backward compatibility), this function simply integrates whatever Series is passed — it is NOT limited to full-year profiles.' Its in-module caller in _try_richardsonpy_profile needs a 3-line comment (load.py:378-380) to say it measures the window's energy. Its sibling scale_profile_to_annual(target_annual_kwh) has the same mismatch: it scales to any total. Neither name is in solar_challenge.__all__, so the backward compatibility protects only load.py and tests/unit/test_load.py (9 references). The prose came from commit dbc1758, 'amend: log fallback warning; clarify calculate_annual_consumption naming', which clarified the name in prose rather than renaming.
findings.proposal: Rename both to say what they do, e.g. energy_kwh(profile) and scale_profile_to_energy(profile, target_kwh). Update test_load.py and delete the disclaimer and the explanatory comment.
findings.next_change: An agent fixing the prior seasonal-normalisation defect at load._get_daily_profile_kwh, or scaling a partial-year window, reads calculate_annual_consumption/scale_profile_to_annual as annualising and adds or removes a 365/days factor. Only the docstring disclaimer warns against that, and only test_load would catch it.

findings.statement: The heat-pump type vocabulary is written out in five places and the per-type COP curve in a sixth: (1) the HeatPumpType Literal (heat_pump.py:13); (2) the valid_types tuple in HeatPumpConfig.__post_init__ (heat_pump.py:131); (3) calculate_cop's if/elif chain and its error-message list (heat_pump.py:94-109); (4) config.py:1779 `if heat_pump_type not in ('ASHP', 'GSHP')` with its message; (5) the cast to Literal['ASHP', 'GSHP'] at config.py:1786. Each type's COP curve is four loose module constants (8 in all, heat_pump.py:35-46), chosen by that if/elif, not one record per type.
findings.proposal: Use one per-type record (type to COP intercept, slope, min, max). Derive the Literal check and the parser's accepted values from its keys, and make calculate_cop a lookup.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a heat-pump type, e.g. water-source or hybrid. It must edit the Literal, the config tuple, calculate_cop's branch and message, config.py's tuple and its cast, and add four constants. mypy flags only some of the misses. A missed tuple shows up as a ValueError at construction or parse time, and nothing ties the vocabulary to the curves.

findings.statement: The project's policy for running a pvlib chain lives only inside simulate_pv_output: it suppresses scipy._chandrupatla's 'invalid value encountered' RuntimeWarning around run_model. Any caller that needs more than aged AC output (in-plane irradiance, v_mp, cell temperature) must take the raw ModelChain from create_model_chain or create_model_chain_picking_from and call run_model itself, and each such caller re-copies the filter. scripts/measure_pv_performance_ratio.py::in_plane_irradiation copies the 5-line filter verbatim. scripts/measure_mppt_window.py::main installs it process-wide, so its measure_year and operating_voltage run_model calls depend on main having run first. tests/unit/test_measurement_scripts.py carries a fourth, broader copy as a pytest mark. This adds evidence to the prior that pv.py's two entry points disagree about what 'the PV model' is.
findings.proposal: Have pv.py expose one public 'run the chain over weather' function that applies the run policy and returns the run chain. simulate_pv_output and the scripts would both call it; this fits the prior's proposal to give the PV model one home.
findings.next_change: An agent adds another consumer of chain internals (a POA-based check in validation, or a new measurement script) and calls create_model_chain(...).run_model(weather). Unless it finds and copies one of the filters it emits RuntimeWarnings, and nothing tells it the policy exists. If pv.py's policy changes, for example a pvlib upgrade moves the warning to another module, the copies drift.

findings.statement:
The choice of battery dispatch strategy is carried as plain strings in two vocabularies under one YAML key name. The home-level key accepts any value with no check.

- **Home and fleet level:** `dispatch_strategy` is a str on HomeConfig (default 'greedy'). Only fleet_distribution's copy of the key is checked, against config._VALID_DISPATCH_STRATEGIES = {'greedy', 'tou_optimized'}.
- **Battery block:** `battery.dispatch_strategy` is a DispatchStrategyConfig. Its own tuple, ('self_consumption', 'tou_optimized', 'peak_shaving'), is checked in __post_init__.
- 'greedy' and 'self_consumption' name the same behaviour.
- **Precedence:** which of the two wins is decided inline in home.simulate_home.
- **Home key unchecked:** parse_home_block copies the home key into HomeConfig unchanged (`**{key: home[key] for key in _HOME_SCALAR_KEYS}`), and HomeConfig does not validate it.
- **Explanatory docstrings:** BatteryDistributionConfig and FleetDistributionConfig each carry a paragraph explaining the two meanings of dispatch_strategy. That prose is there to make up for the unclear naming.

Probed at 7dfea36:
- parse_home_block accepts a home-level dispatch_strategy of 'tou_optimised', 'peak_shaving', 'self_consumption' or 42, and each such home is then simulated with self-consumption.
- parse_fleet_config refuses fleet_distribution.dispatch_strategy 'self_consumption' ("valid values: ['greedy', 'tou_optimized']").
findings.proposal:
Make the strategy a closed type and parse it at the boundary:
- A StrEnum, or a frozen tagged union of the strategy configs, with one validator.
- parse_home_block refuses an unknown value, naming its block path.
- Retire the 'greedy' alias or map it there.
- simulate_home reads one resolved strategy rather than reconciling two fields.
findings.next_change:
Plausible next change: add a new dispatch strategy (e.g. an arbitrage or export-limited mode), or let a homes: file choose tariff-driven TOU.

What the agent must find and change in step:
- DispatchStrategyConfig's valid_strategies tuple.
- _VALID_DISPATCH_STRATEGIES.
- The if/elif in home._create_dispatch_strategy.
- The precedence in simulate_home.
- The 'greedy' defaults in HomeConfig and generate_homes_from_distribution.
- scenario_writer, which writes the home-level string back unchecked.

Nothing ties these together. A misspelt or wrong-level value is accepted and simulated as self-consumption, so the change only gets caught if a test asserts the strategy_name of a simulated result.

findings.statement:
create_summary_table takes `summary: Any` and picks its rows by testing for attribute names (hasattr and getattr). The SummaryStatistics names it probes are not the names FleetSummary uses: fleet_self_consumption_ratio, fleet_grid_dependency_ratio, total_net_cost_gbp and total_seg_revenue_gbp. So `fleet run` silently drops the fleet's self-consumption ratio, grid dependency, net cost and SEG revenue rows. mypy cannot see the gap because the parameter is Any.

The Any-typed duck-typed parameter makes the fleet-vs-home variation a series of inline flag checks (heuristic 3), and the hasattr tests route on attribute names as strings (heuristic 12). The comment above the financial rows claims they are guarded 'so FleetSummary is unaffected', but FleetSummary does carry total_import_cost_gbp and total_export_revenue_gbp, so those two rows do print for fleets while their siblings are dropped.

Probed at 7dfea36 with a fully populated FleetSummary, the table had 9 rows: Total Generation, Total Demand, Self-Consumption, Grid Import, Grid Export, Number of Homes, Simulation Days, Grid Import Cost, Grid Export Revenue.
findings.proposal: Replace the duck-typed function with one table builder per summary type, each typed (SummaryStatistics, FleetSummary), sharing a small typed row helper for the five energy totals. Alternatively, have each summary expose a typed tuple of (label, value) rows. Then a renamed field fails mypy.

findings.statement:
Where a YAML-defined sweep may sit is decided in one hard-coded place, while the grammar accepts it in 19.

- **Parsing:** _parse_distribution_spec accepts a proportional_to spec with a `multiplier: {type: sweep, ...}` for any of the 19 distribution fields.
- **Detection:** detect_sweep_spec, _replace_sweep_with_value and expand_sweep_configs look only at battery.capacity_kwh.
- **Sampling:** _DistributionSampler.sample_with_context refuses an unexpanded SweepSpec only when generation reaches it.

Results for a sweep multiplier on battery.max_charge_kw or heat_pump.thermal_capacity_kw (probed at 7dfea36):
- `fleet sweep` (parse_sweep_fleet_configs) says 'No sweep specification found in config. Use proportional_to with type: sweep in multiplier.', which is what the file already does.
- `fleet run` and `validate config` (parse_fleet_config) say 'Cannot sample ProportionalDistribution with SweepSpec multiplier directly. Use expand_sweep_configs() to expand sweep values first.' That names an internal function and neither the field nor its path.
- The same internal-function message is what `fleet run` prints for a valid battery.capacity_kwh sweep file.
findings.proposal:
Make the placement one fact:
- Either refuse a sweep multiplier at parse time everywhere except the fields the expander supports, naming the field path.
- Or have detect_sweep_spec and _replace_sweep_with_value walk all distribution fields, so the sweep's location is data, not code.
Either way, the sampler's late refusal becomes an assertion rather than a user-facing message.
findings.next_change:
Plausible next change: support sweeping a second parameter (e.g. PV capacity, or battery power proportional to capacity), as the 'Parameter sweeps' architecture line suggests.

What the agent must change:
- detect_sweep_spec, _replace_sweep_with_value and parse_sweep_fleet_configs' FleetConfig naming ('multiplier=...').
- cli/fleet.py::sweep's 'YAML sweep: multiplier' labels and its multiplier_*.csv filenames.
- The validate path.
The agent must also notice that the parser already accepts the new placement, so the old silent-misdetection behaviour is the baseline.

What catches a wrong version: only an end-to-end CLI sweep test for that placement. No check at construction relates where a SweepSpec sits to where it is detected.

findings.statement:
The documented fleet-simulation seam is bypassed by the two commands named after fleets.

The cli/utils module docstring says 'A command that simulates a fleet reads its simulator from Click's context object, ctx.ensure_object(CliFleetSimulator).simulate'. tests/_cli_fleet_simulator.py says its invoke_cli runs 'with *simulate* running every fleet simulation' 'so its simulating commands never reach PVGIS'.

Only `finance run` and `optimize configs` read CliFleetSimulator.
- `fleet run` calls fleet.simulate_fleet_iter directly. It then restates fleet.simulate_fleet's assembly: a [None]*n slot list, an assert-not-None loop, and FleetResults(per_home_results, home_configs). It does this only to advance a progress bar.
- `fleet sweep` calls simulate_multi_sweep_iter directly.

As a result, invoke_cli(['fleet', 'run', ...], fake) silently ignores the fake. Fleet-run tests must seed a real weather cache and simulate real homes. Any change to how simulate_fleet builds FleetResults must be repeated in cli/fleet.py.

This is also the CLI path where the SEG (prior parse_fleet_config finding) and summary-row (finding 2) divergences sit.
findings.proposal: Give simulate_fleet (or CliFleetSimulator.simulate) an optional per-home progress callback. Then `fleet run` reads ctx.ensure_object(CliFleetSimulator).simulate like its siblings, and the hand-rolled assembly goes. Give `fleet sweep` the same seam, or narrow the module docstring and the test-helper docstring to the commands that honour it.
findings.next_change:
Plausible next change: make `fleet run` apply the file's seg: block (pending task 185), or add a field to FleetResults (e.g. the weather or timebase used).

What the agent must know:
- The CLI's fleet run does not go through simulate_fleet, so the FleetResults change must be made twice.
- A test written with tests/_cli_fleet_simulator.invoke_cli will not exercise the fake simulator for this command, despite both docstrings.

What catches a wrong version: only a fleet run test that runs a real simulation.

findings.statement: `finance run` has three independent axes: --assumptions (physics/spreadsheet/both), --flex-band, and FinanceConfig.grid_services_model. Each one reaches a different subset of the computations rendered into one board report. --assumptions is applied only to the two bill_distribution calls. project_multi_year, solve_cost_recovery_rate and compute_grid_services_at_events all read the unmodified scenario `finance`. Two consequences follow. With `--assumptions spreadsheet`, the bill section uses the 0.70 override while the economics and cost-recovery blocks use physics. With `--assumptions physics` and an override set in the YAML, the reverse holds. The spreadsheet-only mode then passes dist_spreadsheet into generate_finance_report's first parameter, which is named `bill_physics`, so the report heads the override's figures '## Householder Bill (Physics Assumptions)' (heuristic 1: a label that lies on a board-facing artifact). The capacity-at-events income that project_multi_year books into fleet revenue is rendered only inside output.py's `if flex_band is not None:` block. Without --flex-band it does not appear, although it moves the economics shown. The mode is expressed as three near-identical generate_finance_report call branches.
findings.proposal: Resolve each mode to its own FinanceConfig once at the top of run. Drive every computation (bill, projection, solve, events) per mode from that value. Have generate_finance_report take labelled sections keyed by mode instead of a positional bill_physics. Render the grid-services events income with the economics it changes, not under the flex block.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: report the cost-recovery solve or the economics under both assumption sets, or add a fourth mode such as a calibrated override. The agent must know four things beyond this file. generate_finance_report's first positional is named bill_physics and fixes the heading. The projection and solve read FinanceConfig.self_consumption_override directly. The events income is nested under the flex block in output.py. The spreadsheet default comes from finance.DEFAULT_SPREADSHEET_SELF_CONSUMPTION. Nothing catches a wrong version: no test drives spreadsheet mode through the CLI, and the mislabel already ships.

findings.statement: A fleet file (the parse_fleet_config document) has no parser for its scenario-level blocks, so cli/optimize.py::configs and cli/finance.py::run each build a ScenarioConfig by hand from the raw YAML dict, and they disagree. Period: configs reads `raw.get('period', {})` with dict `.get('start_date', '2024-01-01')`, so a CLI flag beats the file, which beats 2024. run never reads raw['period'] and simulates --start/--end, which default to 2024-01-01..2024-12-31. The same fleet file with a June-August period block is therefore simulated for 92 days by `optimize configs` and for 366 days by `finance run`. configs' raw-dict read also bypasses config._parse_period's _refuse_unrecognised_keys({'start_date','end_date'}). A misspelt `period: {start: ...}` silently falls back to the full year, where the scenario parser would raise ConfigurationError (heuristic 12: an ad-hoc parse of a structured block). run likewise reads `raw.get('flex_band')` and lower-cases it in the CLI. Both commands load the YAML twice: load_config, then load_fleet_config, which calls load_config again. The SEG threading copy is covered by the prior _reconcile_seg_homes finding. The period and key-validation divergence is not.
findings.proposal: Add one config.py function that parses a fleet document's scenario-level blocks (period, seg, finance, flex_band, tariff) into a typed scenario, with the same key refusal as _parse_scenario. Make both CLIs call it, so period and SEG policy each have one home.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: honour another scenario-level block for fleet files, for example a top-level tariff (the live 185/296 family) or a period in `finance run`. The agent must edit both CLIs, plus cli/home for SEG, and know that they already resolve period differently and that config._parse_scenario cannot parse a fleet_distribution document. No test runs the two commands on the same file and compares their ScenarioConfig, so a third divergence lands silently.

findings.statement: householder_bill's public parameter `annual_self_consumption_kwh` is not annual. The function multiplies it by the annualisation scale (`sc_kwh_physics = annual_self_consumption_kwh * phys.scale`), so it must be the simulated window's figure. The only src caller, bill_distribution, passes the window's basis-C own-use. A caller that believes the name and passes a true annual figure for a short window is double-scaled. Nothing downstream refuses the result: neither _billed_energy nor BillBreakdown checks own-use against demand or generation. BillBreakdown's only construction check is the CBS-slice identity, so a self_consumption_fraction above 1 constructs. The signature is frozen in tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py FROZEN_SURFACE, and the package exports householder_bill as a platform-facing name.
findings.proposal: Rename the parameter to the window quantity it is, or drop it: every src caller derives it from `summary` via _cbs_own_use_kwh. Enforce own-use <= demand where billed energy is resolved, naming the offending values.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: a platform or new CLI consumer bills from an annual own-use figure (for example the spreadsheet assumption, or a measured annual meter read) through householder_bill. To get it right the agent must read the body and see that the 'annual' input is re-annualised. Nothing catches a wrong version: the bill constructs with a self-consumption fraction above 1, and the public-surface test pins the misleading name.

findings.statement: TariffConfig's defining invariant, that its periods tile the 24-hour day exactly once, is not checked at construction. Its __post_init__ only re-parses each period's times, which TariffPeriod.__post_init__ has already done. A gap is found only at use: get_rate raises 'No tariff period matches timestamp' at the first uncovered minute, which flow.py and home.py::simulate_home reach per timestep inside the fleet simulation. An overlap is never found, because get_rate returns the first matching period. config._build_custom_tariff builds YAML tariffs through this constructor with no coverage check, so a mistyped custom tariff is accepted at parse time. TariffPeriod.rate_per_kwh uses `< 0`, which admits NaN. TariffPeriod's docstring says start_time/end_time accept 'HH:MM format or time object', but both fields are `str`, and _parse_time on a datetime.time raises.
findings.proposal: Check in TariffConfig.__post_init__ that the sorted periods are contiguous and cover 24 hours exactly once, raising with the gap or overlap times named. Add a finite-rate check to TariffPeriod.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: add a multi-period preset (an Agile-like or Go-like tariff) or a web custom-tariff editor. The agent must know that get_rate is first-match and that nothing validates coverage before simulation. A wrong version (a gap) is caught only when a simulation reaches the uncovered minute, inside a worker after weather and PV work. An overlap is never caught and silently bills the earlier period's rate.

The overlap tariff constructs and get_rate(08:00) returns 0.10, the first match. NaN is accepted because `< 0` is False for NaN. findings.statement: sensitivity_panel cannot accept a baseline sweep that has already been computed, so cli/optimize.py::configs evaluates the whole baseline grid twice: run_sweep in configs, then the identical run_sweep(base_configs, retained_cash_floor_gbp=retained_floor, simulate=simulate) inside the panel. The panel's floor-axis short-circuit compares the swept value with the override argument (`v == retained_cash_floor_gbp`). It does not compare with the effective floor that RankedSweep.retained_cash_floor_gbp already echoes. On the CLI default path the override is None, so the short-circuit never fires, and the 27.0 floor value re-runs a sweep identical to the baseline. cli/optimize's cost comment is also stale: it describes 'a full-year default run of 72 configs'. The default --pv/--battery/--inverter lists give 4 x 3 x 3 = 36.
findings.proposal: Let sensitivity_panel take the baseline RankedSweep, and compare floor values against its retained_cash_floor_gbp.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: add a sensitivity axis or make the CLI pass the scenario floor explicitly. The agent must know that the panel recomputes its own baseline and that the floor short-circuit keys on the override argument, not the effective floor. A wrong version only costs runtime (each redundant sweep is 36 configs x 8-26 fleet simulations), and no test counts sweeps.

findings.verdict_notes: Read cli/optimize.py::configs in full, optimize.py sensitivity_panel and run_sweep, and the FinanceConfig defaults (finance.py:112-113). Read bristol-phase1.yaml's finance block at 7dfea36. — The panel calls run_sweep for the baseline itself, with no parameter to accept a precomputed sweep, so configs issues the same sweep twice. The floor short-circuit tests `v == retained_cash_floor_gbp`, the override, which is None on the default path, so it never fires. With defaults the run_sweep calls are 1 (configs) + 1 (panel baseline) + 3 floor values + 3 grid-services values = 8. The scenario floor is 27.0, so the floor-27 call duplicates the baseline. The default grid_services value is 0.0, which differs from every swept value, so there are no further duplicates: 8 issued, 6 distinct. The defaults 4x3x3 give 36 configs, and the comment 'full-year default run of 72 configs' is stale. Real cost, 2 of 8 sweeps redundant, but runtime only.

findings.statement: GridServicesAtEvents' docstring declares `sum(per_window_income_gbp) == annual_income_gbp` a 'design invariant', and it requires per_window_avail_kw and per_window_income_gbp to align with the config's windows. The frozen dataclass has no __post_init__, so neither is enforced. In the same area, BillBreakdown enforces its identity at construction. The only producer, compute_grid_services_at_events, also pairs windows with capacities through a non-strict `zip(cfg.event_windows, avails)`, while compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw uses strict=True.
findings.proposal: Give GridServicesAtEvents a __post_init__ that checks the sum identity (to float tolerance) and equal tuple lengths, and make the producer's zip strict.
findings.next_change: Plausible next change: the known age-0 memo gap is fixed by making event income vary with battery SOH per window, or by adding a per-window derate. An agent editing compute_grid_services_at_events can let annual_income_gbp and the per-window tuple disagree, or drop a window. output.py renders annual_income_gbp, while consumers are told not to re-derive it. Nothing catches the mismatch.

The frozen dataclass has no __post_init__, the docstring declares the sum identity a design invariant, and the zips are 1 non-strict of 2. The claimed cost is thin. The only producer builds annual_income_gbp as float(sum(per_window_net)) from the same list as per_window_income_gbp, so the identity holds by construction. compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw returns exactly one entry per window, so the non-strict zip cannot misalign today. The 'drop a window' scenario is hypothetical. The age-0 memo gap is another invented trigger. The unenforced documented invariant is a genuine but low-weight heuristic-10 gap. The comparison with BillBreakdown holds, but a 3-field result type with one producer carries little next-change risk.

findings.statement:
A stored run's config.json and summary.json are rebuilt into the current HomeConfig, SummaryStatistics and FleetSummary by field name, and nothing marks which version of those dataclasses wrote them.

_deserialize_dataclass skips a key the class no longer has (storage.py:98-100) and builds the class with whatever keys remain:
- A field added later with a default is silently filled in. Probe: a summary dict without total_grid_charge_kwh, the field task 469 added on SummaryStatistics, loads with total_grid_charge_kwh=0.0. Every run saved before 469 therefore reports no grid charging.
- A renamed or new required field raises TypeError. Probe: SummaryStatistics.__init__() missing 'total_generation_kwh'. Reading a fleet run's config as a home config also raises TypeError (missing 'pv_config' and 'load_config').

load_home_run's and load_fleet_run's Raises sections name only FileNotFoundError and ValueError. Their four callers handle two different exception sets:
- routes.home_results, routes.fleet_results and api.history_export_csv catch only FileNotFoundError, so drift is a 500.
- api.history_export_yaml catches TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError and ConfigurationError, and answers 500 JSON.

So the requirement that every future field of three core dataclasses must keep a default, or every stored run stops loading, is stated nowhere. A rename silently drops the old value.
findings.proposal: Have save_home_run and save_fleet_run write a format version beside the JSON. Have the loaders compare it and raise one named StoredRunUnreadable that carries the run id and the offending field. Make _deserialize_dataclass refuse unknown keys and missing required keys through that error rather than skipping or raising TypeError. Have the four callers handle that one exception uniformly. Pin the old-format behaviour with a frozen fixture run under tests/.
findings.next_change: A simulation-core agent adds or renames a field on SummaryStatistics, HomeConfig or FleetSummary, as task 469 did. To get it right, the agent must know that web/storage.py persists these by field name in every run under ~/.solar-challenge/runs, and that loading picks up a missing field's default silently. It must therefore give the field a default and accept that old runs report that default as fact. A rename silently loses data. Nothing catches a wrong version: core tests never load stored web runs, the web round-trip tests save and load under the same schema, and the first signal is a 500 on a results page or export for a run saved before the change.

Read web/storage.py _deserialize_dataclass, load_home_run and load_fleet_run, routes.py and api.py call sites, and tests/unit/test_web_storage_roundtrip.py. Ran a probe with the repo .venv. — The silent default, the TypeError on a missing required field, and the 2 exception sets across 4 callers all reproduce. The test measurement is wrong. test_web_storage_roundtrip.py already writes older-shape stored files: TestGridChargeKwhRoundtrip.test_summary_saved_without_total_grid_charge_kwh_loads_zero deletes the key from summary.json, and the module docstring lists a run saved without grid_charge_cost reloading as None and a stored config holding a retired field's key set to null still loading. findings.statement:
RunType ('home', 'fleet', 'sweep') selects a run's loader, results page, CSV export and YAML export. No single mechanism maps a type to those behaviours: each site compares the type string inline, and the sites disagree on what any other value means.

- api.history_export_csv: `run.type == "home"`, otherwise it loads a fleet.
- api.history_export_yaml: `run.type == "fleet"`, otherwise it reads a home.
- templates/dashboard.html:78: 'home' links to home_results, anything else to fleet_results.
- templates/history/runs.html:174 and :273: build '/results/' + run.type + '/' + id, so 'sweep' or NULL links to a 404.
- progress-tracker.html:37 builds '/results/{{ result_type }}/' from a template argument.
- assistant.py:629 and :695 hard-code the two URLs.
- routes.home_results and routes.fleet_results are chosen by URL alone and never read the record's type.

Two consequences of the routes never checking type:
- /results/home/<fleet run id> calls stored_home_config on a fleet config, which raises TypeError (probe) and answers 500.
- /results/fleet/<home run id> flashes 'Fleet run not found.' for a run that exists.

The save/load and submit pairs in storage.py and jobs.py are parallel per-type method pairs with no shared table.
findings.proposal: Give storage one per-type table, or a RunRecord method, that names a run's results endpoint, loader and exporter. findings.statement:
The database schema is created only by CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (database.py:171-225). No schema version is written or checked: no PRAGMA user_version anywhere in src/. The module docstring's whole migration policy is to delete the database file, which drops every run's history row while its files stay under data_dir/runs.

Two results follow:
- **Constraints added since a database was created never reach it.** Tasks 548 (2026-10-08) and 576 (2026-10-10) made the RunType, RunStatus, JobStatus, ChatRole and PresetType CHECKs and DEFAULTs derive from the Literals. Probe: an existing runs table without CHECKs keeps its old DDL after init_db, and then accepts type='bogus' and status='weird'. On every dashboard database created before those tasks, the second enforcement point exists only on paper.
- **RunRecord is coupled to the live table's exact columns.** storage._record_of_row builds RunRecord(**dict(row)) from SELECT * (storage.py:218, 652, 667), and _run_row_upsert names every RunRecord field (228-242). Adding a column to the DDL and to RunRecord therefore makes every run read on an existing database raise TypeError, and every save fail with 'no such column'.

The column list itself is stated twice, in the DDL and in RunRecord's fields, with no test comparing them.
findings.proposal: Have init_db write PRAGMA user_version and, on an existing file, compare it. It should either apply ordered migrations or refuse with an error naming both versions and the file. Derive the runs DDL column list from RunRecord's fields, as _run_row_upsert already does, and add a test that compares PRAGMA table_info(runs) with fields(RunRecord).
findings.next_change: An agent adds a column to runs (a sweep_id, say, to fix the prior sweep finding) or a new member to one of the Literals. To get it right, the agent must know three things: an existing user database will not receive the change; RunRecord(**row) then fails on every read; and the only documented remedy is deleting the user's history. Nothing catches a wrong version: every test builds a fresh database with init_db, so the suite stays green and the failure appears only on a real ~/.solar-challenge database.

findings.statement:
The dashboard needs one process per database (create_app's docstring note, app.py:69-74), but the only statement of that invariant is the docstring. It is enforced nowhere: there is no lock on DATA_DIR or the database, and no owner recorded on the jobs rows.

recover_stale_jobs is the code that depends on it most. create_app runs it on every construction (app.py:130). It UPDATEs every jobs row that is 'running' or 'queued', and every runs row that is 'running', to failed with 'Interrupted by server restart', whichever process owns them.

cli/web.py::start calls create_app() before flask_app.run() binds the port. A second `solar-challenge web start` against the default ~/.solar-challenge database, which then fails with 'Address already in use', has therefore already failed every in-flight job of the live server in both tables. The live job later rewrites both rows to completed (the save upsert, then _record_completed_job). Each run goes running→failed→completed, the illegal transition a prior finding says nothing refuses.
findings.proposal: Acquire an exclusive lock file under DATA_DIR in create_app before recovery, and refuse to start with an error naming the holder. Alternatively, stamp jobs rows with an instance id and recover only rows whose owner is gone. Either way, run recovery after the lock is held, not before the port is bound.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a deployment path such as a gunicorn entry point or a second dashboard on another port, or moves recover_stale_jobs. To get it right, the agent must know that recovery assumes every unfinished row belongs to a dead process. Nothing catches a wrong version: each test owns a temporary database, and the e2e server is the only process on its database.

findings.statement:
The server has two Server-Sent Events producers, assistant.chat and api.get_job_progress. Neither shares an encoder with the other.

- **Frames are written by hand at ten sites:** assistant.py:809, 938, 970, 1008 and 1032, and api.py:180, 203, 208, 221 and 230.
- **The event-stream Response is built twice with the same headers:** assistant._event_stream (812-821) and api.get_job_progress (233-240).
- **The 'error' event carries three payload shapes across the two streams:** {message} in assistant._error_frame, {status, message} in api._job_event_payload, and {error} in api's two literal frames.

The prior get_job_progress finding covers the last two shapes inside api.py. The cross-module copy of the framing and the response policy is not covered.
findings.proposal: Move SSE framing into one small web module, sse_frame(event, payload) plus event_stream(frames), and route both blueprints through it with one typed error payload.
findings.next_change: An agent acts on the prior finding by renaming the server's 'error' event so it no longer collides with EventSource's native one, or adds an id:/retry: field so reconnects resume. To get it right, the agent must edit both modules and both browser consumers, and must know that assistant.js reads {message} while progress-tracker.js reads {message} or {error}. Nothing catches a partial edit except e2e runs of both pages.

The default name of a run is spelled at 11 sites in 6 files: 'Web Simulation', 'Fleet Simulation', 'Unnamed Run', 'Unnamed Fleet Run', 'Home Simulation' and 'Unnamed'.

Four of these sites have no effect on the job path:
- jobs.py:663 and :730 default the name again when calling save_home_run and save_fleet_run.
- storage.py:411 and :533 default it a third time.

The runs row is inserted at submit with run_name already defaulted (jobs.py:274, 321), and the save's upsert keeps the existing name, because 'name' is in _COLUMNS_A_RESAVE_KEEPS (storage.py:225). Editing it changes nothing, because the name actually stored is the one written at submit (jobs.py:321) and kept by the upsert. Getting it right requires reading storage's resave-keeps rule in another file. A test of the stored name would catch the wrong edit, but only if one is written.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10, uniformly enforced: what a refused web request raises has no single definition. number_fields.py's module docstring names ValueError as 'the error every web caller answers with HTTP 400'. ConfigurationError is not a ValueError (MRO measured: ConfigurationError, Exception), so each reader that calls a config parser decides on its own how to bridge the two. simulation_params rewraps ConfigurationError as ValueError at three sites (parse_seg_tariff, _parse_battery, parse_home_config's tariff), and its routes catch (ValueError, TypeError). fleet_scenario lets ConfigurationError through. It exports FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS = (ValueError, TypeError, ConfigurationError), which api.py catches at four routes and fleet_presets at one. builder_form catches (ConfigurationError, ValueError, IndexError) around load_fleet_config and ConfigurationError alone around parse_seg_rate. api.py's run export catches (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError, ConfigurationError). The tuple lists the exceptions seen so far rather than defining a refusal type, and the gaps reach users. AttributeError escapes: POST /api/fleet/export-yaml with location null, 51 or {latitude: 50} answers HTTP 500, measured at the pin. IndexError escapes too (prior fk-a0866b1bd680). TypeError inside the tuple turns a programming error in any reader into a 400 that carries Python's internal message.
findings.proposal: Give web refusals one type. Either make config.ConfigurationError a ValueError subclass, or define one web RequestRefused raised by every reader through a single boundary translator. Every route then catches that one type, FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS and the three rewraps are deleted, and TypeError stops standing in for a refusal.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a config parser call to one reader, for example parsing a heat_pump or ev block on the fleet form with config's _parse_heat_pump_config grammar, or parse_location_block for a fleet location. To get it right it must know which of the three conventions that reader's routes use: rewrap, export it in the tuple, or a local tuple. It must also know that ConfigurationError is not a ValueError and which routes catch which tuple, which means reading api.py and number_fields. A wrong guess answers HTTP 500. Nothing catches that unless a test posts exactly the refused input, because the per-reader tuples are not checked against each other.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings. The home and fleet readers take a location as a string, either a preset name or a 'lat,lon' pair that home.html builds by joining custom_lat + ',' + custom_lon. shared.resolve_location splits it on ',' and falls back silently to Bristol for anything it cannot parse. Measured at the pin: 'londn', 'nan,0' and the strings 'None' and "{'latitude': 50}" all resolve to Bristol. parse_home_config first applies str() to any JSON value, so a null or mapping location runs in Bristol. POST /api/fleet/export-yaml with location 'londn' answers 200 and writes latitude 51.45 into the exported scenario. A non-string location on the fleet form answers HTTP 500 (finding .1). The slice holds two other location grammars. builder_form._location_block refuses an unknown preset and takes custom coordinates as numbers. The scenario grammar's location is a mapping that fleet import reads with config.parse_location_block. That makes three readers with three policies for one fact (heuristic 11) and silent substitution in two of them (heuristic 10, informative). The assistant's trigger tools describe location as a free string, 'e.g. bristol (default) or london' (assistant.py:446-449), so a model-chosen 'Cardiff' runs Bristol with no error.
findings.proposal: Parse location once at the request boundary into a Location, refusing an unknown preset or bad coordinates with a message that names the value. Send custom coordinates as a {latitude, longitude} mapping rather than a comma string, ideally the mapping parse_location_block already reads, so that the home, fleet and builder readers share one reader.

findings.statement: Heuristic 3, orthogonal dimensions of variability. Whether a field counts as 'not sent' is one axis, and each of the three request readers decides it differently, mostly as a side effect of merging dicts. builder_form._present_fields states one rule: null and '' are both absent. parse_home_config merges {**_HOME_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, **data}. A null therefore reads as unset only where the default happens to be None (the battery settings, consumption_kwh, name, heat_pump, tariff, seg, dispatch_strategy). It is refused where the default is a value (pv_kw, azimuth, tilt, occupants and the rest; measured: pv_kw null gives 'pv_kw must be a finite number, got None'). '' reads as absent only for start and end, through _window_sent, and is refused everywhere else, including days. The fleet form reads n_homes and seed with form_data.get(key, default), so an absent seed is 42 but a null one is refused. Its blocks follow a stated rule where null means none. A null location crashes it (finding .2), and fleet import reads a null seed as absent. Presence was fixed one reader at a time: 244, 393, 447 (twice), 496 and 524 all landed in fleet_config.py or simulation_params.py.
findings.proposal: State presence once: one helper, like builder_form._present_fields, that every reader applies to its body before reading. Separate 'default when absent' from 'nullable' in the defaults map, instead of letting the default's value decide.
findings.next_change: An agent adds an optional field to the home form (an EV block, or an altitude for a custom location) or to the fleet form. To make a cleared input behave like the other fields it must know that _HOME_CONFIG_DEFAULTS' None-versus-value default decides whether null is accepted, that only the window fields treat '' as absent, and that the builder treats both as absent. That takes the merge semantics, home.html's parseFloat-to-NaN-to-JSON-null behaviour, and builder_form. A wrong guess shows up as a 400 or a silent default that only a test for that exact null or '' would catch. The fix history shows it is usually caught after merge.

findings.statement: Heuristic 3 and heuristic 11. The tariff types and dispatch strategies the fleet form holds, and each one's settings, are spelled in three files across two languages, with no server constant reaching the page. fleet_scenario._FORM_TARIFF_SETTINGS and _FORM_DISPATCH_SETTINGS decide what an imported scenario may hold. simulate/fleet.html hard-codes the option lists (flat_rate, economy_7, economy_10; self_consumption, tou_optimized, peak_shaving) and the x-show conditions for each type's inputs. fleet-simulator.js branches on the type in buildPayload, which serialises, and in _applyTariff/_applyDispatch, which apply an imported form. Its else branches encode a rule the server table does not: every tariff type other than flat_rate is a peak/off-peak pair. config.py keeps the grammar's own type table on top of these. The copies agree today. Only the post-merge e2e lane (tests/e2e/test_fleet_interactions.py) exercises the JS against the server.

If it misses the table, the export succeeds but re-import refuses with 'tariff.type must be one the fleet page holds'. If it misses the JS else branch, peak/off-peak keys are posted for the new type. findings.statement:
The tree tracks `.claude` as a symlink (git mode 120000, blob 6ddfab8) whose target is `../../../../.claude`. It was added in a4c2970 (2026-02-20, 'auto-claude: subtask-4-4 - End-to-end verification...') from a worktree nested four levels deep, where that path reached the main repo's .claude.

At this repo's layout the target is wrong everywhere:
- From the main checkout it resolves to /.claude, which does not exist.
- From every orchestrator task worktree (.worktrees/<N>/.claude) it resolves to /home/leo/.claude, the user's global Claude configuration. That directory holds agents/, CLAUDE.md, cache/ and backups/.

So this repo can hold no project-scoped .claude content. In main a write fails. In a task worktree, the project scope is the user's global scope: outside git, outside review, and shared with every other project. The breakage is already absorbed in test infrastructure rather than fixed: tests/_working_tree.py::copy_working_tree's docstring and test_working_tree_helper.py::test_leaves_out_a_listed_path_that_is_not_a_regular_file special-case 'a worktree's .claude symlink'.
findings.proposal: Remove the tracked symlink (git rm .claude). If project-level Claude config is wanted, commit a real .claude/ directory. Reword the _working_tree docstring and its test to a generic symlink case.
findings.next_change:
An agent adds project-scoped Claude configuration. Examples: the /prd skill's optional overlay at .claude/skills/prd/project.md, or a project permission or hook in .claude/settings.json.

- In a task worktree, the write goes through the symlink into ~/.claude. `git status` shows nothing, the commit carries nothing, review sees nothing, and the change silently applies to every project's sessions. Under the landlock sandbox the write is refused instead, with an error naming a path outside the worktree that the agent cannot explain.
- In the main checkout the write fails on a dangling link.

To get it right, the agent must know the symlink's history, which nothing in the tree records. Nothing in the verify catches the wrong version.

findings.statement:
test_marker_registration.py guards network access by hand-kept lists, which the offline guard has since made a second mechanism (heuristic 11).
- INTEGRATION_FILES names 8 of the 25 tests/integration/test_*.py modules.
- NETWORKED_UNIT_CLASSES and PURE_UNIT_CLASSES name 9 classes across 3 files.
- Its own docstring concedes that a new network-touching class lacking @pytest.mark.slow 'will NOT be detected unless someone also adds it' to the list.

tests/conftest.py::pytest_runtest_protocol now fails every non-slow, non-e2e test in every module that reaches the network, naming the destination.

The file also pins the registration of the `integration` mark. Its pyproject description, 'may hit real PVGIS', does not match what the mark does (heuristic 1):
- No command selects or deselects on it: test_command uses -m 'not slow and not e2e', and no lane job names it.
- 14 integration modules apply it.
- 5 of those 14 are not slow and run offline in every verify: test_tou_dispatch_synthetic_weather, test_flex_timeshift, test_grid_charge_arbitrage, test_grid_services_events and test_flex_grid_services.

The mark carries no behaviour, and its stated meaning overlaps slow's.
findings.proposal: Delete TestIntegrationSuiteExcludedUnderNotSlow and TestNetworkedUnitClassesExcludedButPureKept, leaving the offline guard as the one mechanism. Then either retire the `integration` mark or give it a consumer and a description that matches it.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a TMY-fetching test class to tests/unit/test_fleet.py, or a new tests/integration module. The offline guard already fails it, naming PVGIS's host. findings.statement:
The public-surface contract is split between test_init_lazy_surface.py and test_public_api_surface.py by the PRD's task decomposition, not by behaviour. The docstrings say so directly: 'T3 owns this file...', 'T4 owns the surface-lock', and 'Bounded overlap in H3 / H4 is deliberate — this file must stand alone'.

Three tests exist in both files:
- test_import_is_pvlib_free, with the same body.
- test_touching_pv_imports_pvlib / test_touching_pvconfig_imports_pvlib.
- test_tariffperiod_collision_resolved.

The surface size 69 is asserted as a literal twice. One copy is test_init_lazy_surface.py:38. The other is test_public_api_surface.py:170, where `len(__all__) == len(FROZEN_SET)` already catches a duplicate. The count is restated in four more comments and docstrings, and get_cli_app's exclusion is asserted in both files.

The docstrings and section banners name H2/H3/H4, T3/T4 and PRD §3.1/§3.5/§10. A reader can resolve those only by opening docs/prds/domain-library-extraction.md. tests/integration/_external_probe.py says its pattern was 'adapted from tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py:47-64'; that function now spans lines 50-65 and reads private names the probe does not.
findings.proposal: Merge the two files into one surface-contract module organised by behaviour. Derive the count from FROZEN_SET instead of writing it as a literal. Drop the T3/T4/H-number ownership prose, and fix or remove the line-number pointer in _external_probe.py.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a 70th export. Besides __init__'s three tables, FROZEN_SURFACE and the release note, it must find the two `69` asserts in two files. Those fail loudly, but the four prose 69s and the T3/T4 ownership notes drift silently. If the agent instead changes laziness, for example making pv eager, it must edit two identical pairs of subprocess tests and decide which file 'owns' the change, from a task ID it cannot resolve without the PRD.

findings.statement:
The length of the simulated window has a carrier, SummaryStatistics.simulation_days, which home.calculate_summary derives from the minute index (home.py:539). bill_distribution and householder_bill (both on the frozen public surface) still take it as a separate simulation_days argument. Nothing checks that the argument matches the summaries it bills.

The callers take it from two sources:
- finance.py:2361-2363 and optimize.py:914-915 pass summaries[0].simulation_days.
- project_multi_year uses each home's s.simulation_days (finance.py:1578).
- cli/finance.py::run passes `days = (end_date - start_date).days + 1` computed from its own --start/--end (cli/finance.py:176, 209, 223).

That CLI expression subtracts tz-aware midnights, so it undercounts by one day for any window that crosses the spring-forward but not the autumn fall-back. load.py:284-289 carries a comment explaining exactly this, and uses calendar-date arithmetic instead. Probe at 7dfea36: for 2024-03-31..2024-04-01 the CLI expression gives 1 day, while the summary formula on the simulated minute index gives 2. For 2024-01-01..2024-06-30 it gives 181 against 182.

The annualisation scale is 365/days below 360 days, so `finance run` on the 2-day window bills the same summary at a total outlay of £1,647.98 instead of £938.96. Passing 365 for a 30-day summary gives £292.95 instead of £996.45, with no error.

The day-count formula itself is written at 10 sites in 7 modules: the 4 CLI commands, home.py, validation.py ×2 and web/charts.py ×2, plus load.py's correct variant. It has no shared helper.
findings.proposal: Keep the frozen signature, but have bill_distribution and householder_bill refuse a simulation_days that differs from the summaries' own, naming both values. Have cli/finance.py pass summaries[0].simulation_days. Put one covered-days helper in timebase.py, which home.calculate_summary, validation, charts and the CLI messages call.
findings.next_change: A finance or CLI edit that adds a new consumer of bill_distribution (a web finance page, a new CLI report) will pick a day count again, from dates or from summaries. To get it right, the agent must know that SummaryStatistics.simulation_days is the authoritative length and that tz-aware timedelta.days is wrong across DST, which only load.py's comment records. Nothing catches a wrong version: no test runs `finance run` over a DST-crossing window, and bill_distribution accepts any int.

findings.statement:
What 'Economy 7' and 'Economy 10' cost has two disagreeing homes.

**Library:** TariffConfig.economy_7 defaults to off-peak 0.09 / peak 0.25 £/kWh (tariff.py:208-209), and economy_10 to 0.08 / 0.27 (tariff.py:248-249). config.parse_tariff_config applies these to a rate-less block. Three shipped scenarios restate them by hand: bristol-phase1-flex.yaml:43-44, bristol-arbitrage.yaml:53-54 and example-economy7.yaml:45-46.

**Web forms:** both forms hard-code 0.35 / 0.13 in their Alpine state, home.html:48-50 and fleet-simulator.js:43-45. They hold one peak/off-peak pair shared by both economy types, and always send it (home.html:156-160, fleet-simulator.js:126-130).

Probe at 7dfea36: parse_tariff_config({'type': 'economy_7'}) charges 0.09 at 03:00 and 0.25 at 18:00, while the web's default Economy 7 payload charges 0.13 and 0.35. The web's default Economy 10 is identical to its Economy 7, where the library's differs. A dashboard run and a CLI run of a home described identically as 'Economy 7' are therefore priced about 40% apart at both rates.

The same pages already receive one server fact this way: routes.py passes seg.SEG_PRESETS into both templates (routes.py:98, :167). No tariff default reaches a page. The flat-rate default is a third independent value per page: 0.28 in home.html and fleet-simulator.js, 0.245 in scenario-builder.js:117, beside finance's retail_baseline_rate_pence_per_kwh of 23.0.
findings.proposal: Decide which rates are the Economy 7/10 reference, then give TariffConfig named preset defaults. routes.simulate_home_page and simulate_fleet_page should pass those defaults into the templates as they already pass SEG_PRESETS. The forms should then hold a rate per economy type, read from those defaults.
findings.next_change: A change to the tariff presets or the dashboard's tariff tab, such as a 2026 price refresh or adding a 'cosy' preset, would be made in tariff.py or a scenario and would not reach the forms, or the reverse. The agent must know that the forms keep their own numbers in Alpine x-data and in fleet-simulator.js. Nothing catches the drift: no test compares the forms' defaults with TariffConfig's.

findings.statement:
The default simulation window has no home in the library.

- **Library:** config.SimulationPeriod declares no default, and _parse_period requires both dates.
- **Web:** web/simulation_params.py holds the policy as FULL_YEAR_START = 2024-01-01, FULL_YEAR_END = 2024-12-31 and DAYS_WINDOW_START = 2024-06-01 (:34, :37, :42). assistant.py derives from these.
- **CLI:** it restates the same values as string literals in every command, with no import of either. These are --start/--end option defaults in cli/home.py run (:78, :85), cli/fleet.py run (:134, :141) and sweep (:274, :281), and cli/finance.py run (:83, :90). cli/optimize.py configs has its own fallback (:238-239).
- **Days window:** `home quick` starts it at the literal pd.Timestamp('2024-06-01') (cli/home.py:243), under the comment '# Default to starting today'.
- **Templates and JS:** `config template` emits the full-year pair twice (cli/config.py:40-41, 124-125), and scenario-builder.js restates it twice (:110-111, :136-137).

The copies agree today. Changing the reference year, or the days-window start that both `home quick` and the web's days requests use, takes 21 independent edits across 8 files in Python, YAML-in-strings and JS, and no test ties them together.
findings.proposal: Define the default full-year window and the days-window start once, as constants beside SimulationPeriod or in timebase.py. Have the CLI option defaults, cli/optimize's fallback, cli/config's templates, `home quick` and web/simulation_params import them, and have the builder page receive them from its route.
findings.next_change: Any move of the reference year needs one edit at each of the 21 sites in 8 files. Examples are a TMY-alignment change, a non-leap default, or a 'last full year' default. So does a new CLI command that simulates. The agent must find every literal by grep, because none points at the others. A missed site shows up only as two entry points silently simulating different windows.

findings.statement:
Two PVGIS request policies live in weather.py, and only one of them has a single home.

- **TMY request:** a frozen PVGIS_TMY_REQUEST mapping (weather.py:39-50). weather.get_tmy_data and scripts/measure_tmy_irradiation.py:85 both read it.
- **Hourly climate-years request:** this is the series whose mean annual GHI scales every TMY (docs/tmy-irradiation-scaling.md). It has no counterpart mapping. Its keyword set is spelled out three times: weather._fetch_mean_annual_ghi_kwh_per_m2 (weather.py:362-373), scripts/measure_tmy_irradiation.py::fetch_real_years (:95-106) and scripts/measure_pv_performance_ratio.py::fetch_pvgis_estimate (:146-162). Each repeats start=CLIMATE_YEARS[0], end=CLIMATE_YEARS[-1], usehorizon=True, url=PVGIS_API_URL, timeout=PVGIS_TIMEOUT_S and map_variables=True.

The scripts produce the measurements the scaling and losses docs cite. If the shipped scaling's horizon or database policy changes, they keep measuring against the old one. The two scripts also each define an identical annual_ac_kwh (measure_pv_performance_ratio.py:124, measure_tmy_irradiation.py:120).
findings.proposal: Add a frozen PVGIS_HOURLY_REQUEST mapping beside PVGIS_TMY_REQUEST in weather.py, holding the shared climate-years arguments. All three callers then spread it and add only their own components, surface and pvcalculation arguments.
findings.next_change: A change to PVGIS policy needs 3 edits, one per call site. Examples are the v5_3 to next radiation-database move, dropping usehorizon, or a different climate-year span not expressed through CLIMATE_YEARS. Getting it right means finding the two scripts that copy the call. Nothing catches a missed copy: the scripts run only by hand, and the pvgis lane job tests only weather's own requests.

findings.statement:
How the dashboard opens a SQLite connection is written three times:
- database.init_db (database.py:63-65) sets journal_mode=WAL and row_factory, but not foreign_keys.
- database.get_db (database.py:243-245) sets row_factory and foreign_keys=ON. It serves 19 call sites in 7 files.
- jobs.JobManager._run_job (jobs.py:598-600) copies get_db's two setup lines for its long-lived per-job connection.

foreign_keys matters because the schema's jobs.run_id has REFERENCES runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (database.py:91). SQLite enforces that only on connections that set the pragma.

The history shows the drift mechanism. 82dc6c8 (2026-03-10, 'enable WAL mode and foreign key enforcement') changed database.py only. cded581, the same day, introduced jobs.py's own connection by copying the setup. A future pragma, such as busy_timeout for the WAL writer contention that a background job and request handlers share, must be added at both places, and init_db's connection already differs from both.
findings.proposal: Extract one database.connect(db_path) that applies the connection policy. get_db, init_db and jobs._run_job's long-lived connection all call it.
findings.next_change: Adding a connection pragma or a sqlite3 adapter means editing get_db and also jobs._run_job, which nothing points to. Examples: busy_timeout, synchronous=NORMAL, a datetime adapter. A missed copy surfaces only under contention in a running job: no test opens a job connection and inspects its pragmas.

findings.statement:
Two domain value types, DispatchStrategyConfig (config.py:356) and GridChargeConfig (config.py:254), are defined in config.py, the YAML-parser stratum that sits above every simulation module. Yet they are fields of BatteryConfig (battery.py:164-165), and the simulation reads them below config:
- flow.py:183-188, 261 and 385 read battery.config.grid_charging.target_soc_fraction into dispatch.GridChargeContext.
- home._create_dispatch_strategy (home.py:262-289) maps strategy_type, peak_hours and import_limit_kw onto dispatch.py's strategy classes.

battery.py can name the types only under TYPE_CHECKING (battery.py:11-12), because config.py imports battery at top level. That one typing edge, battery->config, is the edge that closes import_graph's 8-module typing cycle (battery, community, config, finance, fleet, flow, gridservices, home). Removing it leaves only the 3-module config/finance/gridservices cycle.

The cost leaks into the web layer. web/storage.py imports the whole 2,815-line solar_challenge.config module (storage.py:31) for one purpose: _field_types merges vars(solar_challenge.config) into the annotation namespace so that get_type_hints can resolve battery's string annotations. Its docstring spends 3 lines (storage.py:113-115) explaining why. web/fleet_config.py:26 also imports DispatchStrategyConfig from config under TYPE_CHECKING. The two modules that consume the types disagree on the error type: DispatchStrategyConfig.__post_init__ raises ConfigurationError, and home._create_dispatch_strategy re-checks the same three strategy strings and raises ValueError.
findings.proposal: Make dispatch.py the owner of the dispatch-configuration types and the strategy factory, which moves home._create_dispatch_strategy there. Parsers in config.py then construct these types and never define them.
findings.next_change: Move GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig into the simulation stratum: dispatch.py, which imports only timebase, or battery.py. Import them at top level in battery.py, and have config.py import them from there. Delete the vars(solar_challenge.config) merge and its docstring in web/storage._field_types, and repoint web/fleet_config.py's import. The agent must know two things. First, the scenario_writer and config block parsers name these types. Second, the strategy vocabulary in DispatchStrategyConfig and in home._create_dispatch_strategy is the subject of the prior _VALID_DISPATCH_STRATEGIES finding, so the move should give that vocabulary one home. A wrong version is caught by mypy strict, by the stored-run round-trip tests in tests/unit/test_web_storage*, and by re-running the SCC script: no typing cycle through battery.

findings.statement:
ConfigurationError is the exception that domain value objects raise when a domain invariant fails, but it is defined in config.py (line 35), the parser that imports 13 domain modules at top level. finance.py and gridservices.py raise it, and they can reach it only through function-local imports, which import_graph marks closes_cycle=true:
- finance.py: lines 119 and 1540.
- gridservices.py: lines 237, 240, 243, 246, 251, 256, 261, 266 and 345.

Those 11 imports are the whole of the hidden cycle config -> finance -> gridservices -> config. The workaround costs prose: a 7-line 'Import cycle note' in gridservices' module docstring (lines 35-41), an 11-line '.. important::' block in EventWindow.__post_init__ (lines 224-234), a further docstring and comment explanation in GridServicesEventsConfig.__post_init__ (lines 337-345), and an inline comment at finance.py:119. Each new validation branch in EventWindow must repeat the import inside the branch, because DEFAULT_EVENT_WINDOWS constructs EventWindow at module load.

The rest of the domain does not use it. The other 18 domain modules raise ValueError only (battery 15, dispatch 26, pv 14, optimize 21, and so on). finance mixes the two (10 ConfigurationError, 22 ValueError), as does gridservices (14 ConfigurationError, 3 ValueError). A caller cannot tell from a module's stratum which exception a refused value raises.
findings.proposal: Give the package a bottom stratum for its shared error vocabulary, and make 'which exception a domain invariant raises' one decision recorded there.
findings.next_change: Create a leaf module that imports no solar_challenge module, such as solar_challenge/errors.py. Define ConfigurationError there and import it at top level in config.py, finance.py and gridservices.py. Delete the 11 local imports and the cycle prose. The agent must know two things. ConfigurationError is not in __all__, so tests that import it from solar_challenge.config keep resolving through config's own import of it. And whether it should subclass ValueError is the web finding fleet_form_refusals's open question, so decide that in the same change or leave it unchanged on purpose. A wrong version is caught by mypy, by the 156 pytest.raises and except sites in tests, and by import_graph showing no hidden cycle.

findings.statement:
finance.py, at 2,376 lines and over the 2,000-line alarm, holds two strata, and the layering cost appears as function-local imports and a private cross-module import.
- **Lower stratum:** FinanceConfig, BillBreakdown, BillDistribution, bill, householder_bill, bill_distribution and their helpers, 1,195 lines. These do arithmetic over SummaryStatistics, and config.py imports FinanceConfig from here at top level.
- **Upper stratum:** project_multi_year (318 lines), solve_cost_recovery_rate (181), project_economics (132), _aged_homes, _throughput_at, _NodeData, _resolve_homes, _reconcile_seg_homes and the NPV/IRR helpers, 933 lines. These take a ScenarioConfig and run fleet simulations.

The upper half needs everything above the lower half. It reaches it only through 7 function-local imports that import_graph marks closes_cycle=false: fleet.simulate_fleet at 1517 and 2276, FleetConfig at 1561 and 2350, home.calculate_summary at 1562 and 2351, pv.calculate_degradation_factor at 1563, and battery.compute_soh at 1422. It also needs a TYPE_CHECKING import of config.ScenarioConfig (line 35), the edge that, with ConfigurationError, closes config<->finance.

optimize.py imports the private finance._resolve_homes (optimize.py:35). It is the only private-name import between src modules in the whole graph, and it shows that the scenario-orchestration helpers are a shared stratum with no module of their own.

Partition measurement (heuristic 14): lower->upper references 0; upper->lower references 10. Five of those are private: _annualisation_scale, _annualise_physics, _billed_energy, _cbs_own_use_kwh and _seg_export_income_gbp. A split therefore passes heuristic 13 only if those 5 become the lower module's named interface. Otherwise the upper file would reach into the lower file's privates.
findings.proposal: Name the missing stratum as a scenario-economics layer that composes simulation with bill arithmetic, so that finance.py is the bill-arithmetic module config can depend on and nothing below it needs a lazy import.
findings.next_change: Move the scenario-driven projection and solver functions (project_multi_year, solve_cost_recovery_rate, project_economics and their helpers) into a module above finance, beside optimize.py, which already sits at that level. That module imports config, fleet, home, pv, battery and gridservices at top level. Promote the 5 private bill helpers it uses to finance.py's public interface. The agent must preserve the frozen surface: solar_challenge.__init__ maps solve_cost_recovery_rate to 'finance' in _SYMBOL_MODULE. It must also preserve the pvlib-free bare import, since a top-level fleet import pulls pvlib via pv.py. The test_public_api_surface/test_init_lazy_surface tests and mypy catch a wrong version, and the import graph should show 0 deferred imports in either file.

findings.statement:
ScenarioConfig encodes 'the homes of a scenario' as an either/or of `home` and `homes`, and 'the SEG rate' as a scenario-level float beside each home's seg_tariff. It offers no accessor for either, so each consumer above it re-derives both, with different policies.

Homes are resolved in 4 independent places:
- finance._resolve_homes (finance.py:1796): 3 callers in finance, and optimize imports it privately.
- cli/validate._scenario_homes (cli/validate.py:174).
- config.run_parameter_sweep, which branches on home vs homes (config.py:2488-2506).
- optimize._repriced_at_seg_rate and _build_axis_configs, which read scenario.homes only (optimize.py:435, 489).

Probe: _build_axis_configs(..., 'degradation', 0.02) on a single-home ScenarioConfig returns the home's degradation_rate_per_year unchanged at 0.005 and homes=[], so the knob silently does nothing.

SEG is threaded onto homes in 3 places, with 3 policies:
- finance._reconcile_seg_homes fills homes whose seg_tariff is None and refuses a mismatch. Its docstring says it 'mirrors the threading workaround in cli/finance.py:162-169'; at the pin those lines are 163-170.
- cli/finance.run overwrites every home's seg_tariff.
- optimize._repriced_at_seg_rate overwrites every home and the scenario rate.

Two of finance's _resolve_homes callers, project_economics and optimize's age-0 outlay at optimize.py:890, do not reconcile SEG at all.
findings.proposal: Make ScenarioConfig a deep value object that hides its home/homes and scenario-SEG encoding behind two methods, so that the finance, optimize and CLI strata stop reconstructing it.
findings.next_change: Give ScenarioConfig the operations its consumers re-derive. One is a homes property that returns the non-empty list for either form. The other is a single SEG-resolution method that returns homes with the scenario SEG applied under one stated policy. Replace finance._resolve_homes, _reconcile_seg_homes, cli/validate._scenario_homes, the optimize knob loops and the cli/finance threading with calls to them. findings.statement:
Sweeps have no stratum of their own. config.py, the parser, contains a simulation runner, run_parameter_sweep (config.py:2465-2506), with its SweepResult, ParameterSweepConfig and four _apply/_modify helpers: 266 lines with no src caller (only tests/unit/config/test_parameter_sweep.py). It is the only reason config.py imports simulate_home and simulate_fleet at top level (config.py:24, 27).

It is also wrong. _apply_parameter_to_home rebuilds HomeConfig field by field at 3 sites and drops heat_pump_config, ev_config and seg_tariff, 3 of HomeConfig's 10 fields. Probe: a home with an ASHP and a SEG tariff, swept on pv_capacity_kw or annual_consumption_kwh, comes back with heat_pump_config=None and seg_tariff=None.

The sweeps that ship live elsewhere, as 3 more runners:
- fleet.simulate_multi_sweep_iter, used by cli fleet sweep.
- optimize.run_sweep.
- web/api.simulate_sweep, one home job per point.

Sweep values are generated 3 ways:
- config.SweepSpec.get_values: min/max/steps/mode, refusing an unknown mode.
- config.ParameterSweepConfig.get_values: step/n_steps.
- web/api.py:555-564: restates SweepSpec's geometric/linear arithmetic and its min>0, max>min and steps>=2 checks inline, but treats an unknown mode as linear instead of refusing it.
findings.proposal: Keep sweep definitions (value generation) in one type that the parser and the web reader both build, and keep execution in the simulation/orchestration strata, never in the parser.
findings.next_change: Delete run_parameter_sweep, SweepResult, ParameterSweepConfig and _apply_parameter_to_home/_modify_* together with their test file, which removes config's runtime dependence on simulate_home and simulate_fleet. Have web/api.simulate_sweep construct a config.SweepSpec, or a sweep-values type moved below config, and call get_values. The agent must confirm with the platform-consumer contract that these names are not used outside the repo (they are absent from __all__). The web sweep tests (tests/e2e/test_parameter_sweep.py, tests/unit web api tests) catch a changed value set, and a probe of mode='bogus' should now give a 400.

findings.statement:
The two front ends each define their own location-string grammar, because no stratum below them owns one. location.py offers only Location.bristol().
- **CLI:** cli/utils.parse_location (cli/utils.py:98) accepts the preset 'bristol' only, 'lat,lon' or 'lat,lon,alt', and raises on anything else.
- **Web:** web/shared.resolve_location (web/shared.py:59) accepts 4 presets (bristol, london, edinburgh, manchester, defined in LOCATION_PRESETS beside it) or 'lat,lon', and falls back silently to Bristol.

Probed at the pin, the same string means different places. '51.5,-0.1,11' is London's coordinates in the CLI and Bristol on the web. 'london' raises in the CLI but is London on the web. Meanwhile `solar-challenge config locations` lists only bristol and advertises the lat,lon,altitude form the web cannot read. The presets are spelled again in 3 templates: simulate/home.html, scenarios/builder.html and scenarios/sweep.html.
findings.next_change: Put the named presets and one strict 'preset or lat,lon[,alt]' parser beside Location, in location.py, and make cli/utils.parse_location and web/shared.resolve_location thin callers. Rendering the template option lists from the preset table is the web half. The agent must decide with the web owner whether the web keeps its silent Bristol fallback, which is the web finding _fleet_form_location's question. cli tests for --location and the web location tests catch a wrong grammar.
