findings.statement:
web/shared.py ('Shared helpers') mixes two strata.
- **Request-reading values:** NotAJsonObject, require_json_object, request_json_object, LOCATION_PRESETS and resolve_location.
- **Flask service accessors:** get_storage and get_job_manager. To return typed objects these import web.jobs and web.storage at top level (shared.py:11-12).

The three pure request readers import shared only for the first group: builder_form for LOCATION_PRESETS, NotAJsonObject and require_json_object; fleet_scenario for resolve_location; simulation_params for require_json_object and resolve_location. Through shared, their import closure therefore includes web.jobs (the job manager, which imports fleet and home), web.storage (which imports all of config, fleet and home) and web.database (sqlite). So the form-parsing stratum sits on top of the persistence and job stratum it never calls.

The module's purpose cannot be stated without 'and'. Its 7 importers split cleanly: history and routes use only get_storage. api and assistant use both groups. The three readers use only the first group.
findings.next_change: Split shared.py along that line. The request-reading helpers and the location presets go to a module that imports no web service. That module, or location.py per layering.6, can hold the location parser. get_storage and get_job_manager go next to app/jobs. The agent must update 7 import sites and keep NotAJsonObject's ValueError base, which the refusal tuples rely on. Re-running the closure script catches a wrong version: the readers' closure must exclude web.jobs and web.storage.

findings.statement: Grid charging (battery top-up from the grid in cheap periods) is one axis. It is switched on only by a three-way conjunction of settings that live in three different homes: BatteryConfig.grid_charging (battery block), HomeConfig.tariff_config (home block), and which dispatcher home.py picks (HomeConfig.dispatch_strategy or BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy). The conjunction is re-tested at four sites in two modules: flow.py:261 (tariff is not None and grid_charging is not None), flow.py:385 (grid_charging inside simulate_timestep_tou's cheap branch), and dispatch.py:510 and :662 (ctx is not None and is_cheap_period, in TOUOptimized and PeakShaving). SelfConsumptionStrategy accepts grid_charge_ctx and documents it as 'accepted but not used' (dispatch.py:288). No site refuses or warns about a grid_charging block that the chosen dispatcher will ignore. Probe: one synthetic June day, Economy 7, GridChargeConfig(target_soc_fraction=0.9). The default dispatch stores 0.000 kWh from the grid, and so do an explicit battery self_consumption strategy and home tou_optimized without a tariff. Home tou_optimized stores 2.080 kWh and battery peak_shaving 2.000 kWh. The only warning raised is the unrelated SEG one.
findings.proposal: Make dispatcher selection the single owner of the axis. _create_dispatch_strategy should take the battery's grid_charging and the tariff. It returns a dispatcher that honours grid charging, or it refuses the combination with a ConfigurationError that names grid_charging and the chosen strategy. flow would then build the context only from what the selected dispatcher declares it needs.
findings.next_change: An agent adding grid charging to self-consumption dispatch, or a new strategy, has to learn the conjunction from four scattered sites and from home.py's use_tariff_tou precedence. Nothing catches a new strategy that ignores grid_charge_ctx, and nothing catches a config that sets grid_charging under a dispatcher that ignores it: the result is a plausible-looking 0 kWh. A wrong version is caught only by a test that asserts non-zero grid charge for that exact combination.

findings.statement: 'When is it peak or cheap' is one axis, defined by four independent mechanisms. (1) flow._is_cheap_period classifies from the home's TariffConfig; simulate_timestep_tou and every GridChargeContext use it. (2) DispatchStrategyConfig.peak_hours is a hand-entered list of whole hours (config.py:366) that TOUOptimizedStrategy._get_tariff_period uses for its charge and discharge decisions. (3) ev.py's literal 00:30-07:30 and 10:00-16:00 windows (already held under the ev canonical; named here only as a site). (4) TariffConfig.economy_7/economy_10's own off_peak_start/end parameters. A single TOUOptimizedStrategy step uses two of them at once: peak_hours gates discharge and tariff cheapness gates grid charging. The 9-line 'Seam note' at dispatch.py:497-505 exists to explain this. peak_hours is validated at three points: DispatchStrategyConfig.__post_init__ (config.py:380-384), home._create_dispatch_strategy (home.py:281) and TOUOptimizedStrategy.__init__. With the shipped scenario's peak_hours [[16,19]] (scenarios/dispatch-comparison.yaml:176), the strategy treats 840 of the 1,440 minutes of an Economy 7 day as off-peak although the tariff charges the day rate. It therefore holds the battery and imports at 0.25 £/kWh.
findings.proposal: Have TOUOptimizedStrategy take its period classification from the tariff (the GridChargeContext already carries is_cheap_period) rather than from peak_hours. Keep peak_hours only as an explicit override that is refused when it contradicts the home's tariff. The EV scheduler would then read the same classifier.
findings.next_change: A change to how peak is defined, such as seasonal tariffs, the Flux or Agile style tariffs the briefing anticipates, or a new tariff preset, has to edit the tariff, then also the YAML peak_hours that tou_optimized homes carry and the EV windows. An agent reading only tariff.py would not know that dispatch has its own clock. No test compares the strategy's peak hours with the tariff it runs under.

findings.statement:
The two optional extra loads, heat pump and EV, are added to demand by two different mechanisms at two layers.

Heat pump: home.simulate_home composes it itself (home.py:351-361) and keeps it as a named series, SimulationResults.heat_pump_load. It gets three Optional SummaryStatistics fields and presence branches at every layer above: home.py 3, output.py 5, web/charts.py 1, results/home.html 2, simulate/home.html 1, scenario_writer 1, config.py 4.

EV: it is threaded as an ev_config kwarg into load.generate_load_profile, the household load model. A function-local import of ev (load.py:447, import graph deferred, closes_cycle=false) merges it into demand there. It leaves no series or summary field, and has 0 mentions in output.py, fleet.py, web/ or cli/.

So an EV's charging energy cannot be told apart from household demand in any result, report, chart or stored run. Each further load kind (both prior shapes are already there) costs about 15 presence branches across 7 files under the heat-pump pattern, or is invisible under the EV pattern.
findings.proposal: Give additional loads one mechanism. home.simulate_home composes a sequence of (name, series) contributions from each configured load component; the EV moves out of load.generate_load_profile. Results then carry a mapping of named load series, and summary, output and charts iterate it instead of branching per kind.
findings.next_change: Adding a third load, such as a heat battery or immersion diverter, or showing EV energy on the results page, needs an agent to choose between two precedents and then add an Optional field, three summary fields and branches in output, charts, templates, writer and parser. The tests pin each layer separately, so a forgotten layer is silent, as the EV's absence everywhere already is.

findings.statement:
How a fleet is executed (parallelism, worker cap, balance validation, which home simulator, progress) is one axis carried by four mechanisms.

- **fleet.py:** the positional and keyword tuple (validate_balance, parallel, max_workers) is threaded through simulate_fleet, simulate_fleet_iter and simulate_multi_sweep_iter, with validate_balance continuing into both _simulate_home_worker variants, home.simulate_home and community.simulate_community.
- **finance and optimize:** an injected `simulate: Optional[Callable]` is threaded through 6 functions (finance.project_multi_year, solve_cost_recovery_rate; optimize.run_sweep, sensitivity_panel, _evaluate_config, _age0_baseline_outlay). It is defaulted by `if simulate is None` at 3 sites, two of them a function-local import of fleet.simulate_fleet (finance.py:1517, :2276).
- **CLI:** cli/utils.CliFleetSimulator holds the third mechanism.
- **Web:** web/jobs._run_fleet_simulation loops sequentially over an injected simulate_home (jobs.py:707-713) and assembles FleetResults itself.

The mechanisms do not compose. --workers and --sequential exist on 2 of the 4 fleet-simulating commands (fleet run, fleet sweep), so `finance run` and `optimize configs` (default path: 8 run_sweep calls over 36 configs) always fan out to every CPU. No src caller ever passes validate_balance=False, so 7 signatures carry a switch only tests flip (2 sites, test_community.py). FleetResults is assembled from fresh simulations at 4 sites (fleet.py:410, :646, cli/fleet.py:207, web/jobs.py:716).
findings.proposal: Make the execution policy one frozen value (for example a FleetRunner holding parallel, max_workers, validate_balance and a progress sink) with a single simulate(FleetConfig, start, end) method. Build it once at each boundary (CLI options, web JobManager, tests) and pass it to finance and optimize in place of the bare callable. The kwargs then leave fleet.py's public functions.
findings.next_change: Adding a worker cap or progress to `finance run`, or making the web fleet job use the process pool, needs an agent to thread new kwargs through finance and optimize's 6 functions, or to wrap simulate_fleet in a closure in each CLI. Whichever mechanism is chosen leaves the other three behind. The overlap with the held cli/fleet.py::run finding is the CLI half only. This is the library half: nothing type-checks that the injected callable honours the policy.

findings.statement:
'Vary one named setting of a scenario across runs' is one axis. It has five mechanisms, each with its own string vocabulary for which knob moves:

1. config.detect_sweep_spec and _replace_sweep_with_value: only battery.capacity_kwh's multiplier (held canonical, named here as a site).
2. cli/fleet.py sweep --param: any ${VAR} substituted into raw YAML.
3. web/api._SWEEP_PARAMETER_HOME_KEYS: 3 knobs mapped to home-form keys.
4. config._apply_parameter_to_home: 8 knobs, test-only callers.
5. optimize: enumerate_configs/_apply_install has 3 fixed install axes, and _build_axis_configs routes any FinanceConfig field plus the string aliases 'seg'/'seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh' and 'degradation'/'degradation_rate_per_year' through an if/elif chain. On top of these, sensitivity_panel special-cases the literal 'retained_cash_floor_per_home_per_year_gbp', and cli/optimize._SENSITIVITY_ALIAS_MAP adds 5 more aliases.

One knob therefore has many spellings. Battery capacity is battery.capacity_kwh multiplier, battery_capacity_kwh, battery_kwh and a free ${VAR}. PV capacity is pv_capacity_kw, pv_kw and pv_kwp. Sweep spacing is a mode string defaulting to 'geometric' in SweepSpec and the CLI but 'linear' in web/api.py:550. Degradation and SEG can be swept only in optimize, and tilt and occupants only in the test-only engine.
findings.proposal: Define one knob registry below the entry points: a mapping from a typed knob identifier to a pure ScenarioConfig -> ScenarioConfig (or HomeConfig) transform, with value generation always from SweepSpec. optimize's sensitivity axes, the web sweep, the CLI and the YAML sweep resolve names through it. Aliases live in one table, and the test-only _apply_parameter_to_home is deleted in its favour.
findings.next_change: Adding a sweepable knob, for example inverter size on the web sweep page or tilt in optimize, means picking one of five routers and inventing a sixth spelling. An unknown name is refused in each router's own words, or in the YAML case accepted and then refused at generation (held detect_sweep_spec finding). No test checks that the same knob name means the same field across entry points.

findings.statement:
How a simulated window's length changes a figure is one axis, and each consumer decides it with its own rule and threshold.

- **finance._annualisation_scale** (its docstring says 'the single annualisation rule') scales by 365/days below 360 days, else by 1.0.
- **validation.validate_consumption_profile** always scales by 365/duration (validation.py:302), so a 400-day window is scaled down by 0.9125, which finance never does.
- **validation._check_annual_yield** returns None under 365 days and does not scale above it (validation.py:88).
- **output.aggregate_annual**, documented 'Aggregate results to annual totals', never scales: it returns calculate_summary's window totals.
- **web/charts gates:** the monthly chart is suppressed under 90 days (charts.py:371) and the seasonal one under 180 (charts.py:527).

The window length itself is recomputed from a series index as `(index[-1] - index[0]).days + 1` at 4 sites (validation.py:87, :299; charts.py:370, :526), although SummaryStatistics.simulation_days (home.py:539) already holds it. The same 30-, 362- or 400-day run is therefore annualised differently by the bill, by validation and by the 'annual' aggregate.
findings.proposal: Make the window a typed value: SimulationWindow(days) carrying annualisation_scale(), defined once below finance, validation and output. Have each consumer take the scale from it (or from SummaryStatistics.simulation_days). Rename aggregate_annual to name the window total, or make it annualise through the same rule.
findings.next_change: An agent changing the annualisation threshold or basis (a leap year, a multi-year run) edits finance's helper and believes its docstring that it is the single rule. Validation and the aggregate keep their own rules, and the board report and validation report then disagree on the same run without any test failing. The held householder_bill (h1) and _check_annual_yield defect findings are each one symptom of this axis.

Weaknesses: (1) The finance docstring does not claim to be the single rule for the codebase. It says the rule is single because householder_bill and project_multi_year both annualise through _annualise_physics, so the reviewer's 'an agent believes its docstring' is a misreading. findings.statement: Whether a community has a shared battery is one fact encoded twice: the mode string sharing_mode ('p2p' | 'community_battery') and the presence of community_battery. CommunityConfig.__post_init__ spends 3 ifs keeping them consistent (community.py:85-98). simulate_community then branches on the battery's presence (`cb_config is None`, community.py:268), not on the mode. The mode string is copied into CommunityResults.sharing_mode (Literal) and into output.CommunityMetrics.sharing_mode, where it is widened to `str` (output.py:433). The YAML grammar requires both keys and refuses mismatches (config.py:2768-2785). A writer must therefore state the axis twice, and the parser, the dataclass and the report each restate the two-word vocabulary.
findings.proposal: Derive the mode from the configuration: drop sharing_mode as an input, or make it a property computed from community_battery. If more modes are coming, make each mode a frozen variant type carrying exactly its own fields.
findings.next_change: Adding a third sharing mode, for example VNM billing without netting, has to extend the Literal, the three consistency ifs, the parser's message and the str-typed report field, while the dispatch keeps branching on battery presence. That makes it easy to add a mode the simulation silently treats as p2p.

findings.statement:
Per-home seeding (CLAUDE.md: 'Reproducible simulations via per-home seeding') is carried through process-global state, not the call. _try_richardsonpy_profile does `np.random.seed(config.seed); random.seed(config.seed)` and then lets richardsonpy draw from the global numpy and random generators. config.generate_homes_from_distribution, by contrast, samples through an explicit random.Random(config.seed).

A profile's output therefore depends on whatever ran before it in the same process:
- **Unseeded after seeded:** an unseeded LoadConfig simulated after a seeded one is a deterministic copy (probe: two unseeded runs after seed 5 are identical).
- **External seeding:** an unseeded run after an external np.random.seed(123) is reproducible, so a caller's unrelated seeding silently fixes it.
- **Concurrent threads:** the web JobManager runs simulations on a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) (jobs.py:207), and web fleets are seeded (default seed 42, home i gets 42+i, config.py:1751-1754). Two concurrent seeded profiles (seeds 42 and 43) differed from their serial runs in 10 of 10.

A web fleet run started while another job runs is stored as seeded yet is not reproducible, and nothing reports it. The same leak crosses homes within a ProcessPoolExecutor worker in fleet.simulate_fleet_iter. The stochastic engine also has no seam: tests reach it by patching richardsonpy's module attribute (test_load.py:404, 431, 514) and load's private _simulate_stochastic_day (test_load.py:547).
findings.proposal: Give load.py one owner of the global-RNG hand-off: a module-private lock plus a context that saves the np.random/random state, seeds it from the LoadConfig's seed (or fresh SeedSequence entropy when the seed is None), runs the richardsonpy window, and restores the state. Every stochastic draw goes through it. Make the per-day simulator an injectable parameter of generate_load_profile so tests stop patching richardsonpy and load privates. Add a test that runs two seeded profiles on two threads and compares them with the serial ones.
findings.next_change: An agent adding parallelism (e.g. raising JobManager max_workers, or running web fleet jobs through simulate_fleet) or a new stochastic generator will assume the seed travels with LoadConfig, as the config sampler's does. They must know richardsonpy reads only the globals. Today nothing catches a wrong version: no test runs two seeded simulations concurrently or checks an unseeded home after a seeded one.

findings.statement:
flow.py reaches through the Battery into its config: 11 reads of battery.config.* (capacity_kwh, max_charge_kw, grid_charging). These are facts the Battery already owns in derived form, and flow hands the raw ones to dispatch.

Both dispatch paths pass the nominal battery.config.capacity_kwh as the capacity against which the grid-charge target is computed:
- simulate_timestep -> strategy.decide_action(battery_capacity_kwh=...) at flow.py:270;
- simulate_timestep_tou -> compute_grid_charge_power_kw(capacity_kwh=...) at flow.py:394.

dispatch then sets target_kwh = target_soc_fraction * capacity_kwh (dispatch.py:179). Battery bounds SOC by effective_capacity_kwh = capacity_kwh * soh. The fraction therefore has three readings: GridChargeConfig's docstring says 'fraction of usable capacity', dispatch uses nominal total, and Battery uses effective.

Probe: target 0.5 grid-charges a new battery to 0.500 of effective capacity, but a SOH-0.7 battery to 0.714. This path is live. finance.project_multi_year ages every battery through dataclasses.replace(battery_config, soh=...) (finance.py:1409-1422), so the multi-year projections of grid-charging fleets over-charge aged batteries from the grid.
findings.proposal: Have the Battery answer the question dispatch needs: a target SOC in kWh for a fraction (on the capacity basis GridChargeConfig documents), or a GridChargeContext built from Battery and tariff that already carries target_soc_kwh and the charge limits. flow then passes the Battery's answers and stops reading battery.config. Add a test for grid charging at soh 0.7.
findings.next_change: Any change to grid charging, SOH or a new dispatch strategy will pick one of three capacities. The agent must read battery.py, dispatch.py, flow.py and config.GridChargeConfig to see which one is meant. No test covers grid charging on a battery with soh < 1, so a wrong choice passes.

findings.statement:
project_multi_year computes the capacity-at-events grid-services figure through a closure memo. The memo (_event_gs_memo, finance.py:1554) is filled by whichever _simulate_age call runs first, and only call order makes that the age-0 run (seeds dict built from age 0 first, finance.py:1644).

The figure is fetched with a function-local `from solar_challenge.gridservices import compute_grid_services_at_events` (finance.py:1606). import_graph marks that import closes_cycle=true, closing the hidden cycle config -> finance -> gridservices.

Two tests (test_grid_services_events.py:261 and :359) verify compute-once by monkeypatching gridservices.compute_grid_services_at_events. Their docstring states that they depend on the lazy import re-resolving the attribute. They therefore pin the cycle-closing import's placement: hoisting it to module level, which is the layering fix, turns the count to 0 and fails them.

Callers cannot hand in what they already have. With --project and --cost-recovery, cli/finance.py::run simulates the fleet itself (line 183) and computes the same figure itself (line 191). It then calls project_multi_year (line 251) and solve_cost_recovery_rate (line 259). The latter calls project_multi_year again (finance.py:2294) and simulates age 0 once more (finance.py:2355).
findings.proposal: Make the figure an explicit input. Either project_multi_year takes an optional precomputed GridServicesAtEvents (or annual figure) and the age-0 FleetResults, or it simulates age 0 once up front, computes the figure from it, and passes it to every _simulate_age. The memo disappears, and the compute-once tests assert through an injected `simulate` or a returned field rather than a module patch. That frees finance.py:1606 to move once ConfigurationError lives below config.
findings.next_change: An agent untangling the config/finance/gridservices cycle, or reusing CLI-side results to cut simulation time, must find the closure memo and the two tests that depend on the import's placement. A layering fix that hoists the import fails 2 tests for a reason unrelated to behaviour.

findings.statement:
The run database has no single owner. Every interaction that writes it re-derives the store from ambient Flask config strings.

- **The singleton.** create_app builds one RunStorage(db_path, data_dir) from app.config and registers it as app.extensions['storage'] (app.py:122-123). shared.get_storage() serves it to 12 call sites.
- **The JobManager bypasses it.** It is constructed with no store (app.py:126). Each submit_* is handed db_path and data_dir as strings, which each of the 6 submit sites (api.py:83, 126, 404, 586; assistant.py:618, 684) first reads out of current_app.config. Nine JobManager methods then thread db_path. Each job opens its own connection (jobs.py:598 sqlite3.connect, get_db x3) and builds a fresh RunStorage per run (jobs.py:656, 723).
- **A third copy.** assistant.py:732 builds another RunStorage from config strings.

In all, current_app.config['DATABASE'|'DATA_DIR'] is read 17 times in api.py and assistant.py, and get_db is opened directly from a path in api, assistant, jobs, presets and routes. A JobManager can therefore be pointed at a different database per call than the storage its app serves.
findings.proposal: Construct the JobManager with its RunStorage (the app's singleton) and have jobs write through it, so submit_* drops db_path and data_dir. Route the presets, history and assistant reads through RunStorage, or one connection provider it owns, and keep app.config reads in create_app only.
findings.next_change: A schema change, a connection-policy change (the server seat's WAL and foreign_keys seam), or moving storage behind another backend has to find 11 direct connection sites and 4 RunStorage constructions. A missed one keeps writing through the old path, and only tests that happen to cross that path catch it.

findings.statement:
finance.py (2,376 lines, past the 2,000-line alarm) has a private layer that other modules use as an interface.

- **src:** optimize.py imports finance._resolve_homes (optimize.py:35, 890). It is the only src import of a private name across modules in the package.
- **tests:** 5 test files import 7 more finance privates. 3 are finance mathematics: _npv, _irr_bisection and _annuity_payment (test_finance_economics). 4 are billing/annualisation domain records: _cbs_own_use_kwh, _annualise_physics, _seg_export_income_gbp and _reconcile_seg_homes (test_cost_recovery_calibration, test_finance_bill, test_finance_projection_revenue, test_finance_projection_scenario_seg). They hold 61 references to state expectations.

The tests state expected values in terms of these internals because no public seam exposes them. One example: basis-C own-use, the figure every bill and the projection read, is reachable only as a private function. Any rename, signature change or partition of finance.py (the h14 measurement would want one) breaks those test modules, and a satellite holding these helpers would be reached by tests and optimize at private names.
findings.proposal: Give the two private clusters public homes: a finance-maths module with npv, irr and annuity_payment, and public billing-energy records (basis-C own-use, annualised physics, SEG export income) that bills and projections read. Move ScenarioConfig home resolution to config (see stateless.10). Then repoint the tests at those public names or at the public bill and projection seams.
findings.next_change: Partitioning finance.py, or changing how own-use or annualisation is computed, means editing 5 test modules and optimize at private names. The tests check the helper, not the bill or projection that uses it, so a behaviour change in how a public function combines them can slip through.

findings.statement:
create_app builds JobManager() with the real simulate_home and keeps it only in app.extensions['job_manager'] (app.py:126-127). Neither a manager nor a simulator can be passed in, and nothing returns the manager to the caller.

- **Tests write the attribute.** They replace the manager by writing into app.extensions 10 times in 7 files: e2e/conftest.py:157 and :161 swap it mid-session and back, plus test_tool_use x3, test_simulate_sweep, web_api/conftest, test_web_jobs, test_web_jobs_drain_scope and test_cli_web. This works only because every handler re-reads shared.get_job_manager() from current_app on each request.
- **The CLI uses a global registry.** cli/web.py::start holds flask_app but cannot reach its manager. It shuts down every manager in the process through the module-global WeakSet registry (jobs.py:48, shutdown_all_managers).
- **The test harness reaches the same registry.** tests/conftest.py::_shutdown_job_managers reads it through sys.modules.

findings.statement:
BatteryConfig's annotations name DispatchStrategyConfig and GridChargeConfig, which battery.py imports only under TYPE_CHECKING (battery.py:11-12) because config.py imports battery.py. The class's own type hints therefore do not resolve in its own module.

web/storage.py::_field_types, which rebuilds stored runs, works around this by reaching into two other modules' namespaces: `{**vars(solar_challenge.config), **vars(sys.modules[cls.__module__])}` (storage.py:120). Its docstring explains the battery/config import order.

Probe: of the 14 dataclasses reachable from the stored types (HomeConfig, SummaryStatistics, FleetSummary), exactly 1, BatteryConfig, raises NameError from get_type_hints without config's namespace. So the web persistence layer encodes a core-layer cycle. A stored dataclass that names a TYPE_CHECKING-only type from any module other than config would load with NameError.
findings.proposal: Define DispatchStrategyConfig and GridChargeConfig below battery, in dispatch.py or a leaf module, with ConfigurationError moved to a leaf errors module so they can still raise it. config.py then imports them and BatteryConfig's hints resolve in battery.py. _field_types drops the config namespace and uses get_type_hints(cls) alone.
findings.next_change: Adding a field to a stored config, or moving a type between core modules, can break loading of stored runs at runtime, not at type-check time. The agent has to know that storage resolves names by merging config's namespace.

--quiet travels by mutating a module-global Rich Console. cli/main.py's callback calls set_status_quiet(quiet) (main.py:65), which sets cli/utils.status_console.quiet (utils.py:268). findings.statement: There is no shared definition of a valid physical quantity. Each class spells its own comparison, in three incompatible polarities. (a) NaN-permissive: `if x < 0` / `if x <= 0`. dispatch.py has 21 such guards: DispatchDecision.__post_init__ x3, the same five-check input block copied into each of the three decide_action methods x15, compute_grid_charge_power_kw, PeakShavingStrategy.__init__. heat_pump.py::HeatPumpConfig has 2 and ev.py::EVConfig has 1. (b) NaN-refusing but inf-accepting: `not x >= 0` in flow.py::EnergyFlowResult.__post_init__ and battery.py::_require_valid_request. (c) Fully finite: `not 0 < x < math.inf` in battery.py::BatteryConfig and require_valid_power_limit, and in load.py::LoadConfig. flow.py::simulate_timestep and simulate_timestep_tou check none of their own inputs (generation_kw, demand_kw, timestep_minutes). Whether a bad value is refused depends on which path runs, whether a battery is present, and which downstream object happens to look. docs/domain-library-consumption.md needs one paragraph per fix (590, 633) just to enumerate which path now refuses what. Probed at the pin, all of these are accepted: HeatPumpConfig('ASHP', nan, nan); EVConfig('7kW', 18, required_charge_kwh=nan); DispatchDecision(nan, 0.0); PeakShavingStrategy(nan) (task 673). simulate_timestep(inf, 1.0, None) returns generation=inf and grid_export=inf (tasks 659, 672). The only reusable finite-number helper, web/number_fields.py::as_finite_float, lives in the web layer, above the domain that needs it.
findings.proposal: Add a dependency-free domain module src/solar_challenge/quantities.py with three checkers: require_finite_at_least(name, value, low, *, inclusive), require_fraction(name, value, *, open_low, open_high) and require_positive_finite(name, value). Each raises ValueError naming the quantity, its value and the bound, which satisfies INV-2. Every __post_init__ in battery/dispatch/flow/heat_pump/ev/load calls them. That rewrites the 21 dispatch guards, HeatPumpConfig, EVConfig, and EnergyFlowResult (which also refuses inf). battery.require_valid_power_limit and require_valid_capacity_setting stay public, as one-line delegations because of the frozen surface. Give flow.simulate_timestep and simulate_timestep_tou one shared entry check, _require_timestep_inputs(generation_kw, demand_kw, timestep_minutes), so behaviour no longer depends on the path. The five-check block copied into each decide_action collapses into one dispatch-module helper the three strategies call. They keep it because consumers call strategies directly. web/number_fields.as_finite_float delegates to quantities.py. Add a unit test that AST-scans src/solar_challenge for `raise ValueError` guarded by a bare `<`/`<=` comparison against a literal and fails, naming the site, so the polarity cannot regress. This removes the bug class of tasks 378, 590, 633, 659, 672 and 673 and the unfiled HeatPumpConfig/EVConfig NaN acceptance.
