findings.statement: The battery has five capacity concepts and no single value owns them. (1) BatteryConfig.capacity_kwh is nominal. (2) BatteryConfig.nominal_usable_capacity_kwh uses the config's SOC fractions, not a Battery's overridden ones. (3) SOH is resolved only inside Battery.__init__: the override wins, otherwise compute_soh with throughput fixed at 0.0. finance.py::_aged_homes runs compute_soh separately and injects the result as config.soh. (4) Battery.effective_capacity_kwh, min_soc_kwh and max_soc_kwh exist only on the mutable, stateful Battery. (5) The grid-charge target is measured against nominal capacity. flow.py::simulate_timestep passes battery.config.capacity_kwh as decide_action's battery_capacity_kwh, documented as 'Total battery capacity', and simulate_timestep_tou passes it as compute_grid_charge_power_kw's capacity_kwh. compute_grid_charge_power_kw then computes target_kwh = target_soc_fraction x nominal, while Battery clamps the SOC at a fraction of SoH-derated capacity. Probe: BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=10, soh=0.6) has max_soc_kwh=5.4, while the default 0.9 target asks for 9 kWh, so the controller never sees the gap close (task 632). Any reader that needs the derated limits must construct a throwaway Battery: web/charts.py::battery_soc_chart (the task 645 fix) and gridservices.py::compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw (Battery(battery_config).min_soc_kwh). A reader that does not know this uses nominal figures, as the chart did before 645.
findings.proposal: Add a frozen value battery.py::SocEnvelope(effective_capacity_kwh, min_soc_kwh, max_soc_kwh). One pure function builds it: BatteryConfig.soc_envelope(*, min_soc_fraction=None, max_soc_fraction=None), which also does the single SOH resolution (override or compute_soh), moved out of Battery.__init__. Battery holds the envelope, recomputes it when an SOC-fraction setter fires, and derives min/max_soc_kwh, usable_capacity_kwh and available_* from it. charts.battery_soc_chart and gridservices.compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw call config.soc_envelope() and stop instantiating Battery. Flow passes envelope-derived capacity to strategies and the grid-charge controller. compute_grid_charge_power_kw clamps target_kwh to the envelope's max_soc_kwh. Signatures stay frozen; only the documented meaning of battery_capacity_kwh changes, under the release note. Record the rule 'every capacity a dispatcher sees is SoH-derated' as one invariant in battery.py, and pin it with a test that runs a derated battery through both flow paths. This closes 632 and the class of 645, and stops the next consumer from picking the wrong capacity.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — battery.py Battery.__init__ still resolves SOH via compute_soh(..., 0.0, ...); effective/min/max_soc_kwh only on Battery; flow.py:270 and :394 still pass battery.config.capacity_kwh to decide_action and compute_grid_charge_power_kw; dispatch.py:179 target_kwh = target_soc_fraction * capacity_kwh.

findings.statement: This finding takes the briefing's key decision to keep two dispatch behaviours as given. The mechanism, not the behaviour, is what is duplicated. DispatchStrategy.decide_action returns one decision computed from the pre-step SOC. The rate-aware path needs PV charging to land first and the grid top-up to be sized from the post-PV SOC. That sequencing does not fit the interface, so flow.py::simulate_timestep_tou decides and executes inline with interleaved battery.charge calls. It then repeats the same 27-line settle tail as simulate_timestep: battery_charge sum, direct and self-consumption, split-source export/import, EnergyFlowResult construction, and an identical 7-line comment (task 270). As a result the 'shared' grid-charge controller is fed different inputs on the two paths. simulate_timestep_tou passes post-PV-charge SOC and pv_charge_power_kw = min(excess, max_charge_kw). The strategy path, via TOUOptimizedStrategy/PeakShavingStrategy.decide_action, passes pre-step SOC and an unclamped charge_kw. So with excess PV in a cheap period, the strategy path sizes the grid draw as if no PV were stored and overshoots the target, while the TOU path does not. The two strategies also each carry a copy of the 15-line grid-charge gate block. EnergyFlowResult accepts caller-computed derived flows, so energy balance is checked after the fact by validate_energy_balance, which callers can switch off and which reads six of eight flows. It is never true by construction.
findings.proposal: Add one pure settle function in flow.py, _settle(generation_kwh, demand_kwh, pv_stored_kwh, grid_stored_kwh, discharged_kwh, soc_kwh) -> EnergyFlowResult, as the only producer of derived flows. Both paths call it, the duplicated tail and its comment are deleted (task 270), and the result balances by construction; validate_energy_balance stays as a redundant check. Then add one executor, _execute(decision, battery, minutes) -> (pv_stored, grid_stored, discharged). Express the rate-aware path as a two-phase decision (PV phase, then grid phase sized from the post-PV SOC) through the same executor, keeping its behaviour. Have the strategy path size grid charge from the SOC after PV in the same way, so compute_grid_charge_power_kw sees the same SOC basis on both paths. Move the copied grid-charge gate in TOUOptimizedStrategy and PeakShavingStrategy into one module helper, _grid_charge_kw(ctx, soc, capacity, charge_kw, discharge_kw, minutes). A dispatch change is then made once.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — flow.py:319-438 still decides inline with interleaved battery.charge calls and passes post-PV SOC and min(excess,max_charge_kw); strategies pass pre-step SOC and unclamped charge_kw; the identical 15-line grid-charge gate is still in TOUOptimizedStrategy and PeakShavingStrategy.

findings.statement: Which dispatcher a home runs is decided by two string fields with different vocabularies. HomeConfig.dispatch_strategy: str ('greedy' or 'tou_optimized') has no __post_init__, so HomeConfig(dispatch_strategy='peak_shaving') or any typo silently runs self-consumption. BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy is a DispatchStrategyConfig whose strategy_type: str is checked against a local tuple. The vocabularies are restated in config.py::_VALID_DISPATCH_STRATEGIES, the tuple in DispatchStrategyConfig.__post_init__, the if/elif in home.py::_create_dispatch_strategy (which re-checks peak_hours and import_limit_kw, already refused by the config because DispatchStrategyConfig is a mutable @dataclass), and the strategies' name properties. The precedence rule (tariff TOU only when the battery has no strategy, and only with a tariff) lives in simulate_home's use_tariff_tou. It is restated as a warning in config.py::_read_fleet_distribution_file and had to be documented side by side in 5e0f953. 'tou_optimized' names two different mechanisms, and simulate_home hard-codes strategy_name='tou_optimized' for the tariff path, so results cannot say which one ran. import_limit_kw's positivity is checked twice, both times NaN-permissive (task 673).
findings.proposal: Replace the routing with one resolver in home.py (or dispatch.py), resolve_dispatch(home_config) -> DispatchPlan. DispatchPlan is a frozen sum type: either StrategyDispatch(strategy) or TariffTouDispatch(tariff), each with a distinct result name such as 'tou_optimized' and 'tou_rate_aware'. It is the only place the precedence and the no-tariff fallback are decided. config.py's warning calls it instead of restating the rule. Give HomeConfig a __post_init__ that validates dispatch_strategy against the single vocabulary, moved out of config.py's _VALID_DISPATCH_STRATEGIES. Freeze DispatchStrategyConfig and give it a to_strategy() method, so _create_dispatch_strategy's if/elif and its re-checks are deleted. Widening the fields to Enums is the follow-up that needs the frozen-surface version bump. This stops the class seen in 340/519/335 where each reader re-learns how the two keys relate.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — home.py HomeConfig.dispatch_strategy: str = 'greedy' with no __post_init__; _create_dispatch_strategy if/elif re-checks peak_hours/import_limit_kw; simulate_home use_tariff_tou predicate and hard-coded strategy_name='tou_optimized' unchanged.

findings.statement: Battery.charge clamps each call's power to config.max_charge_kw. flow.py::simulate_timestep executes a decision with two calls: battery.charge(decision.charge_kw, ...) and then battery.charge(decision.grid_charge_kw, ...). DispatchDecision.__post_init__ does not bound charge_kw + grid_charge_kw. The built-in strategies keep the sum under the limit only through compute_grid_charge_power_kw's residual arithmetic. DispatchStrategy is a frozen extension point that consumers implement. Probe at the pin: with a strategy returning DispatchDecision(charge_kw=5, discharge_kw=0, grid_charge_kw=5) against BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=10, max_charge_kw=2.5), one 60-minute step stores 4.875 kWh, which is twice the hardware limit times efficiency. The per-step power invariant belongs to the battery but is enforced by caller arithmetic.
findings.proposal: Make the battery own the per-step limit. Add Battery.charge_split(pv_kw, grid_kw, duration_minutes) -> (pv_stored_kwh, grid_stored_kwh), which clamps pv_kw + grid_kw to max_charge_kw once, giving PV priority. simulate_timestep and simulate_timestep_tou use it. Alternatively, flow clamps grid_charge_kw to max(0, max_charge_kw - min(charge_kw, max_charge_kw)) before the second call. Add a test with a consumer strategy over the limit.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — battery.py Battery.charge clamps per call to config.max_charge_kw; flow.py:276-283 still makes two charge calls (charge_kw, grid_charge_kw); DispatchDecision.__post_init__ bounds neither the sum nor discharge vs shortfall.

findings.statement: home.py::simulate_home (about 180 lines) does nine jobs: weather fetch and year-length check, PV simulation and expansion, base and EV load (delegated), heat-pump temperature alignment and load composition (inline), battery construction, dispatch routing, the timestep loop, tariff and SEG pricing, and results assembly. The 'additional household load' axis has two mechanisms. EV load is folded in inside load.generate_load_profile through a function-local import and a fill_value union. Heat-pump load is folded in inside simulate_home, with its own UTC TMY alignment and an annual-year check. That check is spelled twice: _YEAR_LENGTHS_IN_HOURS in home.py and _YEAR_LENGTHS_IN_MINUTES in heat_pump.py, both from reference_year_lengths, which lives in heat_pump.py although it describes the TMY. Every fix at this seam (166 UTC alignment, 168 series naming, 190 leap day, 206 annual-demand sharing) had to be made inside simulate_home, and 276 had to repeat 168's naming fix inside heat_pump.py. A new load component (e.g. a second EV, storage heating) has no obvious home.
findings.proposal: Create src/solar_challenge/demand.py with household_demand(config, weather_year, index) -> HouseholdDemand. HouseholdDemand is a frozen value with base_kw, ev_kw, heat_pump_kw and total_kw, all on the one timebase.minute_index from the EV finding, with each component's series name fixed there. It owns TMY-to-index alignment for temperature and the reference-year check, and reference_year_lengths moves to weather.py beside align_tmy_to_index. simulate_home shrinks to weather, PV, demand, dispatch loop and pricing, with pricing extracted as _price_results(results_list, index, tariff, seg). generate_load_profile keeps its frozen ev_config parameter as a delegation to the same composition.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — home.py:292-472 simulate_home unchanged (~180 lines, nine jobs); _YEAR_LENGTHS_IN_HOURS in home.py:30 and _YEAR_LENGTHS_IN_MINUTES in heat_pump.py:29 from reference_year_lengths in heat_pump.py; EV still folded in via load.py:447 function-local import.

findings.statement: load.py::_try_richardsonpy_profile (about 170 lines) does all of the following: resolves richardsonpy's data-file paths, seeds global RNGs, normalises dates, builds occupancy, loops over days, trims or pads for DST (a copy of _generate_elexon_profile's block), and scales to the seasonal target. All of it sits inside `except Exception` that logs and returns None, so a defect in the project's own code (e.g. a ValueError in the scaling) silently switches the model to the deterministic Elexon shape. The only seam is the module-private _simulate_stochastic_day. tests/unit/test_load.py::TestWindowedStochasticGeneration reaches it with monkeypatch.setattr(load_module, '_simulate_stochastic_day', ...) to exercise the fallback. Its window-count tests patch richardsonpy's own run_application_simulation to count calls, which pins third-party internals, not behaviour.
findings.proposal: Extract a narrow adapter, a RichardsonpyDaySource class with one method day_kw(date, occupants) -> ndarray, built once per profile. _try_richardsonpy_profile becomes a short loop over minute_index days that calls the adapter and then a shared _scale_to_seasonal_target. Narrow the except to wrap only the adapter calls, so the project's own errors propagate. Tests inject a fake day source through a keyword-only parameter of a module-level helper the public path calls, which removes both monkeypatches.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — load.py:228-399 still one try block covering richardsonpy imports, seeding, windowing, DST trim/pad copy and scaling, ending in `except Exception` returning None.

findings.statement: PVConfig.module_efficiency is validated in __post_init__ but is read nowhere in pv.py; the only module-building function that accepts an efficiency, create_simple_module_params, is not fed from PVConfig. _module_parameters applies temperature_coefficient only through the sentinel test `config.temperature_coefficient != -0.004`, and writes it to gamma_pdc on a CEC catalogue module, where pvlib's single-diode model reads gamma_r (live task 195). When custom_module_params is set, temperature_coefficient and module_efficiency are dropped silently. Yet both fields are parsed from YAML, sampled as fleet distributions (config.py::generate_homes_from_distribution samples module_efficiency per home), written back by scenario_writer, and offered as sweep or distribution axes. Users can therefore vary module efficiency across a fleet and get identical output. This is the same shape as the task 236 defect, a default value doubling as 'keep the catalogue value', and no check ties a PVConfig field to the path that consumes it. Because each parameter is checked at construction but never at use, the next unread field will not be caught either.
findings.proposal: Make the module choice one typed value resolved at construction. Introduce a frozen module spec in pv.py (catalogue module / PVWatts module with rating_w and gamma_pdc / custom parameters) and have PVConfig carry that instead of the loose module_efficiency, temperature_coefficient and custom_module_params trio. Enforce applicability in one place, PVConfig.__post_init__ and the module resolver: a field the chosen path ignores must be absent or refused, with an error naming the field and the path. Either wire the CEC path properly (gamma_r and efficiency into the single-diode parameters, with a measurement as for 203/236) or remove the two fields from the scenario grammar and distributions. This deletes the `!= -0.004` sentinel, the dead module_efficiency distribution plumbing, and the 'ignored when custom' footgun, and would have prevented tasks 195 and 236 and the 196 chain mismatch.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py:480-487 still applies temperature_coefficient only when != -0.004 and writes gamma_pdc on the CEC dict; module_efficiency is still read nowhere in pv.py; custom_module_params still drops both silently.

findings.statement: System losses are a step inside the pvlib ModelChain (_deduct_system_losses, DC side), while ageing and the non-negative clip are applied after the chain, on AC, by simulate_pv_output (apply_degradation(ac_power, ...)). The public create_model_chain therefore returns a chain that does not age, and simulate_pv_output returns something the chain cannot produce. Two entry points disagree about what 'the PV model' is, and the measurement scripts use both (create_model_chain at scripts/measure_pv_performance_ratio.py:110, simulate_pv_output at :126). Ageing on AC after the inverter clips is the wrong place (live task 284, documented in docs/pv-system-losses.md §7), and apply_degradation has no other caller once that is fixed (live task 609). finance.py computes its own pv_soh from calculate_degradation_factor in parallel. The derating policy has no single home.
findings.proposal: Make the model chain the single owner of DC derating. Fold the degradation factor into the losses step as kept_fraction = (1 - system_losses) * calculate_degradation_factor(config.system_age_years, config.degradation_rate_per_year), computed in one named function that both the chain and finance's SOH display call. simulate_pv_output shrinks to run, convert W to kW and clip. Then delete apply_degradation (609) and the after-the-fact multiply (284), and give every consumer of create_model_chain the same physics. Task 284 and 609 are symptoms; this is the structure that produced them.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py:727-769 still applies apply_degradation on AC after the chain while system losses are the chain's losses_model step; create_model_chain returns an un-aged chain; scripts/measure_pv_performance_ratio.py still uses both entry points.

findings.statement: After tasks 239 and 324, validation's annual-yield and peak checks divide by wired_dc_capacity_kw(config). That function calls _module_parameters and _module_count itself rather than reading what _pv_system built, so the wired DC and the actual PVSystem agree only because two call sites run the same helpers; nothing stops a new input to the sizing from reaching one and not the other. The fix stopped at two checks: validate_simulation still passes pv_config.capacity_kw (nameplate) to validate_self_consumption_pv_only and validate_self_consumption_with_battery, which use a hard-coded `capacity_kw * 900` 'rough UK yield' in their exception messages. That figure belongs to neither the 300-1200 band nor the measured ~1000 kWh/kWp. cli/validate.py `results --pv-kw` rebuilds a default PVConfig from a number to guess the wired DC of a CSV. finance.py::compute_project_economics prices capex on nameplate capacity_kw. The same quantity (the PV array's size) thus has three definitions, the same drift class as tasks 239 and 324.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen PVDesign in pv.py (module parameters, module count, wiring, inverter) built once by design_pv(config, candidates). _pv_system(design) builds the PVSystem from it, and design.dc_kw is the one wired DC. wired_dc_capacity_kw becomes design_pv(config).dc_kw, and validate_* take the design's dc_kw (or the PVConfig and call it once) in every check. Move the 900 kWh/kWp figure and the 10% peak margin into named constants beside the yield band in validation.py, or delete the exception-message heuristics. State once, in PVDesign, which size finance prices on. This removes the two-helper coincidence and the nameplate-versus-wired split, and would have prevented 239 and 324.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py:601-613 still recomputes _module_parameters/_module_count instead of reading the built PVSystem; validation.py:389 and :461 still use capacity_kw * 900; validate_simulation still passes pv_config.capacity_kw to both self-consumption checks.

findings.statement: get_tmy_data(location, use_cache) fetches its cache from the process-global _weather_cache through get_weather_cache()/set_weather_cache(). The cache is therefore an implicit input, a temporal coupling on a prior set_weather_cache call, and it does not cross a process boundary under spawn or forkserver. Task 460 (workers ignored the injected cache, read .cache/weather and fetched PVGIS) is the symptom, and it reproduces only on the interpreter-matrix lane. The fix compensates in a different module: fleet._tmy_by_location fetches one TMY per location in the parent and passes it down as weather_data, and simulate_fleet_iter's docstring explains why workers must not read the cache. Scripts, tests/conftest.py and measure_mppt_window.py mutate the global to inject a cache. Any new process-spawning caller can reintroduce the bug.
findings.proposal: Make the cache an explicit argument: get_tmy_data(location, *, cache: WeatherCache | None = None), with the process default resolved only at the top-level entry points (CLI, web, public facade). Keep get_weather_cache/set_weather_cache exported, because they are in the frozen API, but have them only supply the default. Tests and scripts then pass a cache instead of mutating the global. The parent-side pre-fetch in fleet stays as an optimisation but stops being a correctness requirement. A test that runs a fleet under each start method with a seeded cache pins it.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — weather.py:259-274 process-global _weather_cache with get/set_weather_cache; get_tmy_data still reads it; scripts measure_mppt_window/measure_pv_performance_ratio main() still call set_weather_cache; fleet._tmy_by_location compensation unchanged.

findings.statement: An entry is a CSV plus a JSON sidecar. Round-trip fidelity relies on str(index.tz) being a name pandas can resolve (put refuses zones whose str names none, via _require_timezone_name) and on freqstr round-tripping through asfreq. The sidecar is written with prefix, latitude, longitude, start_date and end_date, none of which get reads; get reads only timezone and freq. If the CSV exists but the sidecar is missing, get silently returns a frame parsed by parse_dates=True with no timezone, a different type from a normal hit. The put docstring concedes that two os.replace calls are atomic only 'while every put under one key stores the same timezone and frequency'. Task 464's two fixes (UTC-then-convert, round_trip floats) and the amend added _require_timezone_name are each a patch for a place where text stood in for a typed index. The cache has also moved key versions (task 285).
findings.proposal: Store one self-describing file per entry so the single os.replace covers the whole entry and the sidecar disappears: for example a format that records the index as UTC instants plus the timezone name in the same file (parquet would do this directly, but pyarrow is only in the web extra, so check before choosing). Parse into a frozen CachedFrameMeta (timezone, freq) at the boundary; get then returns either a typed frame or a miss, never a degraded frame. Drop the unread metadata keys, and with them _require_timezone_name's round-trip gate if the format stores the zone key rather than its str.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — weather.py WeatherCache.put still writes prefix/latitude/longitude/start_date/end_date that get never reads; get returns a parse_dates frame with no tz when the sidecar is missing; put docstring caveat on two os.replace calls unchanged.

findings.statement: _module_rating_w returns module_params.get('STC', 400.0). create_simple_module_params writes both pdc0 and STC, so the library helper is consistent. But custom_module_params of the form {'pdc0': 300, 'gamma_pdc': -0.004}, which _inverter_and_wiring accepts as PVWatts parameters (via _PVWATTS_MODULE_KEYS), have no STC. The module count is then round(capacity_kw*1000/400) while pvlib's PVWatts DC model scales each module by pdc0 = 300 W. The modelled DC and wired_dc_capacity_kw's count*400 W disagree, and a 4 kW config models 3 kW of modules while validation reads 4 kW. No error is raised. (Computed from the code; not run, since pvlib is not installed in the review environment.)
findings.proposal: Resolve the rating from the parameter set that the DC model actually reads: pdc0 when the PVWatts keys are present, STC otherwise, and raise (naming the missing key) when neither exists, instead of defaulting to 400. Put it in the module-spec resolver of finding 1, so that count, wired DC and the chain all see the same number.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py:543-545 still returns module_params.get('STC', 400.0); _PVWATTS_MODULE_KEYS path still accepts pdc0/gamma_pdc dicts without STC.

findings.statement: Location.__post_init__ checks `self.altitude < -500`, which is False for NaN, so altitude=nan passes (and inf passes by design); the same sequence of range checks is not written to refuse non-finite values the way PVConfig's was after task 332. timezone is any string: a typo such as 'Europe/Londn' is accepted at construction and fails only inside PVLibLocation in create_model_chain_picking_from, or later in the load profile's tz handling, far from the config that caused it. Locations are the cache key input for fleet._tmy_by_location and WeatherCache._make_key. This is the 'checked in some constructors and not others' pattern PVConfig had.
findings.proposal: In Location.__post_init__, require math.isfinite on altitude and validate the timezone with zoneinfo.ZoneInfo (error naming the field and value), so that the construction and use points both agree. A unit test over (nan, inf, -inf) for every float field closes the class.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — location.py:64-70 still `if self.altitude < -500` (NaN passes); timezone is an unchecked str.

findings.statement: Battery charge losses vanish from the energy accounts on both charge paths, and the per-timestep balance validator cannot see it. Battery.charge returns the energy STORED after charge_efficiency (battery.py:430-463), and both simulate_timestep (flow.py:276-283, 303-304) and simulate_timestep_tou (flow.py:383-399, 425-426) then set grid_export = excess - pv_charge_stored and grid_import = shortfall - discharge + grid_charge_stored. So (a) on the PV path the charge loss is reported as grid export: measured on the pinned tree, 1.000 kWh of excess PV taken by a 10 kWh battery gives battery_charge 0.9750, SOC rise 0.9750 and grid_export 0.0250 kWh; (b) on the TOU arbitrage path the grid draw is recorded on the stored basis: one off-peak hour of grid charging at 2.5 kW records grid_import 2.4375 kWh, not 2.5. validate_energy_balance (flow.py:441-494) closes on stored energy with no loss term, so it passes both. Downstream along the critical path: home.py:428-433 prices grid_charge and import_cost on the stored basis; the phantom export earns SEG in export_revenue (home.py:441-445), which finance reads as CBS SEG income (_seg_export_income_gbp via export_rev_physics, finance.py:650-700); and Basis-C own-use = demand - import (_cbs_own_use_kwh, finance.py:703-748) is overstated by every grid-charge loss, so the CBS bills own-use for energy that never existed. All three biases favour the board case. The defect is known but untracked: docs/prds/tou-grid-charging-battery-arbitrage.md:40 calls it phantom export 'pre-existing and preserved (out of scope, section 10)', and docs/prds/flexibility-value-finance-integration.md:131 estimates the bill-level time-shift ~8% optimistic. It is not among the briefing's known_gaps and no task tracks it. [Also observed by sim-physics:] Battery charge losses never reach the grid accounting. Battery.charge returns the energy STORED after charge_efficiency (battery.py:450-463), and both dispatch paths settle grid_export = max(0, excess - pv_charge_stored) and grid_import = ... + grid_charge_stored (flow.py:303-304 and 425-426), so the PV energy that the charger drew but lost is reported as export and the grid energy lost while grid-charging is never imported (home.py:429-433 then prices import cost and grid_charge_cost on stored energy). Verified: 2 kWh of excess PV into a battery with round-trip efficiency 0.81 (eta_c 0.9) stores 1.8 kWh and exports 0.2 kWh that physically went into the charger; a TOU grid charge that raises SOC by 4.0 kWh at eta_c 0.9 imports 4.0 kWh, not 4.44. On a full 2024 Bristol run (4 kWp, BatteryConfig.default_5kwh, 3,400 kWh) the phantom export is 25.8 kWh (1.6% of the 1,610.3 kWh exported, all valued at SEG), and the AC-side round trip seen by the accounts is eta_d alone. validate_energy_balance cannot catch it because its storage term is stored-minus-delivered with no loss term. docs/prds/tou-grid-charging-battery-arbitrage.md §3.1 names it ('charge-efficiency loss already surfaces as phantom export in the PV path') and §10 puts fixing it out of scope; it is not in the briefing's key_decisions or known_gaps, and the identical 7-line NOTE at flow.py:298-302/420-424 defends the convention rather than pointing at that PRD.
findings.proposal: Account the charge loss at the bus: either Battery.charge reports the energy drawn alongside the energy stored, or flow computes the drawn energy as stored / charge_efficiency. Then export = excess - drawn_from_pv and import = shortfall - discharge + drawn_from_grid, and validate_energy_balance carries an explicit charge-loss term, so closure still holds and the loss is visible. This spans battery, flow, home and finance and changes EnergyFlowResult's meaning (a new loss field on a frozen __all__ class is a breaking change needing a version bump). The calibration scenario and docs/cost-recovery-finance-model.md must be re-run and re-verified under the board-model convention. At minimum, add it to the briefing's known_gaps with a tracking task now.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — flow.py:303-304 and 425-426 still settle grid_export = max(0, excess - pv_charge_stored) and grid_import = ... + grid_charge_stored on stored (post-efficiency) energy; validate_energy_balance has no loss term; the identical NOTE comment remains at both sites.

findings.statement: Both load paths lay each simulated day's 1,440 one-minute values positionally onto a tz-aware Europe/London minute index and trim or pad the surplus at the END of the window (load.py:345-362 for the default richardsonpy path, 492-519 for Elexon), so every day after a clock change inside the window is displaced by an hour against the local wall clock until the next change. Measured on the pinned tree: April 4 2024's Elexon profile peaks at 18:30 BST when the window starts 2024-03-25 but at 17:30 BST when it starts 2024-04-03 (same config, same day, up to 0.18 kW apart); with the stochastic path's per-day arrays tagged by day_of_year, April 4's own day begins at 01:00 BST and 00:00-00:59 carries April 3. For the canonical Jan 1-Dec 31 run every BST minute (31 Mar-27 Oct) is one hour late, while PV and heat-pump temperature are UTC-aligned (the briefing's task-166 decision exists precisely to stop an hour's PV/demand skew) and tariff periods are matched on the local clock: a 4 kWp / 3,400 kWh Elexon home's PV-direct self-consumption reads 1,377.0 kWh against 1,403.2 kWh with correct wall-clock placement (-1.87%), and its no-PV Economy 7 cost reads 754.89 vs 748.25 GBP. The window's end bound is end + Timedelta(days=1) - 1 min (load.py:351, 494), an absolute 24 h, so a window ending on 2024-03-31 runs to 2024-04-01 00:59 BST and one ending on 2024-10-27 stops at 22:59 GMT. ev.generate_ev_charging_profile repeats the pattern (n_days*1440 positional minutes from start, ev.py:186-308): EV charging starts at 19:00 BST instead of the configured 18:00 when the window spans the change, and a window spanning one spring-forward gets an EV index 60 minutes longer than the base load's, which base_load.add(ev_load, fill_value=0.0) (load.py:455) silently unions into a demand index that runs past end_date. The only DST test (tests/unit/test_load.py::TestWindowedStochasticGeneration::test_window_crossing_spring_dst_counts_calendar_days) counts richardsonpy calls and would pass on any placement; git 38c84ed already fixed one DST off-by-one in this function.
findings.proposal: Build each path's minute index per local calendar day (the day's own tz-aware date_range from local midnight to the next local midnight) and place that day's profile by local wall-clock slot, resampling the 1,440-value day onto the 1,380/1,500-minute DST days, instead of concatenating and trimming at the end; compute the window end as the next local midnight (normalize + DateOffset(days=1)), and give ev.py the same per-day placement so the EV series shares the base load's index exactly (then assert equal indexes instead of add(fill_value=0)). Pin it with a test that a calendar day's profile is identical whichever window contains it. Output numbers move for every run spanning a clock change (a release-note item), but no public signature changes; spans load.py and ev.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — load.py:349-362 and 492-519 still lay 1440-value days positionally on a tz-aware index ending end + 1 day - 1 min and trim/pad at the end; ev.py still positional; base_load.add(fill_value=0.0) unchanged.

findings.statement: PVConfig.module_efficiency ("Panel efficiency as fraction") and PVConfig.temperature_coefficient ("Power temp coefficient per degC") have no effect on simulated output on the default path. module_efficiency is read nowhere in pv.py; temperature_coefficient is written only as gamma_pdc onto the CEC module dict, and only when it differs from the literal sentinel -0.004 that duplicates the field default (pv.py:485-486), but pvlib infers the 'cec' single-diode DC model from that dict (verified: ModelChain.dc_model is calcparams/cec) and never reads gamma_pdc, so the module's temperature behaviour stays the catalogue row's. Measured on Bristol's scaled TMY for June: PVConfig(4 kW) default, temperature_coefficient=-0.009 and module_efficiency=0.10 all give exactly 497.7746611592203 kWh. Yet both are public members of a FROZEN_CLOSURE class, accepted from scenario YAML (config.py:709), sampled per home by fleet distributions (config.py:1706-1715 samples module_efficiency for every home), and written back by scenario_writer.py:135-136, so a fleet-diversity or sensitivity study on either axis silently returns flat results. Tests only check that the fields store values (tests/unit/test_pv.py:537-569); test_customised_system_leaves_later_default_systems_unchanged sets temperature_coefficient but asserts only that gamma_pdc does not leak.
findings.proposal: Choose one: (a) make the fields mean what they say on the CEC path (e.g. derive the single-diode temperature terms from temperature_coefficient, and document module_efficiency as area-only since capacity_kw fixes power), or (b) declare them as applying only to create_simple_module_params/PVWatts modules and refuse a non-default value on the CEC path with a ValueError naming the field, or (c) deprecate them. (b) tightens the PVConfig contract and (c) removes frozen-surface members: either is a breaking change needing a version bump; (a) changes outputs for configs that set them. Remove the -0.004 sentinel in every option.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py PVConfig.module_efficiency and temperature_coefficient fields unchanged; module_efficiency unread in pv.py; gamma_pdc sentinel write at pv.py:485-486.

findings.statement: BatteryConfig's dispatch_strategy and grid_charging fields are typed with classes from config.py, the YAML-parsing module at the top of the stack, imported under TYPE_CHECKING (battery.py:11-12) while config.py imports battery at runtime (config.py:20): a cycle hidden by TYPE_CHECKING, and home.py/flow.py read those config.py classes' attributes (home.py:272-287, flow.py:184-192), so the domain layer depends on the parser layer's types. DispatchStrategyConfig is a plain mutable @dataclass with a list field (config.py:355-366), breaking the convention that config and domain objects are frozen: hash(BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh=5, dispatch_strategy=...)) raises 'unhashable type: DispatchStrategyConfig' (verified), and after construction-time validation its import_limit_kw can be set to -5.0 inside a 'frozen' BatteryConfig, refused only later by PeakShavingStrategy with a ValueError instead of ConfigurationError. TOUOptimizedStrategy also keeps the caller's peak_hours list by reference (dispatch.py:375). [Same cost seen from src/solar_challenge/battery.py::BatteryConfig (h9 lens):] battery.py, a bottom-stratum module, names two types defined in the top parse module: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from solar_challenge.config import DispatchStrategyConfig, GridChargeConfig` (battery.py:11-12; BatteryConfig fields at :164-165). config.py imports battery at top (config.py:20), so the reference can only exist under TYPE_CHECKING. The inversion leaks into other modules. web/storage.py must `import solar_challenge.config` (storage.py:31) and merge config's namespace into every get_type_hints call to deserialize a stored BatteryConfig (storage.py:108-121, whose docstring states this reason). GridChargeConfig raises ConfigurationError (config.py:266-270) while its owner BatteryConfig raises ValueError. The consumers sit below config: flow._build_grid_charge_context reads battery.config.grid_charging (flow.py:183-196), and home._create_dispatch_strategy reads DispatchStrategyConfig (home.py:272-289). The same storage serializer also shapes a lower module: tariff.py:70-72 says TariffPeriod's parsed times are cached_property 'because web/storage.py's JSON round-trip walks fields()'. AST import graph: the only other upward edges are finance->config and gridservices->config, both lazy for ConfigurationError (separate finding).
findings.proposal: Define GridChargeConfig and a frozen DispatchStrategyConfig (tuple peak_hours) in the layer that consumes them (dispatch.py), with config.py parsing into them. Both are pinned in FROZEN_CLOSURE as config.DispatchStrategyConfig/config.GridChargeConfig, so moving them (or freezing DispatchStrategyConfig) is a breaking change needing a version bump; a re-export left in config.py would itself be a heuristic-13 shim. [From the src/solar_challenge/battery.py::BatteryConfig view:] Define GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig beside their consumer (battery.py or dispatch.py), have config.py import them downward, and drop storage.py's config-namespace merge. FROZEN_CLOSURE keys them as 'config.DispatchStrategyConfig' and 'config.GridChargeConfig' (tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py:255-256), so moving their defining module is a contract change needing a version bump, unless the closure test accepts the name still importable from config.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — battery.py:11-12 still imports DispatchStrategyConfig, GridChargeConfig from config under TYPE_CHECKING; config.py:20 imports battery at module level; config.py:355-356 DispatchStrategyConfig is still a plain @dataclass.

findings.statement: compute_soh halves the equivalent-full-cycle count it is fed. Its docstring defines cumulative_throughput_kwh as 'Total energy discharged over the battery's lifetime' and computes efc = throughput / (2 * usable_capacity_kwh) (battery.py:89-114); finance._throughput_at accumulates per_home_discharge, the annual battery_discharge_kwh (finance.py:1462-1468, 1587), as docs/cost-recovery-finance-model.md confirms ('the annualised discharge is the yearly throughput that battery cycle ageing integrates'). Dividing a discharge-only total by 2x usable is right only for charge-plus-discharge throughput (the PRD's 'throughput / 2*usable', docs/prds/financial-layer-battery-fidelity.md:342), so the effective cycle fade is half of cycle_fade_per_equivalent_full_cycle (whose own doc reads '5e-5/EFC ~ 30% fade over ~6,000 EFC'). For the Bristol default 5 kWh battery (4 kWh nominal usable, about 1,000 kWh discharged a year: 1,004.6 kWh stored in the measured 2024 run) the code counts ~122 EFC/yr instead of ~245: cycle fade 0.61%/yr vs 1.22%/yr, year-12 SOH 0.687 vs 0.613, and the 0.5 floor reached at ~19 years instead of ~15.5, so the 25-year projection's mid-life battery capacity and Basis-C own-use read high.
findings.proposal: Make the unit one fact: either define cumulative_throughput_kwh as discharged energy and compute efc = throughput / usable, or define it as charge+discharge and have finance pass both. compute_soh is in __all__ and its outputs move, so ship with a release note; spans battery.py and finance.py and the finance model doc.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — battery.py:77-117 compute_soh still computes efc = throughput / (2 * usable) with the docstring defining throughput as energy discharged; finance.py still imports compute_soh (line 1422) and its docstring (~1450) says throughput accrues at the annual discharge.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 (and INV-11, no silent fail-soft): simulate_community ignores, without a word, two configurations the community parser accepts. (1) _parse_community_config builds the community_battery with the full home-battery grammar (config.py:2775-2777, _BATTERY_BLOCK_KEYS 751-756), so a community_battery block holding dispatch_strategy {strategy_type: peak_shaving, import_limit_kw: 20} and grid_charging {target_soc_fraction: 0.9} parses (verified). simulate_community then always dispatches with SelfConsumptionStrategy through simulate_timestep, never simulate_timestep_tou (community.py:292-318). The briefing documents the hardcoding; what contradicts it is accepting configuration that asks for something else. (2) A billing block with a tariff but no SEG parses to CommunityBillingConfig(tariff=..., seg_rate_pence_per_kwh=None) (verified; config.py:2737-2739). simulate_community computes billing only when both are present (community.py:343-347), so the result, the CLI table (cli/fleet.py, 'only when VNM billing was computed') and the report all show no billing and no warning. No task covers either.
findings.proposal: Refuse, in CommunityConfig.__post_init__ or the community parser, a community_battery carrying dispatch_strategy or grid_charging, naming the keys and the self-consumption-only rule. Either refuse a billing block with only one of tariff/SEG, or price the import leg alone with export revenue 0. Contained in community.py and config.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — community.py:292-318 still Battery(cb_config) with SelfConsumptionStrategy() and simulate_timestep without tariff; billing still computed only when both tariff and seg_rate_pence_per_kwh are set (343-347), with no warning otherwise.

findings.statement: The execution contract between a DispatchStrategy (a frozen extension point that the platform implements, per the briefing) and flow.simulate_timestep lives nowhere: DispatchDecision checks only signs and charge/discharge exclusivity (dispatch.py:37-60), and flow executes charge_kw, grid_charge_kw and discharge_kw as separate Battery calls (flow.py:276-287), each clamped to max_charge_kw on its own. Verified with a minimal consumer strategy: charge_kw=2.5 plus grid_charge_kw=2.5 stores 5.0 kWh in one hour on a 2.5 kW battery; discharge_kw=2.5 against a 1.0 kWh shortfall delivers 1.5 kWh that appears in no flow, caught only by validate_energy_balance as 'Energy balance violated: in=0.000000 kWh, out=-1.500000 kWh', which names neither the field nor the limit, and not at all when validate_balance=False. PeakShavingStrategy's docstring says 'the strategy itself does not enforce a total-charge ceiling; the battery layer clamps downstream' (dispatch.py:601-602), which is false for the total. The built-in strategies stay within the limits only because compute_grid_charge_power_kw's residual clamp happens to share the budget.
findings.proposal: State the invariants (charge_kw <= excess PV, discharge_kw <= shortfall, charge_kw + grid_charge_kw <= max_charge_kw) once, as a check flow.simulate_timestep applies to every decision before executing it, raising ValueError that names the decision, the field and the limit (or clamping, a design choice to make explicitly), and fix the PeakShavingStrategy docstring. Either choice changes behaviour for consumer strategies that break the limits today, so it needs a release note.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — dispatch.py:37-60 DispatchDecision checks only signs and exclusivity; PeakShavingStrategy docstring 'the battery layer clamps downstream' still at dispatch.py:601-602.

findings.statement: Smart-charging modes keep charging after the car has left, contradicting the docstring's 'All strategies ensure the required charge is delivered before departure'. When the preferred window is shorter than the charge time, the code starts at the window's opening and charges min(needed, available) minutes from there (ev.py:234-237, 266-268, 285-287), where available is measured from ARRIVAL. Measured: off_peak, 3.6 kW, 35 kWh, arrive 18:00, depart 07:00 charges 00:30-10:13; solar, 3.6 kW, 30 kWh, arrive 08:00, depart 17:00 charges 10:00-18:20. Charging that runs past the window's last minute is silently dropped by numpy slicing (ev.py:300), and overflow into the next day's slots overwrites rather than adds. The function's cognitive complexity is 42 (complexipy; Sonar threshold 15) with the off-peak same-day and overnight branches written out twice, which is where the deadline rule was lost. The positional-minute DST displacement it shares with load.py is reported under load.py::generate_load_profile.
findings.proposal: Compute each session as an interval ending no later than departure: take the preferred window's overlap first, then fill the remainder backwards from the window start (or forwards from arrival) but never past departure; express the three modes as one window-selection function plus one shared scheduler instead of three branch families. Outputs change for configs where the window is too short; no signature change.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — ev.py:234-291 still starts at the window opening and charges min(needed, available) with available measured from arrival; numpy slice at ev.py:300 still drops overflow (a one-day off_peak overnight window yields no charging at all: probed).

findings.statement: Tests stance and the briefing's key scenario 'the same seed reproduces the identical fleet and per-home stochastic profiles regardless of parallel execution order': no test that any lane runs checks it. Five classes in tests/unit/test_fleet.py are marked slow: TestSimulateFleetIter (440), TestParallelMatchesSequential (504), TestSimulateHomeWeatherData (529), TestMultiSweepIter (567) and TestCollectMultiSweepResults (647). They are slow only because they build Bristol fleets without seeding the weather_cache fixture, so they would fetch PVGIS. The verify runs `-m 'not slow and not e2e'` (dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:52), and the only slow tests a lane runs are tests/integration/test_pvgis.py, so these classes run nowhere. CLAUDE.md asks for 'slow' only when a live service is needed. The one parallel-vs-sequential comparison (test_fleet.py:508-526) compares only generation, on create_uniform homes with unseeded stochastic loads. TestParallelFleetWeather (794 onward, not slow) compares parallel with simulate_home only for use_stochastic=False loads. So seeded stochastic loads drawn in worker processes have no executed test. tests/integration/test_fleet_simulation.py and test_ev_fleet.py are slow-marked too. The tests reach no private names of config, fleet, community, output or scenario_writer: an AST scan of tests/ found no imports, attribute reads or dotted-path patches of their _-prefixed names.
findings.proposal: Seed weather_cache with synthetic_june_weather in those classes and drop their slow marks. Add a non-slow test that builds a seeded fleet_distribution with use_stochastic=True and asserts identical per-home demand from simulate_fleet with parallel=False and with parallel=True under forkserver and spawn. Tests only.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tests/unit/test_fleet.py still marks the classes at lines 440, 504, 529, 567, 647 @pytest.mark.slow.

findings.statement: The post-dispatch settlement is written twice: flow.py:412-438 is a byte-identical copy of flow.py:290-316 (battery_charge sum, self-consumption cap, split-source export/import, the 7-line NOTE, EnergyFlowResult construction), and the duration/excess/shortfall preamble is copied too (356-376 vs 235-249). Fix history shows the lockstep cost: c777192 relabelled 'both copies of the split-source comment' and records 'the two 27-line post-dispatch tails stay byte-identical ... The duplicated tail itself is left for a later refactor'; 458232d also edited both sites. The charge-loss defect reported at flow.py::simulate_timestep must be fixed in both copies. simulate_timestep_tou's cognitive complexity is 24 (complexipy; Sonar threshold 15). The briefing's decision keeps two dispatch policies; it does not require two copies of the accounting.
findings.proposal: Extract one private settlement function (inputs: generation_kwh, demand_kwh, pv_charge_stored, grid_charge_stored, discharge, soc) that both paths call after deciding their battery actions; behaviour-preserving, no public change.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — flow.py:412-438 is still a verbatim copy of 290-316 (sum, self-consumption cap, NOTE, split-source flows, EnergyFlowResult), and the preamble 356-376 still copies 235-249.

findings.statement: simulate_home simulates a home AND prices it: in one 180-line body (home.py:292-472, radon cyclomatic 32 = grade E, complexipy cognitive 37) it fetches weather, validates heat-pump weather length, runs PV, expands it, generates load, adds heat-pump load, aligns, builds the battery, chooses between the two dispatch paths with a three-flag predicate and re-branches on it every timestep (home.py:374-415), then prices import cost, grid-charge cost and SEG export revenue with its own warning policy (home.py:424-454) before assembling results. The pricing is the briefing's SEG-valuation convention's enforcement point, so a change to physics orchestration and a change to pricing edit the same function.
findings.proposal: Split into private steps with one purpose each - demand assembly (load + heat pump), dispatch-path selection returning one per-timestep callable, the timestep loop, and a pricing step that turns flows into import cost, grid-charge cost and SEG revenue - leaving simulate_home a short composition; no public signature changes.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — home.py:424-454 still prices import cost, grid-charge cost and SEG export with the warning policy inside simulate_home after the timestep loop.

findings.statement: A full year of demand falls 2.2% short of LoadConfig.annual_consumption_kwh (documented as the 'Target annual electricity consumption'; generate_load_profile says it is 'scaled to match the configured annual consumption'). Each day gets annual/365 x SEASONAL_FACTORS[month] (load.py:159-166), and the stochastic path rescales to the same sum (load.py:371-377, a second copy of the formula), but the day-weighted mean of SEASONAL_FACTORS is 0.978, not 1. Measured: a 2023 Jan-Dec profile for annual_consumption_kwh=3400 totals 3,325.0 kWh on both the Elexon and the seeded richardsonpy path (2024: about 3,336). Every simulated home therefore demands ~75 kWh/yr less than configured, which moves import, self-consumption and Basis-C own-use; docs/finance-spreadsheet-reconciliation.md §4.1 reasons with calibration homes that 'demand 3,400 kWh/yr' and derives its 642.5 kWh over-billing figure from it, so the doc and the simulator disagree. validation.validate_consumption's 20% tolerance (validation.py:304-309) cannot see the gap.
findings.proposal: Normalise the seasonal weights by their day-weighted mean over the simulated year at the point of use (one private helper both paths call), so a calendar-year run delivers annual_consumption_kwh exactly; SEASONAL_FACTORS (in __all__) keeps its values. Outputs move by +2.2% demand (release note); re-check the reconciliation doc's §4.1 figures.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — load.py:159-166 and 370-377 unchanged; recomputed day-weighted mean of SEASONAL_FACTORS for 2023 = 0.97795, i.e. 3,325.0 kWh for a 3,400 kWh target.

findings.statement: Dispatch classifies cheap periods from summaries of the period LIST, not of the schedule the tariff charges, so two tariffs with identical get_rate at every minute can dispatch differently. flow._is_cheap_period is rate < peak_rate and rate <= mean_period_rate (flow.py:157-168), and mean_period_rate counts 'each period once whatever its length' (tariff.py:143-147). Verified: night 0.10 / day 0.20 / peak 0.35 / day 0.20 (4 periods, mean 0.2125) classifies 10:00 at 0.20 as cheap, while the same schedule with the night split 00:00-03:00 + 03:00-07:00 (5 periods, mean 0.19) does not, which switches grid charging at the day rate on or off (the spread gate passes: 0.35 > 0.20/0.95). TariffConfig also never checks coverage or overlap at construction (tariff.py:126-134): a gap raises only at the first uncovered minute mid-simulation, and overlapping periods resolve first-match-wins while still feeding peak_rate - verified: an all-day 0.20 period plus a fully shadowed 16:00-19:00 0.40 period charges 0.20 at 17:00 but reports peak_rate 0.40, so every minute is 'cheap' and the spread gate arbitrages against a price the tariff never charges. Two-rate tariffs (Economy 7/10, the canonical scenarios) are unaffected; custom period lists from YAML (config.parse_tariff_config) and consumers are.
findings.proposal: Refuse, at TariffConfig construction and naming the offending periods, any period list that leaves a minute of the day uncovered or covers one twice, so a tariff's period list and its schedule agree; and classify cheap periods on a duration-weighted mean rate (a private helper in flow.py or a new member). Refusing previously accepted period lists tightens the contract of a class in __all__ (version bump); mean_period_rate's documented meaning can stay.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tariff.py:144-147 mean_period_rate still averages period rates each counted once; flow._is_cheap_period (flow.py:157-168) still compares against it.

findings.statement: Comments stance: community.py is 42% prose by radon (C+M % L), the highest of the five modules, and the prose has drifted. 'Per-step ◆ invariant (PRD §3.2) — mirrors home.simulate_home:299-300' (community.py:319) points at home.py lines that are now simulate_home's signature. The validate_energy_balance call is at home.py:418. The module and its docstrings use planning-slice labels a reader cannot resolve: α, γ, ε, ◆, 'task-34', 'PRD §3' (lines 5, 10, 14, 43-44, 76, 237, 251-252, 286, 339) with no path to the PRD, which is docs/prds/inter-home-community-energy-sharing.md. The module docstring also re-lists the exported symbols (8-14). output.py repeats the pattern, e.g. 'The δ-owned scaffold; η extends it additively' and 'None (default) reproduces the δ output exactly' (output.py:562-563, 573, 582, 664, 734, 753, 769): prose written for reviewers that belongs in commit messages.
findings.proposal: Replace the slice labels and line-number pointers with one docs/prds/inter-home-community-energy-sharing.md path where the rationale must persist, and delete the reviewer-answering prose and the symbol re-list. Docstring-only edits in community.py and output.py.

findings.statement: These modules carry reviewer-answering prose and pointers no agent can follow: the 9-line 'Seam note' defending the cheap-period authority and naming the internal codename 'gamma function path' (dispatch.py:499-507); compute_grid_charge_power_kw's 'Frame note' citing the tests that pin it (dispatch.py:129-139); 'PRD §3.1', 'PRD §3.2', 'PRD §4', 'PRD §11 OQ3' pointers that never name docs/prds/tou-grid-charging-battery-arbitrage.md (flow.py:166, 179, 245, 275, 296; dispatch.py:126, 596); Battery.__init__'s NOTE pointing at 'task zeta (project_multi_year)' (battery.py:305-313); seg.resolve_seg_tariff's 'wiring ... is owned by subsequent tasks' although config.py:1858 calls it (seg.py:44-48); HomeConfig.seg_tariff's 'cross-PRD seam field: the web UI (P2) sets it' (home.py:62-64); validation.py's 'VAL-00x acceptance criteria' blocks; load.py's DST off-by-one history (284-288). dispatch.py is 289 prose lines (docstrings plus comments) beside 295 source lines (radon raw).

findings.statement: target_soc_fraction has three meanings. GridChargeConfig documents it as 'a fraction of usable capacity' (config.py:258-259), GridChargeContext as 'a fraction of capacity', and compute_grid_charge_power_kw computes target_kwh = target_soc_fraction * capacity_kwh (dispatch.py:179) with capacity_kwh = battery.config.capacity_kwh, the nominal total (flow.py:270, 394), while Battery's SOC limits and soc_fraction are fractions of the SOH-derated effective capacity (battery.py:400-413). So 0.5 means 5.0 kWh of a 10 kWh battery whatever its age - 0.625 of an 80%-SOH battery's capacity - and the default 0.9 sits above max_soc_kwh on any aged battery, so the controller requests grid power every cheap minute that Battery.charge then discards.
findings.proposal: Pick one basis (most naturally the battery's own soc_fraction basis, effective capacity) and pass the battery's effective capacity into the context; fix both docstrings. Changes grid-charging outputs for aged batteries (release note).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — dispatch.py:179 target_kwh = ctx.target_soc_fraction * capacity_kwh with capacity_kwh = battery.config.capacity_kwh (flow.py:270, 394); Battery SOC fractions are of SOH-derated capacity (battery.py:400-413).

findings.statement: EVConfig carries charger_type as a meaningful string ('3.6kW', '7kW', '22kW') turned into power by an ad-hoc parser, float(self.charger_type.replace('kW', '')) (ev.py:114-121), and smart_charging_mode as a string routed on == compares in generate_ev_charging_profile (ev.py:216, 242), each validated against a list literal (ev.py:62, 95). The same module defines EVChargerType and SmartChargingMode enums with exactly those values (ev.py:11-35), which nothing in src/ references.
findings.proposal: Use the enums as the field types (parsing strings at the YAML/web boundary) and derive charger power from the enum, or delete the unused enums. EVConfig is in FROZEN_CLOSURE, so changing the field types is a breaking change (version bump); deleting the enums is not.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — ev.py:114-121 still parses charger_type with replace('kW',''); smart_charging_mode still routed on == (216, 242); EVChargerType/SmartChargingMode enums have no src reference (grep: tests only).

findings.statement: The briefing convention 'fleet simulations must be reproducible from a single seed: per-home seed = fleet_seed + index' is enforced only in generate_homes_from_distribution (config.py:1752-1754). FleetConfig's own public constructors cannot express it. create_uniform (fleet.py:49-82) gives every home the same LoadConfig object, so a seeded LoadConfig makes all homes draw an identical stochastic profile, and the default LoadConfig (use_stochastic=True, seed=None) is irreproducible. create_heterogeneous (84-129) always builds unseeded stochastic LoadConfigs. Verified on the pinned tree: three simulate_fleet runs of create_uniform(4, PVConfig(4.0), LoadConfig(annual_consumption_kwh=3400)) on one synthetic day gave different per-home peak demand every run, under both fork and forkserver. Neither constructor has a src/ caller (tests use them), but both are public members of the frozen FleetConfig.
findings.proposal: Give both constructors a seed parameter that applies seed + index per home. That is an additive signature change to a frozen-surface member, so under the briefing's contract it needs a version bump. Otherwise document on each that it builds unseeded loads. Contained in fleet.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — fleet.py:49-129 create_uniform shares one LoadConfig across homes and create_heterogeneous builds unseeded LoadConfigs; unchanged.

findings.statement: Heuristic 8, prefer immutable data, and the briefing's frozen convention: FleetConfig (fleet.py:25) and FleetResults (132) are mutable dataclasses with list fields, and simulate_fleet hands FleetConfig's own list to the result (home_configs=config.homes, 412; collect_multi_sweep_results does the same at 648). So a FleetResults aliases its FleetConfig, and appending a home to the config afterwards breaks the result's pairing invariant. FleetResults compensates by re-running _require_paired_homes at use (get_aggregate_series 180), and calculate_fleet_summary calls that private method from outside the class (434). FleetConfig.__post_init__'s single-timezone rule (43-47) does not survive a later homes.append either. CommunityResults is built and then mutated (community.py:366-368 assigns the three billing fields after construction). Tracked: task 669 (pending, covers freezing).
findings.proposal: Freeze FleetResults and FleetConfig with tuple fields, and construct CommunityResults once with its billing fields. All three are in __all__/FROZEN_CLOSURE, so freezing them and changing list to tuple is a BREAKING change needing a version bump. Short of that, copy the list at construction (list(config.homes)) so results stop aliasing configs. Spans fleet.py and community.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — fleet.py FleetConfig (25) and FleetResults (132) still plain @dataclass with list fields; simulate_fleet passes config.homes (412); calculate_fleet_summary calls results._require_paired_homes() (434); community.py:366-368 mutates CommunityResults after construction.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT: the process-pool fan-out policy is written twice. simulate_multi_sweep_iter (fleet.py:502-571) repeats simulate_fleet_iter (315-371), which is its one-sweep case: the TMY prefetch (343 / 531), the sequential fallback (345 / 538), the worker-count formula `max_workers or min(n, os.cpu_count() or 4)` (356 / 553), the submit/as_completed loop (357-371 / 554-571), and two worker functions (261 / 276) that differ only in a tag. Neither loop puts the home's index or name on a worker's exception: the futures dicts (358, 555) map each future to its index, but `yield future.result()` (371, 571) never uses it, and simulate_home's errors (home.py) carry no home name. A failed home in a 100-home run therefore raises an error that does not say which home failed. The executor's context exit then waits for every pending home to finish, because shutdown runs without cancel_futures. Any fix for that has to land in both copies. Cognitive complexity of simulate_multi_sweep_iter: 20. No task covers this.
findings.proposal: Write simulate_fleet_iter as simulate_multi_sweep_iter over one sweep, or both over one private fan-out helper. In that helper, wrap a worker failure with the home's index and name, and cancel pending futures on error. Contained in fleet.py; public signatures unchanged.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — fleet.py simulate_fleet_iter (315-371) and simulate_multi_sweep_iter (502-571) still duplicate prefetch, sequential fallback, worker formula and submit/as_completed loop; future.result() still yielded without index context.

findings.statement: SummaryStatistics (in __all__) and flow.EnergyFlowResult are plain mutable @dataclass types (home.py:214, flow.py:124), against the briefing convention that domain objects are frozen dataclasses validated in __post_init__: each validates at construction (the grid-charge sub-total invariant, home.py:249-259; the non-negative flows, flow.py:144-151), and plain assignment afterwards bypasses that check. Nothing in src/ or tests/ assigns to their fields (grep).
findings.proposal: Declare both frozen=True. Assignment would then raise for any consumer that mutates them, so it is a breaking change to frozen-surface classes (version bump).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — home.py:214 SummaryStatistics and flow.py:124 EnergyFlowResult are still plain @dataclass with construction-time checks.

findings.statement: SEG export revenue is one fact with two representations on the frozen surface, and its callers show the confusion. total_export_revenue_gbp is the sum of the per-minute export_revenue that simulate_home priced from HomeConfig.seg_tariff (home.py:441-445). seg_revenue_gbp is an independent recomputation from a seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh argument (home.py:544-549), mirrored in FleetSummary.total_seg_revenue_gbp next to total_export_revenue_gbp (fleet.py:462-470, 494). The docstring needs 20 lines (home.py:493-514) to explain when the two differ. cli/home.py:165-171 deliberately avoids passing the rate 'so the revenue is not counted twice'. finance passes the scenario rate at finance.py:1570 and 2358 but never reads the seg_revenue_gbp it produces (it reads total_export_revenue_gbp via _annualise_physics, finance.py:533-546). cli/finance.py:238-241 threads the rate onto the ScenarioConfig only under --cost-recovery, 'to avoid silently changing project_multi_year SEG revenue'. That comment is false: the homes already carry seg_tariff from cli/finance.py:161-169, project_multi_year reads total_export_revenue_gbp, and the branch changes nothing.
findings.proposal: Remove the false comment and the no-op branch in cli/finance.py, and drop the unused seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh argument at finance.py:1570 and 2358 (mechanical). Retiring calculate_summary's seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh path and SummaryStatistics.seg_revenue_gbp / FleetSummary.total_seg_revenue_gbp in favour of total_export_revenue_gbp is a breaking change needing a deprecation cycle and a version bump.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — home.py:475-588 still computes seg_revenue_gbp separately from total_export_revenue_gbp with the 20-line two-path docstring; fleet.py:462-470 still aggregates total_seg_revenue_gbp beside total_export_revenue_gbp.

findings.statement: tests/unit/test_load.py::TestWindowedStochasticGeneration::test_richardsonpy_runtime_error_falls_back_to_elexon monkeypatches the private load._simulate_stochastic_day (test_load.py:547) to reach the fallback. The seam it reaches through is the defect: _try_richardsonpy_profile is a 170-line function whose single try wraps the richardsonpy imports, our own windowing, DST trim/pad and normalisation, ending in except Exception: return None (load.py:257-399, noqa BLE001), so any bug in our own code silently swaps the load model to the Elexon shape with only a log warning; richardsonpy has been a hard dependency since 0cc4276 dropped the import guards, yet the imports still sit inside the try.
findings.proposal: Narrow the guarded region to the richardsonpy calls (or drop the fallback now that the dependency is hard), split windowing/normalisation into functions with their own tests, and drive the fallback test through a public seam (e.g. an injected profile source) rather than a private name.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tests/unit/test_load.py:547 still monkeypatch.setattr(load_module, '_simulate_stochastic_day', _always_raise); load.py:257-399 single try with richardsonpy imports inside.

findings.statement: Age degradation is applied to AC output after inverter clipping (pv.py:762-767), although it is a module (DC) property and the briefing's system-losses decision rejects moving DC losses to the AC side because it 'would stop inverter-limited arrays clipping at their rating'. Measured on Bristol's scaled TMY at age 20 (factor 0.9) against the same factor on DC: 4 kWp/no inverter limit +0.11%, 5 kWp/3.68 kW -0.32%, 6 kWp/3.68 kW -1.80% annual AC - and 3.68 kW inverters on larger arrays are common under G98. tests/unit/test_pv.py::TestSimulatePVOutput::test_degradation_applied_in_live_path pins the exact 0.9 AC ratio. The briefing's degradation decision (linear factor, inside simulate_pv_output) is otherwise honoured.
findings.proposal: Fold the degradation factor into the DC losses step (_deduct_system_losses scales DC by (1 - losses) x factor) so clipping applies to degraded DC, and update the pinned test; outputs change for inverter-limited aged arrays (release note).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — pv.py:762-767 still applies apply_degradation to AC after ModelChain's inverter.

findings.statement: Finiteness is enforced in some domain dataclasses and not others. BatteryConfig, PVConfig, LoadConfig and Location use NaN-safe 'not lo < x < hi' checks, but these accept NaN (verified): SEGTariff(rate_pence_per_kwh=nan) (and inf), TariffPeriod(rate_per_kwh=nan), HeatPumpConfig thermal_capacity_kw/annual_heat_demand_kwh=nan, EVConfig(required_charge_kwh=nan), DispatchDecision(charge_kw=nan), PeakShavingStrategy(nan). calculate_seg_revenue(10, SEGTariff('x', nan)) returns nan, which flows into export_revenue and SummaryStatistics unchecked. The boundaries refuse non-finite numbers case by case (web number_fields.as_finite_float, config.py:1869 for the SEG rate), so a frozen-library consumer constructing these classes directly gets no check: the invariant has no single home.
findings.proposal: One shared finite-range validator (e.g. a require_finite_in(value, lo, hi, name) helper beside whole_numbers.py) called from every config dataclass's __post_init__ in these modules. Refusing NaN/inf that are accepted today is a contract tightening (release note).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — seg.py:24 still `if self.rate_pence_per_kwh < 0` (NaN and inf pass).

findings.statement: tests/unit/test_tariff_period_time_cache.py::TestTimesAreParsedOnce::test_get_rate_never_reparses_period_times patches the private TariffPeriod._parse_time (line 54) to pin a caching implementation. The seam exists because TariffPeriod carries its times as 'HH:MM' strings parsed by an ad-hoc split(':') parser (tariff.py:43-68) into cached_property values kept out of fields() because 'web/storage.py's JSON round-trip walks fields() and cannot encode a datetime.time' (tariff.py:70-72): a domain type's representation set by a web persistence detail.
findings.proposal: Assert the behaviour through the public accessors (the identity test beside it already does) and drop the private patch; longer term parse to datetime.time at the boundary and teach storage to encode it - changing start_time/end_time's type is a breaking change to a class in __all__ (version bump).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tests/unit/test_tariff_period_time_cache.py:54 still patches TariffPeriod._parse_time with wraps; tariff.py _parse_time at line 44.

findings.statement: The 'annual yield' check divides the WHOLE run's generation by wired kWp without annualising (validation.py:87-93), so any run of 365+ days other than one year is misjudged: a two-year series at 1,000 kWh/kWp/yr reports 'Annual yield (2000 kWh/kWp ...) outside the expected UK range' and fails (verified). validate_consumption, beside it, does annualise with 365/duration_days (validation.py:299-302).
findings.proposal: Annualise (total x 365 / duration_days) as validate_consumption does, ideally through one shared helper.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — validation.py:87-93 still divides the whole run's generation by wired kWp for any duration >= 365 days, without annualising.

findings.statement: UK benchmark facts live in several copies that disagree, and validation's are unsourced. validate_self_consumption_pv_only reports 20-45% as the 'UK benchmark range' while its own docstring gives ~25-35% and the bounds are commented 'Slightly wider' (validation.py:342, 365-366); the battery check reports 50-90% against a stated 60-80% widened 'to account for simulation variations' (validation.py:444-445) - fitting edges to model output, which the briefing's yield-band decision forbids and its what_working_means asks to be published bands. web/assistant.py's METRIC_TABLE tells users 30-40% and 55-70% with named sources, and gives Ofgem TDCV medium as both 2,700 and 2,900 kWh and high as 4,100 and 4,200; load.OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS uses 1,800/2,700/3,200/3,900/4,500 by occupant count, which are not Ofgem's low/medium/high values; and both self-consumption checks estimate yield as capacity_kw * 900 'Rough UK yield' (validation.py:389, 461) beside the 300-1200 band and the ~1,000 kWh/kWp the model gives in Bristol.
findings.proposal: Give each benchmark one home with its source in docs/ (as docs/pv-annual-yield-benchmark.md does for yield) and have validation.py and the assistant table read it; label the TDCV-by-occupants table as the project's own interpolation, not Ofgem's figures. Spans validation.py, load.py and web/assistant.py; no public signature changes (OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS's name is frozen).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — validation.py:342/365-366 (25-35% stated, 20-45% applied), 419/444-445 (60-80% stated, 50-90% applied), capacity_kw * 900 at 389 and 461 unchanged; load.OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS unchanged.

findings.statement: config.py has 51 numeric coercion sites, and no one reader enforces the rule 'a finite number, never a bool, a whole number where a count is meant, refused with the key path'. The block readers use three different styles. (a) Raw splat into the domain dataclass: _parse_pv_config, _parse_battery_config, _parse_load_config, _parse_grid_charge_config, and parse_home_block's scalar keys. The component __post_init__ checks bounds only, never type. (b) Inline float(), int() or str(): _parse_heat_pump_config, _parse_ev_config, _build_shuffled_pool_spec, _parse_proportional_to_multiplier, parse_fleet_distribution_config's int(data['n_homes']), _parse_event_windows, and _parse_distribution_spec's isinstance(data, (int, float)), which lets True through. (c) Tables over _number or _number_or_none: the finance and grid-services blocks only. whole_numbers.whole_number is used nowhere in config.py. Probes at 7dfea36 confirm each style's failure. `pv: {capacity_kw: true}` builds a PVConfig whose capacity_kw is the bool True. `azimuth: south` raises a raw TypeError from PVConfig.__post_init__, and cli/utils.handle_errors does not catch TypeError. `use_stochastic: 'no'` is kept as a truthy string. `heat_pump: {thermal_capacity_kw: .nan}` is accepted, because HeatPumpConfig's `<= 0` and `> 50` comparisons are both False for NaN. Location altitude NaN is accepted the same way. `arrival_hour: 18.9` becomes 18, `n_homes: 2.7` becomes 2, `n_homes: true` becomes 1, and a distribution capacity_kw of true becomes 1.0. A null annual_heat_demand_kwh raises a raw TypeError from float(None). The project already has the right reader, in the web layer: web/number_fields.as_finite_float, as_whole_number and their *_within variants. Because config.py lacks it, the web layer compensates. web/fleet_scenario._read_fleet_size_and_seed reads n_homes and seed itself, 'ahead of the loaders, whose int() would refuse n_homes first, naming no setting'.
findings.proposal: Add a module below config.py, scenario_fields.py, beside whole_numbers.py. It holds typed field readers that all raise ConfigurationError naming the full key path and the value given: finite_number(value, path, low=None, high=None), whole_number_field(value, path, low, high), boolean_field(value, path) (only a YAML bool) and choice(value, path, allowed). Move the rule now in web/number_fields into it, and turn number_fields into a thin ValueError adapter over it. Express every block reader as a declarative key-to-reader table, the shape _FINANCE_SCALAR_COERCIONS already has, applied by one function, read_block(block_path, data, table, cls). That function refuses unrecognised keys, reads each present key through its reader, and constructs cls with only those keys, so omitted keys take the dataclass default. This deletes _number, _number_or_none and _float_or_none, the finite check in _parse_seg_rate_scalar, the inline float(), int() and str() calls, and the web pre-read in _read_fleet_size_and_seed. It would have prevented tasks 374, 384 and 498 and the live tasks 314, 382, 521, 558, 559, 570, 573, 616, 618, 651, 675 and 678: each becomes one table row, not a separate fix.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Read config.py at 7dfea36. _parse_pv_config still splats PVConfig(**{...}). _parse_ev_config still does int(data['arrival_hour']), and parse_fleet_distribution_config int(data['n_homes']). _number is used only by the finance and grid-services tables, and whole_number is never imported by config.py. Probe: parse_home_block({'pv': {'capacity_kw': True}}) gives capacity_kw True.

findings.statement: PVConfig's defaults (azimuth 180.0, tilt 35.0, module_efficiency 0.20, inverter_efficiency 0.96, degradation_rate_per_year 0.005) are written four times: in pv.py::PVConfig, in config.py::PVDistributionConfig's field defaults, in config.py::_parse_pv_distribution_config's data.get(..., 180.0) calls, and in config.py::generate_homes_from_distribution's `pv_azimuth if pv_azimuth is not None else 180.0` fallbacks. EV defaults (departure 7, required 35.0, mode 'none') appear in ev.py::EVConfig, _parse_ev_config, EVDistributionConfig, _parse_ev_distribution_config and generate_homes_from_distribution. Heat-pump 8.0 and 8000.0 appear in four places, and battery 2.5 kW in four. Each layer also restates which fields it carries, and they already disagree. The distribution grammar has no temperature_coefficient, inverter_capacity_kw or system_losses for PV, and no SOC limits, efficiencies or degradation for batteries. The sweep rebuilders copy fields by hand: _modify_pv_config drops system_losses and the custom pvlib params, and _modify_battery_config drops dispatch_strategy, grid_charging, the SOC limits, the efficiencies and the degradation fields. A probe confirms a battery-capacity sweep resets grid_charging to None and min_soc to 0.1. generate_homes_from_distribution reaches cognitive complexity 45 largely through these per-component None-fallback branches. The PRDs for financial-layer battery fidelity and live-sim PV degradation already require threading each new field through every one of these sites by hand.
findings.proposal: Make the domain dataclass the only statement of a component's fields and defaults. The sampler builds each component as Cls(**{k: v for k, v in sampled.items() if v is not None}), so an unsampled or null field takes the dataclass default, and the `else 180.0` fallbacks and the *DistributionConfig default values are deleted. Derive each *DistributionConfig's recognised keys from dataclasses.fields(Cls), minus an explicit per-component set of fields the distribution grammar does not sample, and parse each value through _parse_distribution_spec. Replace _modify_pv_config, _modify_battery_config and _modify_load_config with dataclasses.replace. That deletes about 150 lines of copy-constructors and the restated defaults in four places per component. It removes the 'thread through every construction site' cost from future field additions, and it would have prevented f5c5356 and the live tasks 599, 600, 237 and 320.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Read _modify_battery_config. It still builds BatteryConfig(capacity_kwh, max_charge_kw, max_discharge_kw, name) only, dropping dispatch_strategy, grid_charging, SOC limits and efficiencies. The PV defaults are still restated in PVDistributionConfig, _parse_pv_distribution_config and generate_homes_from_distribution.

findings.statement: Which document a config file is (a scenario list, one scenario, a bare scenario, a wrapped or flat home file, fleet homes, a fleet distribution, a YAML sweep) is decided by testing for top-level keys.
