It refuses std < 0 and a uniform min > max. It does not refuse a normal with min > max, negative weights, or a values/weights length mismatch. Verified at the pin: sample_distribution('normal', {mean: 4, std: 1, min: 9, max: 2}) returns [2.0, 2.0, 2.0], and weights [-1, 3] draw samples, although NormalDistribution and WeightedDiscreteDistribution.__post_init__ refuse both. Its shuffled pool also cycles past the end of the pool, whereas a run indexes past the end and raises the IndexError that builder_form._scenario_reader_errors catches for 'a shuffled pool smaller than the fleet'. The preview therefore shows histograms for distributions Run refuses, sampled under different rules. The copy exists because config offers no public way to parse one spec and draw from it: _parse_distribution_spec, _sample_from_distribution and _DistributionSampler are all private.
findings.proposal: Expose a narrow public seam in config: parse_distribution_spec(data, path) -> DistributionSpec and draw_values(spec, n, seed) -> list[Optional[float]], the latter wrapping _DistributionSampler so pools behave as a run does. Ideally replace the isinstance chain in _sample_from_distribution with a sample(rng) method on each frozen distribution type (heuristic 3). The preview then becomes editor dist -> grammar spec (the single decoder) -> parse -> draw. That deletes _draw_samples and all its private refusal messages, and the preview refuses exactly what Run refuses. This would have prevented 569, 571 and the per-check patches 520 needed.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed: sample_distribution('normal', {mean 4, std 1, min 9, max 2}, 3) -> [2.0, 2.0, 2.0]; weights [-1, 3] -> [5.0]*4; _draw_samples unchanged (cognitive 34).

findings.statement: The maximum fleet size has three values. templates/simulate/fleet.html renders n_homes min 10 and max 500. fleet-simulator.js formErrors refuses n > 1000. The server, through read_fleet_size, allows MAX_FLEET_HOMES = 10_000. formErrors also makes rules of its own that the server does not hold. It refuses std <= 0 and min >= max, where config refuses only std < 0 and min > max. It applies those checks to PV only, not battery or load. fleet-simulator.js holds literal starting distributions that differ from FLEET_COMPONENTS.builder_default: battery max 15.0 against 13.5, load max 6000 against 5000, and a different set of PV rows. This is despite fleet_components' docstring saying both fleet pages render their editors from it. The scripts parseInt n_homes, days and peak hours, so 2.5 is sent as 2, which defeats the server's refuse-fractions policy (498). The PV bound 0.5-20 is a literal in both simulation_params.parse_home_config and home.html (live 612). Server constants reach scripts only through per-page ad-hoc channels: scenarios._script_components for the builder and home.html's consumptionRange. The fleet and sweep scripts receive nothing.
findings.proposal: Add web/form_limits.py::page_limits(), returning one JSON-able frozen value that holds MAX_FLEET_HOMES, MAX_FLEET_SEED, MAX_WINDOW_DAYS, each FleetComponent's fixed_range, step and default editor state, the home PV range (moved into FLEET_COMPONENTS['pv'] or a HOME_PV_RANGE that parse_home_config reads), and the sweep parameters. Inject it through a single Flask context_processor, so every template's min/max and every script reads limits.*. Replace the client-side refusals (formErrors) with the server's answer, as the builder already does through /api/scenarios/validate, and send raw numbers rather than parseInt'd ones. What becomes deletable: fleet.html's 10/500, formErrors, the literal pvDist/batteryDist/loadDist (taken from FLEET_COMPONENTS, with builder_default renamed to default), parameterOptions, home.html's 0.5/20 and the PV literal in parse_home_config. This would have prevented 376, 612, 140, 664, 676 and 522.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — fleet-simulator.js:94 'n > 1000', :92/109/118/146 parseInt, literal battery max 15.0 (:59) and load max 6000 (:76); fleet.html:36 min=10 max=500.

findings.statement: The fleet page imports scenarios on the server. fleet_scenario.fleet_form_from_scenario runs the loaders first, refuses a setting the form needs but cannot hold, and lists the rest in not_loaded. The builder parses the same grammar in the browser with js-yaml, in scenario-builder.js scenarioFormFields and componentDistribution, under the opposite policy: it drops silently. A non-flat_rate tariff becomes import_rate '', so the next preview or save writes tariff: null. A preset SEG becomes ''. dispatch_strategy and every non-capacity component setting vanish with no notice. componentDistribution refuses the 'fixed' type, which fleet_config.distribution_form_spec accepts. js-yaml reads .nan and .inf as numbers (298/549) and unquoted dates as Date objects (554), none of which the loaders see. loadPreset bypasses even scenarioFormFields: it copies name, latitude, longitude and n_homes, with the truthiness reads `cfg.location.latitude || 51.45` and `if (fd.n_homes)`. api.py::scenarios_get_preset returns `config` in two untagged shapes: a scenario document for built-ins, and the flat builder form for saved presets, because scenarios_save_scenario stores getFormData's output without validating it.
findings.proposal: Add builder_form.builder_form_from_scenario(document) -> ImportedForm(form, not_loaded). Build it on fleet_scenario's _read_blocks, _not_loaded and _read_typed_block machinery, moved into a shared web/scenario_import.py so both pages import under one policy. Serve it from /api/scenarios/import-yaml and /api/scenarios/presets/<name>, answering {form, not_loaded} as _loaded_fleet_form_answer does. Saved builder presets would store the scenario document, scenario_from_builder_form's output after builder_form_errors, so built-in and saved presets share one shape. What becomes deletable: scenarioFormFields, componentDistribution, distributionRows, loadPreset's field picking, and the builder page's js-yaml dependency. This would have prevented 298, 545, 549, 553, 554 and 360.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — scenario-builder.js still parses uploads with jsyaml.load into scenarioFormFields/componentDistribution (:15, :48, :238).

findings.statement: Docstrings make up 43% of fleet_config.py's raw lines (225 of 545) and 35% of fleet_scenario.py's (188 of 550). Raises sections enumerate refusals transitively: form_to_fleet_distribution_config's points at _component_block, _refuse_battery_dispatch_strategy and _parse_component_distribution, which point further down. fleet_form_from_scenario's docstring is a 20-line policy statement. That prose is the contract a typed refusal or a single grammar owner would carry. Of the window's 94 non-merge commits on the five Python core files, 26 are amend: commits, several docstring-only, whose job was keeping this prose in step with the code: 1ea7939, 6830f03, b62bba5, 1c0fbb2, 6d2ca16 and a90340c. 6d2ca16 described a truncating integer reader that 650 later removed.
findings.proposal: Once the number invariant and the grammar sit in config and a single decoder, as the first two findings propose, each Raises section shrinks to 'ConfigurationError from config's fleet_distribution grammar; ValueError from read_editor_distribution'. Policy prose such as fleet_form_from_scenario's (what the form holds, what it refuses, what goes in not_loaded) moves to a tracked docs/web-fleet-forms.md, with a one-line pointer from the code.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Snapshot prose share fleet_config 0.4312, fleet_scenario 0.3545; read in full: transitive Raises sections ('see :func:_component_block' etc.) unchanged.

findings.statement: Each chart on a results page is described in four unrelated places. (1) routes.py::home_results builds a dict keyed by chart name, whose values are JSON strings. A builder returns '{}' (sankey_diagram, sweep_parameter_chart), None (monthly_summary, seasonal_comparison, heat_pump_analysis) or JSON, so 'nothing to draw' is a three-state string convention (heuristic 12). (2) results/home.html and fleet.html guard each container with `{% if charts.x and charts.x != '{}' %}` and hand-write the card, an h3 title, `id="chart-..."` and `style="min-height: NNNpx"`. The title and height repeat what the Python builder already sets in `fig.update_layout(title=..., height=...)`. (3) The inline script repeats the id in `renderChart('chart-...', ...)`, with a separate and different guard (`{% if charts.monthly %}`, or none at all for chart-financial). (4) chart-renderer.js::renderChart re-checks `jsonStr === '{}'` and then the missing element. The chart_container macro, which bundles card, title, id and height, exists but only history/compare.html uses it (results/home.html has 9 hand-written panels, fleet.html 5). The id-written-twice rule is policed by tests/unit/test_web_results_chart_targets.py, which regex-reads the page's script via tests/_html_page.py::render_chart_targets. Its docstring concedes the converse (renderChart called for a container the guard omitted) is unchecked. The drawing seam is also not single. Results pages use renderChart. compare.html calls Plotly.newPlot itself (see the separate finding). The sweep page's JS `_renderChart` draws with Chart.js, which no template loads. It reads `document.getElementById('sweep-chart')` as a canvas, but sweep.html makes that element a <div>, so the call returns at `typeof Chart === 'undefined'`. charts.py::sweep_parameter_chart, the Plotly equivalent, is called only from tests/unit/test_web_scenarios.py. The Plotly CDN script tag is repeated verbatim in three templates, and results/home.html and fleet.html each also load chart-renderer.js. Measured: three draw paths, one id written 2-3 times per chart, and the same emptiness rule written in Python, Jinja (x2) and JS.
findings.proposal: Introduce one typed description of a chart, e.g. `ChartPanel(slug, title, height_px, figure_json)` (frozen dataclass), in charts.py or a new web/chart_panels.py. Each builder returns a figure or None, never '{}'. A page assembler (`home_chart_panels(results, summary, config) -> list[ChartPanel]`, `fleet_chart_panels`, `comparison_chart_panels`) returns only the charts that have something to draw, grouped by tab. The route passes that list. One Jinja partial, `chart_panels(panels)`, loops it and renders chart_container and the single `renderChart(slug, figure)` call from the same record, so the id, title and height live once and the emptiness rule is 'not in the list'. Pull the Plotly + chart-renderer.js script tags into one `{% block chart_scripts %}` or partial that every chart page includes (this also closes the CDN duplication tasks 129/250). Delete: the `!= '{}'` guards, the `'{}'` returns, the JS `'{}'` check, the hand-written panels, the inline renderChart blocks, tests/unit/test_web_results_chart_targets.py and `render_chart_targets`/`render_chart_figure` regex readers, and the dead Chart.js sweep path or the Python sweep chart (whichever the sweep page keeps). Prevents the id-twice, empty-figure-rule and missing-container classes (637, 674, 639, 635, 683) and the unwired sweep chart (123, 135).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — grep: results/home.html 7 and results/fleet.html 5 "!= '{}'" guards, 0 chart_container uses each; charts.py still returns '{}' (sankey_diagram, sweep_parameter_chart) and None (monthly_summary, seasonal_comparison, heat_pump_analysis).

findings.statement: Colour is defined in at least five places that tests must keep reconciled. (a) tailwind.config.js `primary` is a verbatim copy of Tailwind's built-in amber (its comment says tests rely on that). Accent and status roles therefore share the same classes, and tests/unit/test_web_theme_colours.py needs a 316-line allow-list (_AMBER_ROLES: 5 roles, per-template class sets) to tell an accent use of bg-amber-500 from a status use. Tasks 235, 343 and 539 each fixed one instance of this. (b) charts.py::COLOUR_PALETTE is a separate palette whose `_AMBER = '#f5a623'` differs from primary-500 `#f59e0b`, and a few chart colours are outside it ('#888888' annotation, 'black' Sankey outline). (c) chart-renderer.js hard-codes the card surface and text colours (`#1e293b`, `#e2e8f0`, `#334155`, `#ffffff`, `#e2e8f0`) that mirror Tailwind slate classes on the card in macros.html, so a theme or card edit reaches the page but not the chart. (d) parameter-sweep.js writes '#f59e0b' and '#6b7280' literally; test_web_theme_colours.py's hex checks explicitly skip scripts. (e) run-status colours exist in macros.html's `_run_status_badge_classes` dict, again as bg-green-500/bg-amber-500 in progress-tracker.html, and as an if/elif on flash category in base.html, with statuses as bare strings in JS ('queued', 'pending', 'completed', 'failed'). The Python side already has the typed vocabulary (database.py RunStatus/JobStatus Literals), but the templates and JS key on string literals, so 'queued' silently falls to the neutral badge. The invariant 'the palette is defined once' is enforced only by tests that regex-scan source text, with documented holes.
findings.proposal: Make the theme tokens the one home and have everything else read them. In tailwind.config.js, define semantic status tokens (`status.pending|running|completed|failed`, plus `surface`) as a separate palette from `primary`. Expose them as CSS custom properties in static/src/input.css (`:root`/`.dark`). Then: macros.html badges and progress-tracker.html use `bg-status-*` utilities, which kills the need for _AMBER_ROLES, the amber-copy premise test and per-template class lists. chart-renderer.js takes its surface/text/grid colours from `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--chart-surface')` instead of hex literals, and parameter-sweep.js (or its replacement) reads the same variables. Generate COLOUR_PALETTE's accent/status entries from the same token file (a small JSON read by both tailwind.config.js and charts.py) so the chart palette derives from the theme or is explicitly a different thing. Deletes: _AMBER_ROLES and its 4 guard tests, the 'copies amber' premise check, the JS hex literals, the duplicated status mapping in progress-tracker.html. Prevents the 235/343/539/356/537/342/348 class.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — charts.py:34 _AMBER '#f5a623'; tailwind.config.js:11 still copies amber; chart-renderer.js:29-44 hard-codes #1e293b/#e2e8f0; parameter-sweep.js:220-221 '#f59e0b'/'#6b7280'.

findings.statement: The upstream subsystem is the engine's results layer (home.py SimulationResults/SummaryStatistics, with flow.py). The engine partitions battery charge per timestep: flow.py computes pv_charge_stored_kwh and grid_charge_stored_kwh. SummaryStatistics keeps only one part (total_grid_charge_kwh, whose invariant is enforced in __post_init__) and the totals that include it. The web layer reconstructs the rest. Sankey: sankey_diagram computes `pv_to_battery = total_battery_charge_kwh - grid_charge`, `pv_to_demand = total_self_consumption_kwh - total_battery_discharge_kwh` and `grid_to_demand = total_grid_import_kwh - grid_charge`, which depends on the unstated fact that self-consumption includes battery discharge. Radar: comparison_radar computes 'Battery Utilization %' as `total_battery_charge_kwh / total_generation_kwh`, which does not subtract grid charge. The two charts therefore disagree on the same quantity (task 492; 628 'derived twice'), and fix(469) existed because Sankey previously missed the split. Tariff: `_unpriced_import_note` decides whether a run was priced from `results.tariff_rate.gt(0).any()` and `export_revenue.gt(0).any()`. financial_breakdown's own docstring admits 'SimulationResults records the import tariff's rate but no export rate, so the chart cannot tell [an SEG run that exported nothing] from a run with neither'. That is a chart compensating for a missing engine guarantee. It took three commits plus an amend (76e576d, fba34ca, 1de43b4) to settle. SOC limits: battery_soc_chart takes a BatteryConfig and instantiates a Battery just to read min_soc_kwh/max_soc_kwh. fix(645) found the previous hard-coded 10%/90%. The limits are a fact of the results, not of a config the route must re-supply (routes.py::home_results passes `config.battery_config` and re-guards `has_battery and config.battery_config is not None`).
findings.proposal: Move the facts into the results types where the invariant already lives. On SummaryStatistics add derived read-only properties next to __post_init__, e.g. `total_pv_charge_kwh`, `total_pv_to_demand_kwh`, `total_grid_to_demand_kwh` and `battery_pv_utilisation_ratio`, with their identities documented once. Consider carrying `total_pv_charge_kwh` itself from flow.py. sankey_diagram and comparison_radar both read these, which makes disagreement impossible. Add typed `tariff_configured: bool` and `seg_configured: bool` to SimulationResults (set where simulate_home already knows the tariff), so `_unpriced_import_note` becomes a lookup and the 'cannot tell' caveat disappears. Add `soc_limits_kwh: tuple[float, float] | None` to SimulationResults (or SummaryStatistics) so battery_soc_chart takes `results` only. Deletes: the subtraction arithmetic in sankey_diagram/comparison_radar, `_unpriced_import_note`'s inference and its long docstring, the BatteryConfig parameter and Battery import in charts.py, and the has_battery guard in routes.py. Prevents the 469/492/628/645/665 class. Note the frozen-API consumer: additions are additive properties/fields with defaults.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Read sankey_diagram: pv_to_battery = total_battery_charge_kwh - grid_charge, pv_to_demand = self_consumption - discharge; comparison_radar battery_util = charge/generation without grid charge; battery_soc_chart still instantiates Battery(battery_config); _unpriced_import_note still infers pricing from tariff_rate.gt(0).

findings.statement: history.compare_page builds `runs` from `RunRecord.decoded_summary()` (a JSON blob decoded to `Any`, `{}` on failure) and passes `[r.get('summary', {}) ...]` to comparison_bar_chart and comparison_radar, typed `list[dict[str, Any]]`. Typed loaders exist (storage.load_home_run returns SummaryStatistics; load_fleet_run returns FleetSummary), but the comparison path bypasses them. The charts read `summary.get('self_consumption_ratio', 0)`, `'grid_dependency_ratio'`, `'export_ratio'`, `'total_battery_charge_kwh'` and the five `total_*_kwh` keys. compare_page does not filter by run type (compare.html renders `run_type_badge(run.type)`, so mixed or fleet runs are expected). A fleet run's stored summary is asdict(FleetSummary), whose keys are `fleet_self_consumption_ratio`, `fleet_grid_dependency_ratio` and no `export_ratio` or battery fields. The radar therefore draws 0 for those axes with no error. The `.get(..., 0)` default turns a schema mismatch into a plausible wrong chart (heuristic 10: informative failure). The broad `except Exception: logger.warning(...)` around chart construction in compare_page turns real exceptions into a 'No chart data available.' page, and the same function-local import of charts appears in routes.py (`# noqa: PLC0415` x2), with no import cycle to justify it (charts.py imports only engine modules).
findings.proposal: Define the comparison input as a typed value: `ComparableRun(label: str, summary: SummaryStatistics | FleetSummary)`, built in storage (a `RunStorage.comparable_runs(ids)` that deserialises with the existing `_deserialize_dataclass`) and failing with a named ValueError on an unreadable summary. Give both summary types the shared fields the comparison needs via one small protocol/property set (`self_consumption_ratio`, `grid_dependency_ratio`, `export_ratio`) so the fleet variant maps `fleet_*` fields once, in the type that owns them. comparison_bar_chart/comparison_radar take that typed sequence. Either refuse mixed run types in compare_page with a flash message or chart them correctly. Delete: the `.get(key, 0)` defaults, the stringly `summary_keys` table in comparison_bar_chart, the blanket try/except in compare_page, and the lazy chart imports.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — comparison_radar/comparison_bar_chart still take list[dict[str, Any]] and summary.get(key, 0); history.py:90 passes r.get('summary', {}) from decoded_summary(); function-local charts import with broad except Exception (history.py:87-95); routes.py:122,192 noqa PLC0415.

findings.statement: chart-renderer.js is documented as the shared Plotly renderer: dark/light layout overrides, deferred drawing of charts in hidden tabs via ResizeObserver, a theme-changed redraw. compare.html does not load it. Its script block calls `Plotly.newPlot('chart-comparison-bar', ...)` and `Plotly.newPlot('chart-comparison-radar', ..., {responsive: true})` directly inside DOMContentLoaded with its own try/catch and console.error text. charts.py::_SHARED_LAYOUT sets transparent paper/plot backgrounds and no font colour, so in dark mode the comparison charts get Plotly's default dark text on the slate-800 card (the contrast fix lives only in _darkOverrides). The toggle's `theme-changed` event has no listener on this page. The radar chart sits in a tab with `x-show="activeTab === 'radar'"`, so it is drawn while display:none, the exact case chart-renderer.js's deferral exists for (AC3). The page's tab buttons also lack the role=tab/aria-selected the results pages have. This is the invariant 'every chart goes through renderChart' held nowhere, which is why the draw path drifted. Not observed in a browser: the dark-mode contrast and hidden-tab sizing are read from the code paths.
findings.proposal: Load chart-renderer.js on compare.html and replace both inline Plotly blocks with `renderChart(id, figure)`, ideally via the shared chart-panel partial proposed in the chart-description finding. Then add one test that asserts no template calls `Plotly.newPlot` outside chart-renderer.js. Deletes the inline Plotly try/catch blocks. Prevents the dark-mode and hidden-tab chart bugs of the 683/691 class on the one page that escaped the fix.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — compare.html:177,184 call Plotly.newPlot directly; no chart-renderer.js reference in the template.

findings.statement: macros.html defines `card`, `stat_card`, `chart_container` and the badge macros, but the dominant structures are not routed through them. `card` is invoked once (dashboard.html), while the same card class triple (`bg-white dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg shadow-sm`) is written about 50 times across templates. The tab-button class string `border-primary-500 text-primary-600 dark:text-primary-400 ... border-transparent text-slate-500 ...` is copied into 10 buttons (results/home.html x4, results/fleet.html x3, history/compare.html x2, simulate/home.html x1). The pages have drifted apart: the results pages' tabs carry role='tab' and :aria-selected, compare.html's do not, and their padding and gap differ. The accessibility history shows the cost: 188 (dispatch select), 213 (sweep form, seven controls), 275 (fieldset/legend), 385 (distribution card, section captions) and 418 (row controls) each labelled controls one template at a time, and fix(138) and fix(288) repaired one layout at a time. A rule such as 'a tab list has role=tab and aria-selected' or 'a control has a label' lives nowhere a change can reach, so the next page repeats the gap. The remedy for drift so far has been tests that parse the markup (tests/_css_classes.py, tests/_html_page.py).
findings.proposal: Make the macros the only way these structures are written. Add `tab_bar(tabs, model='activeTab')` (renders role=tablist/tab, aria-selected, the active/inactive class pair once), a `panel(title, body)` built on `card`, and a `labelled_control(id, label, ...)` or `field(...)` for form controls whose label association is required by signature (the macro raises at render if no label is given). Convert results/home.html, fleet.html, compare.html, simulate/home.html and dashboard.html to them. Deletes about 50 card class literals, 10 tab class literals and the per-page tab markup. A 'no raw card or tab class string in page templates' test can then replace several parser-based guards. Prevents the a11y-per-control and layout-per-page fix classes (188, 213, 275, 385, 418, 138, 288).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — grep: the exact card class triple appears 32 times across templates; card() macro invoked only via stat_card on dashboard.html.

findings.statement: tests/_css_classes.py (448 lines) is a CSS/Jinja/Alpine/inline-script reader: custom CSS block splitter (`_top_level_blocks`, `_lone_classes`, `_declarations`), CSS-escape handling, Alpine `:class` literal extraction, and Jinja AST walkers for `classes`/`_class` names. Its docstring lists two known unchecked gaps (classes returned from JS getters, and composed in other Jinja expressions). tests/_html_page.py (340 lines) reads page HTML plus regexes over inline script text for renderChart call sites (`render_chart_targets`, `_render_chart_call`, with a docstring about regular-expression literals). The theme and palette guards sit on top (test_web_theme_colours.py 316 lines, test_web_chart_colours.py 310, plus test_web_theme_palettes, test_web_compiled_css, test_web_hand_written_css, test_web_run_badges, test_web_inline_styles). The history shows this machinery being repeatedly repaired as a product: e828400 (blank CSS strings and url() tokens), e0b5b29 (declared_properties_by_class only inside @media/@supports/@layer), 467cee7 (case-insensitive property names), 2d9eb46, fd5dbd5/b0daf73 (function declaration read as a call), d41cef6 (class reader for {% set %}), a729e9a and d5aa3bb (guard premises). These are tests reaching into representation (heuristic 12 applied to tests, and the Tests stance): they pin how the source text is written rather than behaviour. A move of a role into a macro, or a restyle, requires editing allow-lists (_AMBER_ROLES lists template paths and class names). Most of this exists to compensate for the repeated-string design in the other findings.
findings.proposal: Treat the guards as a ratchet that should shrink as the structure improves. After the chart-description, palette and macro findings land, delete tests/unit/test_web_results_chart_targets.py, render_chart_targets/render_chart_figure, _AMBER_ROLES with its 4 tests, and the amber-copy premise check. Keep rendered-output tests (parse the response of the Flask test client with one real HTML parser, as server_drawn_badge already does) and the css-build lane. Do not add further regex/CSS parsers for new conventions. Encode each convention in a macro signature instead.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tests/_css_classes.py still 448 lines; test_web_theme_colours/test_web_chart_colours present in index.

findings.statement: static/dist/style.css is minified build output committed beside its sources, and Tailwind scans the raw text of templates and static/js, so any class-like token in a template, a JS string or a comment can change it. The invariant 'dist equals a fresh build of its sources' is enforced only by tests/css_build in the post-merge offline lane (needs npm and network). The per-task verify cannot run it. tests/unit/test_web_compiled_css.py covers only one direction (every applied class has some selector), so a removed class leaves a stale rule that nothing detects before merge (this is how 626 arose: task 363's server-rendered sidebar left two bare rules without a source). The result is a recurring file-and-fix cycle: 170, 222, 626, 634, 459 plus the licence-copy tasks 380/500/513, each a mechanical rebuild-and-commit. The agent that edits a template has no pre-merge signal that the artefact is stale.
findings.proposal: Make the check part of the task verify, offline: pre-seed an npm cache the way CLAUDE.md already does for uv, and run the same `npm ci --offline && npm run build:css` byte-for-byte comparison used by tests/css_build/test_dist_style_css.py as a non-slow test when node is available (skip with a loud message otherwise). Alternatively a pinned Tailwind standalone binary vendored in the repo. Deletes the post-merge fix-task round trip for CSS drift and the one-directional test_web_compiled_css guard. Reduces the number of tasks that touch dist/style.css after the fact.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — tests/css_build/test_dist_style_css.py remains the only fresh-build check (offline lane); per-task verify unchanged per CLAUDE.md.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10, clear invariants uniformly enforced. A shuffled_pool distribution must hold one value per home (ShuffledPoolDistribution's docstring, config.py:128, 'must sum to n_homes'; the editor's hint, distribution-editor.html:108, 'Counts should sum to the fleet size'), but no reader enforces it: ShuffledPoolDistribution.__post_init__ checks lengths, negatives and an all-zero total only; the fleet form's _pool_counts (fleet_config.py:526-545) caps the total at MAX_FLEET_HOMES only; and _DistributionSampler.sample indexes pool[idx] (config.py:1585). parse_fleet_form generates the homes (fleet_scenario.py:98), so a pool with fewer values than n_homes raises IndexError, which is outside FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS (ValueError, TypeError, ConfigurationError; fleet_scenario.py:47), the tuple documented as the exceptions this module's readers raise for a form they refuse. Measured on the pinned tree with the Flask test client: the fleet page's default PV pool (20+40+30+10 = 100 values, fleet-simulator.js:32-37) posted with n_homes 200 answers HTTP 500 Server Error from POST /api/simulate/fleet-from-distribution and from POST /api/fleet/export-yaml. The same IndexError reaches POST /api/fleet/import-yaml (fleet_form_from_scenario calls parse_fleet_form, fleet_scenario.py:217) and fleet_presets._yaml_loads, which catches only FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS, so such a file in scenarios/ would fail the fleet page's render (routes.py:166). The page's fleet-size slider runs 10-500 in steps of 10 from 100 (fleet.html:31), and both default pools hold 100 values, so every fleet above 100 homes fails with the default PV and battery distributions. Every fleet below 100 silently draws only part of its pool, so the exact-count distribution is not exact. builder_form._scenario_reader_errors (builder_form.py:170-181) already treats this IndexError as a refusal, so the rule is enforced for one form and not the other.
findings.proposal: Give the invariant one home and call it from every reader. Refuse, in config.py at FleetDistributionConfig construction, a shuffled pool whose counts do not total n_homes, with a ConfigurationError naming the block path, the total and n_homes. Then drop IndexError from builder_form's catch. This spans config.py and both web forms, and it changes what config accepts: a pool larger than n_homes, silently truncated today, would be refused, so check the CLI scenarios first. The web-only alternative is to refuse in form_to_fleet_distribution_config. It fixes the 500 but leaves the CLI and the builder on different rules.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed parse_fleet_form with the 100-value default PV pool and n_homes 200: raises IndexError 'list index out of range'; issubclass(IndexError, FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS) is False.

findings.statement: The results page's 'Cumulative Net Savings' line (charts.py:467-475, axis title :486) is cumulative export revenue minus import cost: cumulative_savings = (-(daily_cost - daily_revenue)).cumsum() (charts.py:441-444). That is the run's net energy position, not a saving against any baseline. For an ordinary home whose import cost exceeds its SEG revenue, the 'savings' line falls below zero all year. The package's finance layer defines savings as the difference against a no-solar baseline (finance.bill / householder_bill; BillBreakdown's saving vs baseline). Under the CBS model the export revenue the chart credits to the household belongs to the CBS (briefing finance key_scenarios). So the same word means two different quantities on either side of the web/finance boundary, and the chart's meaning is the one a householder would misread. [Also observed by web-forms:] Heuristic 1, informative names. The pricing is right: daily cost and revenue are aggregate_daily's import_cost_gbp and export_revenue_gbp, the engine-priced series, with no hardcoded rates. But the line labelled 'Cumulative Net Savings (GBP)' (charts.py:444, 469, 486; palette role net_savings) is the running sum of export revenue minus import cost, the negative of SummaryStatistics.net_cost_gbp. It is not a saving against anything. The finance layer defines saving as baseline_bill_gbp minus total_outlay_gbp (finance.py:209, saving_vs_baseline_gbp). For an ordinary tariffed home whose import cost exceeds its SEG revenue, the 'savings' line falls below zero all year, which reads as the system losing money. This is the chart the briefing names as a key scenario.
findings.proposal: Rename the trace and axis to what is plotted (e.g. 'Cumulative net energy cost' with the sign flipped). Alternatively, plot a true saving against a no-solar baseline priced from the run's tariff_rate series and demand. Renaming is mechanical; a baseline line is a design choice.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — charts.py:444 cumulative_savings = (-daily_net).cumsum(); trace and axis still titled 'Cumulative Net Savings'.

findings.statement: The parameter-sweep page never draws its results chart. parameter-sweep.js _renderChart (lines 206-225) draws with Chart.js (new Chart(ctx, ...)) after returning early when typeof Chart === 'undefined'. No template or vendored file loads Chart.js: static/vendor holds alpinejs and js-yaml only, and base.html and sweep.html load no other library. Its target #sweep-chart is an empty <div> (sweep.html:201), not a <canvas>, so getContext would throw even if Chart were defined. The chart card is shown once any point completes (sweep.html:199), so users see an empty panel. The guarded Chart.js path landed in d82d110 ('render results chart on completion') and has never rendered. Meanwhile charts.py's sweep_parameter_chart (charts.py:984), a Plotly builder for this chart, has no caller in src (grep across .py, .html and .js); only two test files reach it. Its 'Optimal' marker is the maximum metric value, which is the worst point for a lower-is-better metric such as grid import, one of the metrics the sweep reports.
findings.proposal: Keep one implementation. Either draw the sweep chart server-side with sweep_parameter_chart through the existing Plotly path (chart-renderer.js), taking the optimisation direction per metric, or delete sweep_parameter_chart and fix the client-side chart by vendoring a library or using Plotly. This spans charts.py, the sweep endpoint or page and parameter-sweep.js. No frozen-surface change.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — parameter-sweep.js:208 'typeof Chart === undefined' guard and :215 new Chart; grep across .py/.html/.js finds no src caller of sweep_parameter_chart; optimal still max().

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 (uniformly enforced) and heuristic 11 (SPOT). FleetComponent.fixed_range is the dashboard's bound on a fixed PV, battery or load value (admits_fixed_value, fleet_components.py:99), and the three forms enforce it three ways. builder_form._dashboard_limit_errors enforces all three through admits_fixed_value (builder_form.py:139-146). parse_home_config enforces load through FLEET_COMPONENTS['load'].fixed_range (simulation_params.py:369-371, added for load alone by task 613, be3ca77). It enforces PV through its own literal 0.5 <= pv_kw <= 20.0 (simulation_params.py:350), which is also hand-copied into home.html:74 and both assistant tool descriptions (assistant.py:430, 471). It does not enforce the battery bound at all. form_to_fleet_distribution_config enforces none; the fleet page bounds only its client-side inputs (distribution-editor.html:87). Measured with one body of 50 kW PV, 100,000 kWh load and a 500 kWh battery: the builder refuses all three values; the home reader refuses PV and load but accepts the battery; parse_fleet_form accepts all three and generates homes with them.
findings.proposal: Add one server-side check on FleetComponent that refuses a value outside fixed_range, naming the field, the range and the value. Call it from all three readers: the fleet form's fixed values, parse_home_config's pv_kw, battery_kwh and consumption_kwh, and the builder. Drop the 0.5-20 literal and render the assistant descriptions from fixed_range, as consumption's already is. The registry is now dashboard-wide, so consider renaming it. This spans fleet_components, simulation_params, fleet_config, builder_form and assistant. Behaviour change: API callers get newly refused values. Not frozen surface.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed: parse_home_config battery_kwh 500 accepted; parse_fleet_form pv 50 kW, battery 500 kWh, load 100000 kWh generates homes; simulation_params.py:350 literal 0.5-20 PV bound.

findings.statement: Heuristic 3, carefully factored dimensions of variability. The distribution type is one axis of variation. The dashboard spells it as a per-type if-chain in seven places, across two wire encodings of one editor state (EditorDistribution, fleet_components.py:20). Fleet page: fleet-simulator.js _buildDistPayload (156-173) posts a nested object {type, mean..., values:[{value,weight}], entries:[{value,count}]}; fleet_config._build_distribution_dict (426-446) reads it into config's grammar; distribution_form_spec (483-508, with its own _EDITOR_DISTRIBUTION_TYPES at 462) is the inverse, in Python. Builder: scenario-builder.js componentFormData (86-101) posts flat prefixed fields (pv_distribution_type, pv_wd_values, pv_sp_entries, pv_mean...); builder_form._distribution_spec (269-287, whose error text lists the types again) reads them; the inverse is client-side JS, componentDistribution (48-71). The seventh is fleet_config._draw_samples (153-188); config.py keeps the grammar's own table. The copies have diverged in policy. The fleet reader fills absent parameters with defaults (mean 0, std 1, min 0, max 1, value 0, weight 1, count 1; fleet_config.py:427-446, 537), so a posted {type: normal, mean: 3400} silently gets std 1 kWh, measured. The builder leaves them out and the loader refuses, measured: "normal distribution ... requires 'mean' and 'std'". The fleet inverse reads {type: fixed, value: 4} and refuses a normal without both clamps. The builder's JS inverse throws on 'fixed' and accepts missing clamps, so one scenario file loads on one page and is refused by the other. Adding or changing an editor distribution takes about seven coordinated edits in four files and two languages.
findings.proposal: Choose one wire encoding of the editor's distribution for both pages; the fleet page's nested object is the natural one. Behind it, keep one server-side pair of readers keyed by a per-type table (type to a form-to-grammar reader and a grammar-to-form reader), as config.py's _DISTRIBUTION_SPEC_TYPES does for the grammar. Move the builder's inverse server-side (as /api/fleet/import-yaml already is) or share it. Structural: it changes the builder form's POST contract and spans builder_form, fleet_config, two scripts and the editor template.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Per-type if-chains still in fleet_config._build_distribution_dict, distribution_form_spec (+_EDITOR_DISTRIBUTION_TYPES), _draw_samples, builder_form._distribution_spec, fleet-simulator.js _buildDistPayload (:156-173), scenario-builder.js componentDistribution.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT. Applying a scenario's fleet-wide tariff and SEG to every home is implemented four times, and the copies disagree. apply_fleet_overlay (fleet_config.py:60-102) gives the fleet form's homes its tariff, SEG and dispatch strategy via dataclasses.replace. config._FleetFileSettings.generate_homes (config.py:2339-2343) applies a fleet file's top-level tariff: only. cli/finance.py:162-170 and cli/optimize.py:225-232 each thread seg: onto the homes by hand. parse_fleet_form writes the form's SEG as the document's top-level seg: (fleet_scenario.py:113-114), and ParsedFleetForm.scenario's docstring (fleet_scenario.py:60-61) says load_fleet_config reads that document back as these homes. For SEG that is false (heuristic 1, a doc that lies), measured: a form with SEG 15 p/kWh runs homes with SEGTariff(15.0), but load_fleet_config of the exported YAML gives seg_tariff None and the homes compare unequal. So `solar-challenge fleet run` of a dashboard export values export at £0, and the builder writes the same top-level seg: (builder_form.py:98). tests/unit/web_api/test_fleet_yaml.py:60 and 73-74 work around it by re-threading. The loader half is tracked by task 185 (pending), which names neither the web export nor apply_fleet_overlay.
findings.proposal: Make config's fleet-file reader the one place that applies top-level tariff: and seg: (task 185, option a). Have parse_fleet_form build its homes by parsing its own scenario document through that reader, so the run and the export cannot diverge; dispatch stays a battery-block field. apply_fleet_overlay and the CLI re-threadings then go. Structural: spans config.py, cli and web, and changes load_fleet_config's result for every caller of a file with seg:. No signature change.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — apply_fleet_overlay unchanged; config._FleetFileSettings (config.py:2330-2343) holds location and tariff only, no SEG; cli/finance.py:162 still threads SEG by hand. Note: config gained parse_fleet_config/_read_fleet_distribution_file in b91894b (2026-10-06) and the web still does not call it.

findings.statement: The fleet page's distribution preview re-implements the engine's sampler and its validation instead of building the config.py distribution objects and sampling them. _draw_samples (web/fleet_config.py:143-186) has its own normal-with-clamps, uniform, weighted_discrete and shuffled_pool draws and its own std<0 / min>max / zero-weights checks, parallel to config._sample_from_distribution, _DistributionSampler and the Normal/Uniform/WeightedDiscrete/ShuffledPool __post_init__s (config.py:50-150, 1281-1311, 1533-1618). The two already disagree. Probe: a shuffled_pool of counts [1,1] for 5 homes previews [4.0, 3.0, 4.0, 3.0, 4.0] (the preview cycles the pool), while generate_homes_from_distribution raises IndexError for the same spec, so the preview shows a fleet the engine cannot build. Distribution type names ('normal', 'uniform', 'weighted_discrete', 'shuffled_pool', 'fixed') are string-routed again in _build_distribution_dict and distribution_form_spec (:405-500). [Also observed by web-forms:] Heuristic 11, SPOT. sample_distribution and _draw_samples (fleet_config.py:105-188) reimplement config.py's sampling (_sample_from_distribution, config.py:1281; _DistributionSampler, config.py:1533) for POST /api/fleet/preview-distribution. _draw_samples is the module's most complex function: cognitive 34 by complexipy, against a threshold of 15; cyclomatic 19 by radon. No page calls the endpoint: no template or script references it, and git log -S over templates and static finds none since it landed in bcdc278. Its only production reference is a function-local import inside that endpoint (api.py:373, noqa PLC0415). Tests keep it alive, and it has absorbed fix work (tasks 278 and 312). The copy disagrees with the engine it previews. A shuffled pool smaller than n_samples is cycled (counts 2+1 and 6 samples give [3,3,4,3,3,4], measured) where the engine raises IndexError. A negative weight previews silently (weights -1 and 2 give [4.0]*6, measured) where WeightedDiscreteDistribution refuses it. And it reads params through _build_distribution_dict's invented defaults.
findings.proposal: Build the preview from the engine: parse the form's spec with config's distribution parser (_parse_distribution_spec, which would need a public name), then draw n samples through the engine's sampler with the fixed preview seed. This deletes _draw_samples' duplicate validation and makes preview and run agree by construction. This spans web and config; it adds a public config helper but changes no frozen name.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed: shuffled_pool counts 2+1 for 6 samples -> [3,3,4,3,3,4] (cycles); grep: /api/fleet/preview-distribution referenced only by api.py:357, function-local import noqa PLC0415 at the endpoint.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10, uniformly enforced. parse_home_config refuses unrecognised top-level keys (simulation_params.py:287-294), and its tariff, seg and dispatch_strategy blocks go through config.py parsers that refuse unrecognised keys. Its heat_pump block reader (simulation_params.py:264-284) reads three keys with .get and ignores everything else. It also speaks a second grammar for the block (heuristic 11): it reads 'type' where config's heat_pump block reads 'heat_pump_type'. It defaults thermal_capacity_kw to 8.0, which config's grammar requires (config.py:991-994). And it restates HeatPumpConfig's annual_heat_demand default of 8000.0 (heat_pump.py:125). Measured: {'heat_pump': {'heat_pump_type': 'GSHP', 'thermal_capacity': 12}}, the config spelling plus a typo, runs an ASHP at 8 kW and 8000 kWh with no error. Reachable through POST /api/simulate/home, each home of POST /api/simulate/fleet, and the sweep's base_config. The home form itself sends 'type' (home.html:147-151).
findings.proposal: Refuse unrecognised heat_pump keys, naming heat_pump.<key>, as the top level does. Better: translate the form's 'type' to 'heat_pump_type' and parse the block with config's heat-pump parser, so the required fields and defaults live in one place. One function, though using config's parser changes which bodies are refused.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed: heat_pump {heat_pump_type: GSHP, thermal_capacity: 12} -> HeatPumpConfig(ASHP, 8.0, 8000.0) with no error.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11: the builder's preset has two shapes and two readers, and 'loads a preset' (a briefing key scenario) applies three fields. loadPreset (static/js/scenario-builder.js:259-278) copies only name, fleet_distribution.n_homes and the location's latitude and longitude. The coordinates use || 51.45 and || -2.58, so a 0 coordinate becomes Bristol's, and altitude is not set. It ignores the distributions, period, tariff and SEG, which the same file's upload path reads in full (scenarioFormFields, :15-44). A preset the builder saved does not load back either. Save stores the builder's flat form: doSave posts config: getFormData() (:200-205), api.py scenarios_save_scenario stores it as is, and tests/unit/test_web_scenarios.py:408-412 pins config == {'n_homes': 12}. loadPreset reads document-shaped keys (cfg.location, cfg.fleet_distribution), so reloading a saved scenario restores only its name. A built-in preset is the scenario document scenario_from_builder_form's output imitates; a saved one is that function's input.
findings.proposal: Store builder presets in one shape, the scenario document scenario_from_builder_form returns, and load every preset through scenarioFormFields, as uploads are. Spans api.py and the script. It changes the saved-preset format, so existing saved builder presets need converting on read.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — scenario-builder.js:259-278 loadPreset; :267 'cfg.location.latitude || 51.45' unchanged.

findings.statement: Heuristic 9: the module's interface carries a builder nothing uses. overlaid_power_flows (charts.py:626-674), documented 'for run comparison page', has no caller anywhere in src (grep across .py, .html and .js). The compare page draws only comparison_bar_chart and comparison_radar (history.py:88-93). It has had no production caller since it landed with the compare page in bcdc278. Four test files exercise it, and test_web_chart_colours.py requires a test case for every public charts function, which keeps an orphan looking used.
findings.proposal: Delete it and its test cases, or wire it into the compare page if the overlay is wanted (a product choice).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — grep across src .py/.html/.js: only the def at charts.py:626.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT. MAX_FLEET_HOMES = 10_000 (fleet_config.py:32) is the server's fleet-size bound for both fleet forms and the builder (builder_form.py:137-138), but the pages carry their own bounds. fleet.html:31 and 36 bound the input to 10-500. fleet-simulator.js:94 refuses more than 1000. builder.html:132 hard-codes max='10000'. The assistant clamps fleets to 100 ('(1-100)' in its tool description). One fleet page shows three different upper limits: 500, 1000 and 10,000. builder_form imports this dashboard-wide limit from the fleet page's helper module.
findings.proposal: Render the page bounds and the JS message from MAX_FLEET_HOMES, as the load range already is via tojson. Decide whether the slider's 500 is a UI convenience or the limit. Home the constant with the other dashboard limits (fleet_components).
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — MAX_FLEET_HOMES = 10_000 (fleet_config.py:32); fleet.html:36 max=500; fleet-simulator.js:94 1000; builder.html:132 max='10000'; builder_form.py:25 imports it from fleet_config.

findings.statement: Comments stance. fleet_config.py is 54% prose by docstring and comment lines (235 of 435 non-blank lines, AST count), against fleet_scenario.py at 44%, simulation_params.py at 39% and builder_form.py at 24%. Much of it is Raises sections that retrace the private call graph ('see :func:`_component_block`', 'see :func:`_refuse_battery_dispatch_strategy`', 'see :func:`_parse_component_distribution`'), and those drift whenever a helper changes. form_to_fleet_distribution_config has a 26-line docstring over about 13 lines of code, and _parse_component_distribution a 22-line docstring over about 12. simulation_params.py:331-334 is inline prose written to answer a reviewer: 'Range validation ... is delegated to PVConfig.__post_init__ ... PVConfig is the single source of truth for these bounds'.
findings.proposal: Keep each public reader's contract (what it refuses, and what the refusal names). Drop the call-graph tracing in private Raises sections, and move the inline defence to the commit history. Best done with the h3 and h6 rework.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Read in full: form_to_fleet_distribution_config docstring 26 lines over ~13 code lines; simulation_params.py:331-334 reviewer-answering inline prose still present.

findings.statement: Heuristic 6, one purpose per entity. fleet_config's module docstring states four purposes: sampling for previews, converting form to grammar, converting grammar back to form, and the fleet-wide overlay. The module also homes the dashboard-wide MAX_FLEET_HOMES and MAX_FLEET_SEED readers. Heuristic 13, files make internal sense in isolation. Its form conversion is half of 'the fleet page's form both ways', which fleet_scenario.py claims as its purpose (fleet_scenario.py:2). fleet_config's docstrings explain its rules by pointing up to its importer: battery.dispatch_strategy is refused because parse_fleet_form gives the root strategy to every battery (fleet_config.py:198-200, 263-266). So form_to_fleet_distribution_config cannot be understood from its own file. builder_form imports MAX_FLEET_HOMES from it (builder_form.py:25).
findings.proposal: Move the fleet form's distribution conversion (form_to_fleet_distribution_config, distribution_form_spec and their helpers) into fleet_scenario, or into a module only fleet_scenario imports. Move the size and seed limits to the dashboard-limits home. With sample_distribution deleted and the overlay settled (see apply_fleet_overlay), fleet_config dissolves. Structural: moves code between modules.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Module docstring still lists sampling, form->grammar, grammar->form and overlay; _refuse_battery_dispatch_strategy docstring still explains itself by parse_fleet_form in its importer.

findings.statement: Heuristic 1. The docstrings of fleet_form_from_scenario and _read_battery say 'A null battery capacity reads as 0 kWh: a home with no battery either way' (fleet_scenario.py:184-185, 427). But _null_capacity_as_zero (444-448) maps only nulls inside a distribution's values list. A scalar capacity_kwh: null and {type: fixed, value: null}, both of which the loaders accept, are refused. Measured: 'fleet_distribution.battery.capacity_kwh must be a fixed value or one of the fleet page's distributions ..., got None' and '... .value must be a finite number, got None'.
findings.proposal: Either map a scalar or fixed null capacity to 0 as documented, or narrow the docstrings to the values-list case.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed fleet_form_from_scenario with battery capacity_kwh: null -> ValueError '... must be a fixed value or one of the fleet page's distributions ..., got None'; _null_capacity_as_zero still maps only list values.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT. _HOME_CONFIG_DEFAULTS (simulation_params.py:56-75) restates engine defaults instead of leaving fields unset: azimuth 180 and tilt 35 (PVConfig, pv.py:70-71), system_age_years 0.0 and degradation_rate_per_year 0.005 (PVConfig's defaults), occupants 3 (LoadConfig, load.py:52), and pv_kw 4.0 (config._PV_CAPACITY_KW_WHEN_OMITTED). The battery settings in the same map follow the other policy: null means unset, which leaves BatteryConfig's default (simulation_params.py:242-261). The copies matter because the assistant's trigger tools send only pv, battery, consumption, occupants, location and window (assistant.py:425-450), so those runs take PV geometry and ageing from these literals, and a change to PVConfig's defaults would not reach them. stochastic is False here against LoadConfig's use_stochastic True, a policy difference stated nowhere.
findings.proposal: Use the battery's pattern for every engine field: an absent field is not passed, so the dataclass default applies. Keep in the map only web-specific defaults (location, stochastic), and say why stochastic differs.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _HOME_CONFIG_DEFAULTS (simulation_params.py:56-75) unchanged: azimuth 180, tilt 35, degradation 0.005, occupants 3, pv_kw 4.0, stochastic False.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10. parse_home_config coerces three fields instead of reading them. stochastic = bool(params['stochastic']) (:342) turns the string 'false' into True, measured. name passes any JSON value into HomeConfig.name, a str field, and into the run name; {'a': 1} measured. location is str() of any value before resolve_location. parse_fleet_form likewise takes name as Any (ParsedFleetForm.name: Any, fleet_scenario.py:64, 100) and keeps a present null as the name. fleet_scenario._read_name (:297-307) refuses a non-string name on import, so one field is read two ways across the module pair.
findings.proposal: Read stochastic as a JSON boolean and name as a string, with absent or null meaning the default. Refuse anything else, naming the field and the value, through number_fields-style readers. Type ParsedFleetForm.name as str.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Probed: stochastic 'false' -> use_stochastic True; str(params['location']) and ParsedFleetForm.name: Any unchanged; parse_fleet_form name [1] -> [1].

findings.statement: surface_form returns a string built from inspect.signature (or the Enum member list, or the constant's type name), and member_forms adds body names. Anything outside that lens is unpinned. I ran the helper on fixture classes (Python 3.14). A frozen dataclass and the same dataclass with frozen=False, order=True produce an identical surface_form ('(a: int, b: str = 'x') -> None') and an identical empty member_forms. This is live task 567; eq, unsafe_hash, slots and match_args are the same (task 668); the briefing's 'frozen but 9 are not' is task 669. A class with __slots__ gets a spurious member {'a': 'member_descriptor'}. A class constant is pinned only by type name ({'LIMIT': 'int', 'NAMES': 'tuple'}). A nested class is pinned as '()', with its own members unpinned. An Enum is pinned by iterating its members, so aliases are invisible (A=1, B=1 gives 'A=1, C=2'). Public module constants are pinned by type name alone in FROZEN_SURFACE: 'SEG_PRESETS': 'dict', 'OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS': 'dict', 'SEASONAL_FACTORS': 'dict', 'ELEXON_PROFILE_CLASS_1': 'list', 'DEFAULT_EVENT_WINDOWS': 'tuple'. Deleting a preset key a consumer indexes passes the lock. Each dimension added so far arrived as a separate patch: members (404), instance attributes (426), settable properties (540), member order (583), and now 567/668/669. There is no per-class contract record, so each new dimension means a new function, a new guard and a new table convention.
findings.proposal: Make the unit of lock a structured, frozen per-name record instead of one string from one lens. Add `tests/_surface_forms.py::NameContract` with fields: kind, bases (names), constructor (signature form), `dataclass_options` (a frozen record of `cls.__dataclass_params__` frozen/eq/order/unsafe_hash/slots/match_args/kw_only, plus `__match_args__`), `members` (existing member_forms), and `value_digest` for public constants (a repr or sorted keys of the dict/list/tuple, so removing a key shows). `surface_form` stays as its constructor rendering. FROZEN_SURFACE and FROZEN_MEMBERS entries then become renderings of one record per name, compared field by field. A new contract dimension becomes one more field with one drift line, not a new function plus guard. Enum aliases (`__members__`), nested classes and slots get a single rule each inside that record. Tasks 567, 668 and 669 collapse into 'add fields to NameContract'. The bespoke member-order and settable-property conventions fold into the member field.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — Read surface_form/member_forms in full: no frozen/eq/order dimension. Ran it at this tree: frozen vs mutable dataclass give equal forms and empty member_forms; surface_form({'x':1}) == 'dict'. FROZEN_SURFACE still pins SEG_PRESETS 'dict', OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS 'dict', ELEXON_PROFILE_CLASS_1 'list', DEFAULT_EVENT_WINDOWS 'tuple'.

findings.statement: The fail-closed contract of task 602 (a construct with no rule raises TypeError naming it) already makes the helper safe on any construct. Despite that, _parsed carries rules for InitVar, TypeVar/ParamSpec/TypeVarTuple (constraints, bound and default), NewType, Annotated, ParamSpec args/kwargs, the recursive-alias cut (_Evaluation, _Enclosing) and Callable parameter lists. I grepped src: the core modules contain no InitVar, NewType or Annotated (Annotated appears only in cli/), and TypeVars only privately (config._Built); the only alias is heart_pump HeatPumpType = Literal[...]. A line trace of the helper over the real surface (69 forms, 8 closure classes, all members of every pinned class) executed 157 of 211 statements. The unexecuted ones are the InitVar branch of _parsed, _parsed_type_variable, _parsed_new_type, _Declared, _Keyword, _ParameterTypes.text, the Annotated branch and the recursion cut in _Unevaluated.classes. The fix tasks 546, 551, 588 (InitVar), 608 (TypeVar/NewType), 617 (forward reference in its own evaluation), 630 and 631 all harden those paths. The 631 fix exists only because the helper reads TypeVar.__default__ and NewType.__qualname__, which typeshed does not declare on every minor, hence the `# type: ignore[union-attr]` and `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` and live task 644 (unused ignores). In test_surface_forms_helper.py, 21 of 94 tests (about 300 of 1,099 test lines) are about InitVar, NewType, TypeVar, ParamSpec, Unpack or self-referential declarations. This is the 12-of-18 'one construct per fix' pattern the mined themes read as 'each new annotation in src triggers a fix'. In fact no src annotation triggered any of them.
findings.proposal: Shrink _parsed to the vocabulary the library actually uses (classes, unions, generics/subscriptions, Literal, ClassVar, strings and forward references, None, bare typing aliases, special forms) and let everything else keep raising the existing TypeError from task 602. Delete `_parsed_type_variable`, `_parsed_new_type`, `_Declared`, `_Keyword`, the InitVar branch plus `_init_only_variables`, the `_Enclosing` TypeVar/NewType members, the typeshed-gap ignores (and so the 631/644 class), and the 21 matching tests. Keep one test pinning that an unmodelled construct raises. When src first uses a construct, the TypeError names it and a task adds one rule driven by a real signature. The `_Evaluation` cut stays only if a real self-referential alias appears. A removed rule can be re-added from git history when needed.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _parsed still carries the InitVar, _TypeVariable, NewType, Annotated, ParamSpecArgs/Kwargs and list rules. _parsed_type_variable keeps `# type: ignore[union-attr]` on __default__ and _parsed_new_type keeps `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` on __qualname__.

findings.statement: _Unevaluated.text() returns the annotation string as written, while _Unevaluated.classes() evaluates it. So one grammar produces two different readings of one annotation. The result is that form depends on a source-style switch, not on the type. I ran surface_form on two equivalent modules. With `from __future__ import annotations`, `def f(a: Optional[A], b: A | None, c: "Optional[A]")` is spelled '(a: Optional[A], b: A | None, c: 'Optional[A]')'. Without it, the same def is spelled '(a: A | None, b: A | None, c: Optional[A])'. FROZEN_SURFACE shows the effect directly: finance.py, community.py and optimize.py (future-annotations modules) appear as `Optional[BatteryConfig]` and `'FinanceConfig'` (quotes included), while pv.py and load.py appear as `dict[str, float] | None`. Adding or removing the future import, or re-quoting an annotation, changes the frozen text of every name in a module with no API change. That fails the lock and triggers the table-edit and release-note ceremony. Ruff selects only `F`, so no pyupgrade rewrite forces this today, but any sweep like task 493's can. The helper already evaluates every string on the real surface to find classes, so the canonical reading exists.
findings.proposal: Make `_Unevaluated.text()` spell the evaluated annotation (`_parsed(_evaluated(source, module), enclosing | {evaluation}).text()`), keeping the written source only for the recursion cut. Then Optional[X], X | None, 'X' and X all render alike on every minor, and `from __future__` and quoting stop mattering. `text()` and `classes()` come from one reading, and the `_Evaluation` cut becomes the only place a string is spelled as written. Regenerate FROZEN_SURFACE, FROZEN_CLOSURE and FROZEN_MEMBERS once, in one commit with a release note saying spelling only. The `Optional['GridServicesEventsConfig']` style entries go away.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _Unevaluated.text() returns self.source while classes() evaluates it. FROZEN_SURFACE still mixes quoted 'FinanceConfig', Optional[...] and pd.Series (finance/community) with unquoted `X | None` and Series (pv/load).

findings.statement: The briefing and _drift_message state that every edit to FROZEN_SURFACE, FROZEN_CLOSURE or FROZEN_MEMBERS needs an 'Unreleased on main' line in docs/domain-library-consumption.md in the same commit. I grepped tests/: the string appears in no test other than inside that message. tests/unit/test_consumption_doc.py contains one test that the doc exists. The workflow is: the failure prints the current form 'ready to paste', the agent pastes it, the test is green. The only gate that distinguishes an acknowledged break from a silent one is a reviewer noticing a missing doc line. The lock also does not classify drift. A removed or retyped parameter (breaking) and an appended defaulted parameter (additive) print the same way, though the forms are structured enough to tell them apart.
findings.proposal: Add an `UNRELEASED_SINCE_TAG: dict[str, int]` table in test_public_api_surface.py mapping each pinned path (name, class, or class.member) whose form differs from the 0.5.0 tag to its task id, and a test asserting each id appears in an 'Unreleased on main' line of docs/domain-library-consumption.md and each such line cites an id in the table. Have `_drift_message` also label a drifted entry as 'additive' or 'breaking' from the structured record in finding 1 (removed name or parameter, retyped parameter, new parameter without default). This turns the prose obligation into an executable one at the same single point where the tables are edited.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _drift_message still only prints the 'Unreleased on main' instruction; grep finds no test asserting the doc line, and drift is still unclassified (breaking vs additive).

findings.statement: _attributes_set_on_self walks the whole class source with ast.walk and matches `Attribute(value=Name(id='self'), ctx=Store())` and the literal `object.__setattr__(self, '<const>', ...)`. I ran it on a fixture. An attribute set by a nested helper class (`class _Helper: def __init__(self): self.leaked = 1`) is attributed to the outer class: undeclared_attributes reported {'leaked'} and also {'ok'} for the outer. A @staticmethod whose first parameter happens to be named self (`self.fromstatic = 1`) is counted. Setting through any other receiver name (`def configure(this, v): this.renamed = v`), `setattr(self, 'x', v)` or `self.__dict__['x'] = v` is missed silently. The home.py SimulationResults case (`object.__setattr__(self, name, series.rename(column))` in a loop) already shows non-constant names occur in pinned classes; there they are declared fields, so the guard passes by luck. The guard enforces the 'declare every attribute you set' invariant of task 426, so a miss lets an unpinned public attribute escape the member lock.
findings.proposal: Scan each function defined directly in the class body (not nested ClassDef) and take its receiver as the first parameter of any non-static method. Collect Store targets on that name, plus constant-name setattr/__setattr__ on it. Fail closed with a TypeError on a non-constant setattr or `__dict__` write on the receiver, naming the class, since the guard cannot tell what it sets. Add the three fixtures above to test_surface_forms_helper.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _attributes_set_on_self still ast.walks the whole class source, matching Name(id='self') stores and the constant object.__setattr__ form only.

findings.statement: _type_checking_imports is `functools.cache`d on the module name string, and _evaluated resolves that name through sys.modules and re-execs the imports on every evaluation. The cache outlives a module reload or a different module reusing the name, and the contract leaks into the tests. The docstring of the test helper `_imported` says 'Give each test's module a name no other test uses: the helper under test reads a module's `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports once per name'. Test authors must know an internal cache to write a correct fixture (the Tests stance: a seam leaking implementation). Separately, _holds_generated_init decides that an __init__ was generated by dataclasses via `init.__code__.co_qualname != init.__qualname__`, an artefact of how CPython's dataclasses compiles and renames the function. It works across the admitted minors today (the interpreter matrix is green) but rests on no documented behaviour. Task 620 and commits 8fe3d5b/65c0893 show it was already revised twice. A change in how dataclasses builds __init__ would silently make inherited fields evaluate in the wrong module, and the NameError would surface as an opaque lock failure.
findings.proposal: Key the TYPE_CHECKING-import cache on the module object (or the code object of its source) and return a fresh namespace per module. Alternatively drop the cache, since the real surface has few modules and parsing is cheap. Then delete the 'unique module name' obligation from `_imported`. Replace the co_qualname test with a positive check made at decoration time: compare `vars(cls)['__init__']` against `cls.__dataclass_params__.init` plus whether the class body's own AST defines `__init__` (the helper already parses class source in `_attributes_set_on_self`). The decision is then derived from source, not from a compiler artefact.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _type_checking_imports is still @functools.cache keyed on the module name; _holds_generated_init still compares init.__code__.co_qualname != init.__qualname__.

findings.statement: The invariant 'every release a declared floor admits works with this code' is checked nowhere, and the lock hides it. uv.lock pins every direct dependency far above its floor: pandas>=2.0.0 against 3.0.3, mypy>=1.0.0 against 2.1.0, pytest>=7.0.0 against 9.0.3, typer>=0.12.1 against 0.26.3, playwright>=1.51.0 against 1.61.0, scipy>=1.7.2 against 1.17.1. The lanes probe the locked set (verify, interpreter matrix) and the newest set (newest-releases), but never the oldest. A consumer that re-locks, or pip install '.[e2e]', can land on a floor release that nothing has run. Floors therefore get found when something breaks, and each find is encoded once as a RED test. test_e2e_extra and test_build_system hold a table of (distribution, first_capable_release, capability) whose 'capability' is a prose claim that the e2e tests or pyproject use some API. Nothing verifies that claim or that tests/e2e still calls the API, so the table can drift silently. The two test bodies are the same declared_floor assertion copied (live task 657), and the dev and runtime floors have no such test at all (live task 655, the mypy floor). Only the floors that have already bitten are guarded: setuptools 62.3 and 77, playwright 1.44 and 1.51, pytest-playwright 0.5 and 0.6.
findings.proposal: Add a lowest-direct lane job, 'oldest-releases'. It runs the same pattern as tests/newest_releases: copy_working_tree, then `uv lock --resolution lowest-direct` in a scratch copy, sync every extra, then run_verify_suite on the pin. A red there files a fix task naming the node-id and the floor to raise, exactly as the newest-releases job does for upstream moves. Give it a LANE_JOBS row with the shared LaneContract set. The floor then derives from an executed probe, which is the single point of truth, and test_e2e_extra's and test_build_system's capability tables become deletable. Keep only the generic invariant that a floor exists for every direct dependency, in one parametrised test that replaces the copied bodies (657). Fixing a failing oldest-release run raises the floor in pyproject.toml, and the same run would have surfaced 251, 258, 292, 589, 471 and 655 before a consumer did. Expect to raise several stale floors on the first run; that is the finding materialising, not a regression.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — test_e2e_extra and test_build_system still copy the same declared_floor assertion with prose capability claims. pyproject floors are unchanged (pandas>=2.0.0, mypy>=1.0.0, pytest>=7.0.0, typer>=0.12.1, scipy>=1.7.2) against uv.lock 3.0.3/2.1.0/9.0.3/0.26.3/1.17.1. No oldest-floor lane job exists.

findings.statement: The orchestrator runs a configured command by looking it up (a verify slot key or a lane job name), joining the job's cwd onto the worktree root, running it under sh -c in an environment with no caller virtualenv or uv lock mode, and optionally collect-only. The tests rebuild this composition at five sites. collect_lane_job composes sole_offline_lane_job, lane_job_directory and run_collect_only(env=). test_each_lane_job_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock repeats the same trio by hand. test_per_task_verify._collect_with_test_command pairs load_orchestrator_config()['test_command'] with run_collect_only. test_the_verify_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock indexes config[key] itself. run_verify_suite reads test_command and then uses a separate Popen runner. Every omission has been a bug. fix(273) found a probe that ignored the job's cwd. fix(344) found probes sharing the caller's .venv and lock mode. fix(309) found a plain `uv run` silently re-locking. Each was fixed at one site while the others kept their own composition. The two runners also differ: run_verify_suite runs in its own session and killpg's the group on timeout, but run_collect_only uses subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=300), which kills only the shell. The environment is a denylist of four names (VIRTUAL_ENV, UV_FROZEN, UV_LOCKED, UV_NO_SYNC), so any other ambient UV_* setting leaks into a probe that is supposed to model a clean lane.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen `OrchestratorCommand` in tests/_orchestrator_config.py, built by `verify_command(project_root, slot)` or `lane_command(project_root, name)`. It carries the command string and the cwd rule. A single `run(root, env, *, collect_only_args=(), timeout=..., new_session=...)` is the only place that applies cwd, the process-group discipline and the collect-only PYTEST_ADDOPTS. collect_lane_job, the two stale-lock tests, _collect_with_test_command and run_verify_suite all become one-line calls, and run_collect_only and run_verify_suite stop being separate runners. Make `isolated_uv_env` an allowlist or an explicit 'lane environment' constructor (PATH, HOME and the UV_ cache keys), so a new caller-side uv switch cannot leak in. A new lane job or slot then cannot be probed without its cwd and environment, which closes the 273, 344 and 309 class.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — test_stale_uv_lock.test_each_lane_job_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock still hand-composes sole_offline_lane_job + lane_job_directory + run_collect_only. test_per_task_verify._collect_with_test_command and test_the_verify_refuses_a_stale_lock index config directly. run_collect_only still uses subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=300) while run_verify_suite killpg's its session.

findings.statement: Three independent axes are carried by two marks. The axes are lane membership (what runs in the verify), network permission (what the guard exempts) and browser dependency. e2e means 'deselected from the verify' and also 'exempt from the offline guard'. slow means 'needs a live service' and also 'exempt'. The e2e lane runs `-m 'not slow'`, so its contract is that every unmarked test works without a live service. The guard cannot check that, because every e2e-marked test is exempt wholesale. The e2e row of LANE_JOBS lists only COLLECTS_ONLY_ITS_SUITE. The session's JobManager (_e2e_job_manager) is the real one with the real simulate_home. Non-slow tests such as test_home_simulation's form-submission tests POST to the live server and start real jobs that fetch PVGIS; only release_held_simulations, used by test_parameter_sweep, swaps in a stub. This is why task 366 (non-slow e2e fetches live PVGIS) and the e2e lane fix tasks 357 and 508 exist, and why the lane depends on PVGIS being up. The e2e mark is also hand-applied as a per-module `pytestmark` in 23 modules. No contract test asserts that a module under tests/e2e carries it, although the same conftest already iterates all items under its directory to add the flaky marker.
findings.proposal: Split the axes. Apply the e2e mark centrally, in tests/e2e/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems beside the flaky marker, and delete the 23 `pytestmark` lines. Drop 'e2e' from _MARKS_OF_TESTS_ALLOWED_ONLINE so only slow exempts. Give `_e2e_job_manager` a deterministic `simulate_home` stub by default, the constructor argument release_held_simulations already uses, so non-slow e2e tests keep the guard's in-process socket refusal (the live server runs in a thread of the pytest process, so the patch applies). Add `EVERY_TEST_OFFLINE_OR_SLOW` to LaneContract for the e2e row. The 'no live service without a slow mark' contract is then enforced for the one suite where it was only assumed, and 366, 387 and 624 stop being possible. Whether Chromium honours the proxy variables is a separate question, so the in-process refusal is the enforcement point.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — _MARKS_OF_TESTS_ALLOWED_ONLINE = ('slow', 'e2e') still exempts every e2e-marked test wholesale. All 23 tests/e2e/test_*.py modules carry a hand-written e2e pytestmark, and no contract test checks it.

findings.statement: Three lane suites (interpreter_matrix, css_build, newest_releases) are kept out of default collections by tests/conftest.py::collect_ignore, which an explicit path overrides. LaneContract.NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION checks it with addopts cleared. The fourth lane suite, tests/e2e, is kept out by three restatements: pyproject.toml's addopts `--ignore=tests/e2e`, test_command's `--ignore=tests/e2e`, and `-m 'not slow and not e2e'`. Its LANE_JOBS row does not list NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION. A default collection with addopts cleared, which dark-factory's serial and confirm reruns append (per the _lane_collection docstring), would reach tests/e2e and fail on `from playwright...` imports with no contract test noticing, the failure fix 3d7474f recorded when a bare pytest was interrupted across all 1084 tests. The redundancy is deliberate (heuristic 10 asks for redundant enforcement). The defect is that the definition of 'lane-only' has no single home, and one member has no checking test.
findings.proposal: Add 'e2e' to tests/conftest.py::collect_ignore (the tests/e2e conftest then never loads in default collections, and an explicit `pytest tests/e2e` still collects it, as for the other three suites). Add NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION to the e2e LANE_JOBS row. Then the addopts `--ignore` and test_command's `--ignore=tests/e2e` become redundant belt-and-braces that the contract test keeps honest, rather than the only line of defence. Derive the ignore list from LANE_JOBS (the `suite` field) if a table row can be read at conftest import time without a cycle.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — collect_ignore still lists 3 suites; tests/e2e is still kept out by pyproject addopts, test_command's --ignore and -m 'not e2e'. Its LANE_JOBS row still lists only COLLECTS_ONLY_ITS_SUITE. More restatements: interpreter_matrix/test_verify_suite._suite_env and newest_releases each set PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--ignore=<own suite>.

findings.statement: The upstream subsystem is the dark-factory orchestrator. Its pydantic LaneCommand model (cwd: str = '.', enabled: bool, command run via sh -c with DF_VERIFY_ROLE=offline) already validates this config on load. This repo cannot import that model, so it re-implements the rules by hand with asserts: lane_job_directory (cwd is a str that resolves to a directory) and lane_job_enabled (a YAML boolean), each citing dark-factory's config.py path in its docstring. It also pins defaults the orchestrator should not apply to a project at all. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml must set offline_lane_infra_enabled: false and offline_lane_legacy_numeric_enabled: false explicitly, because those default-on seams run scripts/run-offline-deep.sh and reify's tests/infra/run_all.sh, which this repo lacks, and `when unset it is on if dark-factory's default ever is` (fix 304 folding 305). The missing upstream guarantees are a project-config validation entry point and a seam default that does not presume the project has the seam script. Meanwhile run_collect_only models the lane env only by what it removes, and omits DF_VERIFY_ROLE=offline, so the model can diverge from the lane silently.
