findings.proposal: Upstream, in dark-factory: expose `orchestrator validate-config <path>` (or a documented schema) that loads the file through OrchestratorConfig and prints each job's resolved command, cwd, enabled flag and env keys, and make the legacy numeric and infra seams default off unless their script exists. Here, make tests/_orchestrator_config.py shell out to that resolver, or read its JSON, once per session. lane_job_directory and lane_job_enabled and their assertions become deletable, and the two explicit `: false` lines plus their pinning test stop being needed. Until the upstream entry point exists, keep the helpers but record the dependency in one place, as a docs/ pointer, instead of per-function docstrings.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — lane_job_directory and lane_job_enabled still re-implement LaneCommand.cwd/enabled with asserts citing dark-factory's config.py. The yaml still sets offline_lane_legacy_numeric_enabled/infra_enabled false explicitly. _uv_env still removes only 4 names and never sets DF_VERIFY_ROLE.

findings.statement: Comments stance. 85 of dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's 134 lines are comments, about 63% of the file. They carry measurements that go stale (the e2e timeout is '~8x the measured 214 s run', pvgis 'measures ~20 s', css-build '17-38 s by host load', newest-releases '17-19 min') and the lane-job intent that CLAUDE.md and each lane test module's docstring restate. The literal lane commands, with their `--extra` sets, appear in CLAUDE.md eleven times as well as in the YAML, with no test tying the two together. Timeouts are likewise spread across the YAML command prefixes (`timeout -k 60 1800`, `600`), _SUITE_TIMEOUT_SECS=7200 'about 15x the slowest measured run (491 s on 3.11)', _UV_TIMEOUT_SECS=900, _NPM_TIMEOUT_SECS=120 and run_collect_only's 300. The css_build comment asserts 'both npm steps' timeouts together fit inside the css-build job's timeout', and the unmarked jobs 'have no timeout: its suite timeout bounds a hang'. Those are relations between constants in different files that nothing checks. findings.statement: The lane contract tests need typed facts about a collection: node id, test file, marks and parametrisation id. They derive them by parsing pytest's text output. collected_node_ids keeps every stdout line containing '::', so any warning or uv line that contains '::' reads as a test. _lies_under partitions the id on '::'. _interpreters_named_by does `node_id.rpartition('[')[2].removesuffix(']')` to recover a parametrise id. The mode itself travels through PYTEST_ADDOPTS and depends on an undocumented ini -v cancelling -q (test_collect_only pins it). test_per_task_verify has already moved to a structured form, a JUnit XML report, for the skip question. So there are two ways of reading a collection, one structured and one parsed, and the hotspot's fix history is dominated by the lane harness diverging from the real lane.
findings.proposal: Write a small `-p tests._collection_report` plugin, placed on PYTHONPATH by run_collect_only, whose pytest_collection_finish hook dumps `[{nodeid, path, marks, callspec_id}]` as JSON to a file named by an environment variable. run_collect_only then returns a typed `Collection` (tuple of frozen `CollectedTest`). collected_node_ids, _lies_under, _interpreters_named_by (it reads callspec_id) and the '::' filter all die. suite_node_ids_matching becomes a filter on `marks` instead of re-running pytest with `-m`.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — collected_node_ids still keeps every stdout line containing '::'. _interpreters_named_by still rpartitions '['. test_marker_registration also regex-parses '<Class (\w+)>' from collect output.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT: `home run` reads a home file through a second reader, cli/utils.py::load_config_with_overrides (utils.py:144-203) plus `config_dict.get("home", {})` (home.py:50-52). The canonical home-file loader, config.load_home_config (config.py:2302-2325), is what `validate config` uses, and the two disagree. (1) Flat home files: config.load_home_config accepts a file whose top level is the home block. A flat file with pv 7 kW, battery 9 kWh and load 5000 kWh validates OK under `validate config`, but home_config_for_run returns the default home: 4.0 kW, no battery, annual_consumption_kwh None (TDCV 3200). (2) Typos: a file whose only key is `hom:` is refused by validate config ('Unrecognised keys in the top level: hom'), and home run silently simulates the default home. (3) Malformed blocks: `home:` with a null value, or `home: {pv: [1]}`, crash home run with an uncaught TypeError traceback because utils.py:173-178 walks the raw dict before any shape check. validate config reports them as clean errors ('home must be a mapping, got NoneType'). (4) The `period:` block is never read. scenarios/bristol-arbitrage.yaml sets a one-day 2024-01-15 period ('Short winter window for a fast demo'), and `home run` on it simulates all of 2024 (defaults at home.py:157/164). `config template home` and `config template scenario` emit `period:` and `output: {csv_path, include_summary}` blocks (cli/config.py:39-41, 66-68, 123-125, 138-140) that no CLI command reads. Commits cacebde, 4b687f4 and 3b5ded1 moved home run onto parse_home_block and parse_location_block, but left this dict-walking override layer in front of them. The layer is also why cli/utils.py hosts home-only config code (parse_location and load_config_with_overrides have no other caller; heuristic 6).
findings.proposal: Build home run's HomeConfig with config.load_home_config, plus the file's seg block, then apply the CLI overrides to the typed HomeConfig with dataclasses.replace instead of to the raw dict. Move the override code out of cli/utils.py into the home command. Decide whether home run honours the file's `period:` block (CLI flag > file > default, as optimize does) or refuses it, and make the templates emit only blocks some command reads. This chooses between designs and changes CLI behaviour, not the frozen library surface. A flat file's `seg:` key is refused by load_home_config today (_FLAT_HOME_FILE_KEYS), so the design must settle where SEG lives for flat files.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — cli/home.py:43 still calls load_config_with_overrides, and :51 still passes config_dict.get('home', {}) to parse_home_block.

findings.statement: Heuristic 1, informative names: the board-facing model document names a command that does not exist. docs/cost-recovery-finance-model.md:28 says a board member 'can reproduce a live `solar-challenge fleet run --cost-recovery` run by hand', and §9 (line 762) says 'Running `solar-challenge fleet run --cost-recovery` appends a ## Cost-Recovery Analysis block'. `fleet run` has no such option; the invocation exits 2 with 'No such option: --cost-recovery'. The flag belongs to `finance run` (cli/finance.py:98-108). §9 also cites its source as `render_cost_recovery_report()` in output.py (line 760), which does not exist; the block is rendered inside generate_finance_report (output.py:542, ## Cost-Recovery Analysis at :714). The doc has carried both names since 0fcd81f (2026-06-17). The briefing's doc-to-code verification convention requires a board member to be able to reproduce the run from this document.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT, and heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings. `finance run` and `optimize configs` each hand-build a ScenarioConfig from the raw YAML dict (cli/finance.py:226-244, cli/optimize.py:266-278) instead of using config._parse_scenario / load_scenarios (config.py:2022-2075, 2273), which already parse name, period, location, seg and finance. The two copies have drifted. (1) Period: probed with a stub CliFleetSimulator on a scenario whose `period:` is 2024-03-01..03-02, finance run simulated 2024-01-01..2024-12-31 and optimize configs simulated 2024-03-01..03-02. fleet run and home run also ignore `period:`, so optimize is the only scenario command that honours it. (2) optimize reads the block ad hoc (cli/optimize.py:237-239: `raw.get("period", {}) or {}`), skipping _parse_period's checks: both dates required, unknown keys refused. `period: "2024"` gives an uncaught AttributeError traceback ('str' object has no attribute 'get'), and finance silently ignores the same file's period. (3) finance parses a top-level `flex_band` key in the CLI (cli/finance.py:144-152) and silently drops a non-string value. config.py has no parser for this key. (4) The SEG-onto-homes loop is duplicated verbatim (cli/finance.py:162-170 and cli/optimize.py:224-232) and is redundant with finance._reconcile_seg_homes. (5) finance's conditional `seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh` threading (cli/finance.py:238-244) has no effect. Its comment says it avoids 'silently changing project_multi_year SEG revenue for existing --project callers'. But the homes already carry seg_tariff, finance.py reads the scenario rate only in _reconcile_seg_homes (a no-op for an equal rate, finance.py:1522/2281) and in calculate_summary's seg_revenue_gbp (finance.py:1570/2358), and no finance code reads that field. So `--project` output is the same with or without the branch, and the comment is false. These are the commands that render board-facing reports.
findings.proposal: Add one config.py entry that reads a fleet scenario file into a ScenarioConfig: period with the CLI-default fallback, scenario-level SEG, flex_band. Both commands call it and override only the CLI flags. Delete the two SEG loops, the ad-hoc period read and the inert CR5 branch with its comment. This spans config.py and two CLI modules. ScenarioConfig's signature is untouched, so no surface bump is needed.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — ScenarioConfig is still hand-built at cli/finance.py:228 and cli/optimize.py:267. optimize still reads raw.get('period', {}) at :237, and finance still parses raw.get('flex_band') at :144.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT: the board-facing sensitivity bands for the W3 ranking report are defined only in the CLI (cli/optimize.py:35-56). Its grid_services band (1.5, 12.0, 48.0) is a second copy of flex.FLEX_VALUE_BANDS' grid_services_per_kw_gbp values (flex.py:114-139, which carry provenance). docs/prds/discrete-install-config-sweep.capability-manifest.md:21 names the producer as `flex.resolve_grid_services_band`. That function exists (flex.py:163) but only tests call it, so a revised flex band would not reach the sensitivity panel. The other four bands (retained floor 15/27/40, battery 200/300/450 £/kWh, PV 800/1200/1800 £/kWp, inverter 100/200/350 £/kW) exist nowhere in the library. The downstream platform, which consumes optimize.sensitivity_panel through the library, cannot reproduce the CLI's panel without copying them. Under heuristic 6, the CLI module owns finance assumptions as well as argument parsing.

The CLI keeps only the alias-to-field mapping. Adding a public constant to optimize.py does not touch the frozen surface, because optimize is not in __all__.

findings.statement: Heuristic 3, carefully factored orthogonal dimensions of variability: one renderer serves two summary types, SummaryStatistics and FleetSummary. It takes `summary: Any` and picks rows by six `hasattr` probes on attribute-name strings (utils.py:233-261). FleetSummary names its fields fleet_self_consumption_ratio, fleet_grid_dependency_ratio, total_net_cost_gbp and total_seg_revenue_gbp, so the probes miss them. Rendering a real FleetSummary gave exactly: Total Generation, Total Demand, Self-Consumption, Grid Import, Grid Export, Number of Homes, Simulation Days, Grid Import Cost, Grid Export Revenue. So `fleet run` never shows the fleet self-consumption ratio, grid dependency, net cost or SEG revenue, yet it shows two of the four financial rows. The comment at utils.py:252 ('guarded so FleetSummary is unaffected') was written on 2026-05-31 (741520b). FleetSummary gained total_import_cost_gbp and total_export_revenue_gbp on 2026-06-16 (d803bae), which silently changed the fleet table. The unit test meant to cover the fleet case (tests/unit/test_cli.py:1056-1072) builds a SimpleNamespace 'FleetSummary-like' double with self_consumption_ratio, which the real class lacks, so it pins the probe's assumption rather than the real type.
findings.proposal: Give each summary type its own row builder: a function per type, or a rows() method in the CLI layer keyed by type. Rows then come from typed attribute access that mypy checks, and the test renders a real FleetSummary. Contained in cli/utils.py and cli/fleet.py, with no contract change.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — cli/utils.py:233-257 still selects rows by seven hasattr(summary, ...) probes.

findings.statement: The --battery-kwh override replaces the file's whole battery: block instead of overriding its capacity: `config['home']['battery'] = {'capacity_kwh': battery_kwh}` (cli/utils.py:184-188). So every other battery setting the file configures is dropped without a warning: grid_charging, dispatch_strategy, power limits, SOC limits, efficiencies and SOH. Probe via cli.home.home_config_for_run on scenarios/bristol-arbitrage.yaml: the file gives grid_charging GridChargeConfig(0.9), but with battery_kwh=10.0 grid_charging is None. So `solar-challenge home run scenarios/bristol-arbitrage.yaml --battery-kwh 10` silently runs without arbitrage. The sibling overrides patch one key (pv capacity_kw :181-182, consumption :190-191). The location override hand-writes the location block (:193-201) instead of using scenario_writer.location_block.
findings.proposal: Patch only capacity_kwh into the existing battery block (create it when absent; drop it only for a zero capacity, as has_battery decides), and write the location override with scenario_writer.location_block. Mechanical, one module.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — cli/utils.py:186 still replaces the whole block: config['home']['battery'] = {'capacity_kwh': battery_kwh}.

findings.statement: Tests stance: tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py::test_every_name_resolves_and_caches (:50-66) reads the package's private solar_challenge._SYMBOL_MODULE and _SOURCE_NAME (two `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`) to compute each name's expected origin. Its expected value is therefore the implementation's own map, so a wrong mapping passes. It also pins the caching detail (`name in vars(solar_challenge)`). The origin pinning it attempts is done through the public seam by test_public_api_surface.py's FROZEN_SURFACE/EXPECTED_KIND, and test_tariffperiod_collision_resolved checks the one alias by identity. Under heuristic 11, the same test file restates the surface count as a literal, `assert len(as_list) == 69` (:39), next to a comment saying T4 pins the names to 'avoid maintaining a second EXPECTED_ALL copy'. A version bump likewise edits pyproject.toml, __init__.__version__ and test_package.py::test_version_is_release_target, though test_pyproject_version_matches_dunder already ties the first two. The laziness itself and the import-time sync check are documented decisions and are not in question.
findings.proposal: Check resolution against public facts: each __all__ name's object is the one importable from its documented submodule, taken from FROZEN_SURFACE's grouping or the TYPE_CHECKING block that the sync test already parses. Drop the private-map read, the vars() caching assertion and the literal 69. Tests-only. The public surface is unchanged, so no version bump.

findings.statement: Heuristic 4, small function scopes, and heuristic 2, simple control flows: `finance run` is one 240-line command body (cli/finance.py:57-298) that does all of the following in sequence: loads and parses the finance block, resolves the flex band, threads SEG, parses dates, simulates, computes capacity-at-events grid services, builds one or two bill distributions, builds a ScenarioConfig, optionally projects economics, optionally solves cost recovery, and renders. complexipy measures cognitive complexity 26, over the Sonar threshold of 15; radon measures cyclomatic complexity 30 (D). The render step repeats generate_finance_report three times, with six identical keyword arguments, differing only in which distribution is first and whether bill_spreadsheet is passed (:262-296). Five `assert x is not None` lines (:249, :257, :263, :285, :286) restate the mode logic that set those values. optimize configs has the same shape: cognitive 29, CC 22 (D).
findings.proposal: After the scenario-reader consolidation, build the (primary, spreadsheet) distribution pair once and make one generate_finance_report call. Extract the economics and cost-recovery steps into a helper that returns both results. Local to cli/finance.py.
findings.verdict_notes: still_present — `run` still begins at cli/finance.py:59, and generate_finance_report is still called three times (:264, :275, :287).

findings.statement: Heuristic 13, files make internal sense in isolation: the CLI's function-local imports serve neither to break a cycle nor to save import cost, so the reader is left to guess why they are local. cli/fleet.py imports rich.table.Table inside _print_community_section (:61) and _print_sweep_summary (:491), although cli/utils.py, config.py and validate.py import Table at module level and rich is loaded before any command runs. fleet.py imports CommunityResults under TYPE_CHECKING (:11-12) while importing solar_challenge.community at runtime at :23. cli/finance.py imports gridservices inside run (:187-188) under the opaque aliases _GSAtEvents and _cgs (heuristic 1), although the module is already in sys.modules: measured, importing solar_challenge.cli.main loads solar_challenge.gridservices, via config.py. Under heuristic 5, _print_community_section takes a `fleet_results` parameter (:57) it never reads. By contrast, cli/web.py's local import of solar_challenge.web (:51-52) is a legitimate deferral of the optional web extra.
findings.proposal: Hoist the three imports to module level under their real names, drop the redundant TYPE_CHECKING guard and the unused parameter. Mechanical.

findings.statement: Heuristic 2, simple control flows: complexipy measures `fleet sweep` (cli/fleet.py:257-486) at cognitive complexity 20, over the threshold of 15. It inlines both sweep modes (CLI --param substitution, :386-405; YAML-defined, :407-420) in one body, and reuses `sweep_spec` across two types behind a `# type: ignore[assignment]` (:409). Under heuristic 3, the mode axis is decided twice: param_name is set from the mode at :384/:394, then the nested on_sweep_complete closure branches on `param is not None` again to name the output file (:446-449), producing the same name `f"{param_name}_..."` either way. Two nested closures, on_sweep_complete and progress_iter, capture mutable locals. cli/utils.py passes by measurement: create_summary_table and load_config_with_overrides are at cognitive 11 and 12, so no heuristic 2 finding there.

The comment '# Default to starting today' (home.py:242) sits above a hard-coded `pd.Timestamp("2024-06-01")` (:243), a comment that lies. findings.statement: Tests stance: TestHomeRunFullConfigParity (tests/unit/test_cli.py:1107-1244) captures the HomeConfig that `home run` simulates by monkeypatching the CLI module's own import binding. It imports solar_challenge.cli.home as _cli_home_module (:22) and calls monkeypatch.setattr(_cli_home_module, "simulate_home", spy_simulate_home) (:1161). The patch pins how cli/home.py imports simulate_home, not what the command does. The seam it reaches through is the defect: home run has no injectable simulator, while the fleet-finance commands have CliFleetSimulator. The test's question, which HomeConfig the file yields, is already answered by the public home_config_for_run (home.py:33), which test_cli_battery_capacity.py:90 calls directly. This is the only test that patches one of this seat's modules by attribute. No test imports a `_`-prefixed name from solar_challenge.cli.*. Every CLI command has a CliRunner test against the real implementation except `home quick`, whose only run test is a refusal path.
findings.proposal: Assert on home_config_for_run(path) for the parity cases, and keep one CliRunner run per case against a seeded weather_cache for the SEG-revenue output. Alternatively, give home commands a context-object simulator seam like CliFleetSimulator. Tests-only, or a CLI-internal seam change.

findings.statement: Comments stance: the cost rationale for the large-sweep warning (cli/optimize.py:252-256) says 'Each config may require up to 3 fleet simulations (age-0 baseline + two cost-recovery solves)'. optimize.run_sweep's own note (optimize.py:1051-1060) lists three calls per config, two of which are project_multi_year. Each project_multi_year simulates at least three seed ages ({0, L/2, L-1}, finance.py:1549) and then adaptive bisection nodes, so a config costs at least 8 fleet simulations, not 3. The rest of the CLI's inline prose is task history or reviewer-answering rather than rationale the next agent needs: 'task E / PRD §3.6 / §10-E' (optimize.py:3), 'δ surface' (finance.py:3), '(ε / task-76)' (finance.py:185), '(task ε / #34) Strictly additive ... byte-unchanged' (fleet.py:91-92, 242), the false 'pre-CR5' rationale (finance.py:239-241), and the eight-line defence of omitting a SEG row (home.py:165-172).
findings.proposal: Correct the simulation-count comment, or drop it and keep the threshold. Move the task-history and defence prose to commit messages and keep only pointers to docs. Mechanical, one pass over cli/.

findings.statement: Comments stance, and heuristic 1, informative names: cli/utils.py's module docstring (:15-17) states as a rule that 'A command that simulates a fleet reads its simulator from Click's context object, ctx.ensure_object(CliFleetSimulator).simulate'. Only `finance run` (cli/finance.py:182) and `optimize configs` (cli/optimize.py:285) do. `fleet run` and `fleet sweep` take no typer.Context and call fleet.simulate_fleet_iter and simulate_multi_sweep_iter directly (cli/fleet.py:194, :458). Under heuristic 3, simulator injection therefore has two mechanisms, the context seam and none. The fleet commands' tests reach the simulator only through a seeded weather cache, and home run's test patches a module binding (see the tests finding on cli/home.py::run).
findings.proposal: Either route fleet run and sweep through the CliFleetSimulator seam, by widening it to the iterator form they need, or narrow the docstring to the two commands that use it. The first changes the seam's shape inside the CLI only.
